right: Right to withdraw consent
description: Withdraw consent to processing at any time; withdrawal must be as easy as giving consent and does not affect prior lawful processing.
exercise: Any time, by means as easy as those used to give consent; data subject must be told of this right before consenting.
quote: The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time.
tl_reason: Withdrawal must be as easy as consent, so a click where consent was clicked; but a letter or email still withdraws validly. Conflict: mechanism vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right of the holder of parental responsibility to give or authorise a child's consent
rightholder: holder of parental responsibility over a child below 16 (or lower national age, min. 13)
description: For information society services offered directly to a child under the age threshold, processing based on consent is lawful only if a parent or guardian gives or authorises consent.
exercise: Controller must make reasonable efforts to verify parental consent (Art. 8(2)).
quote: such processing shall be lawful only if and to the extent that consent is given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility over the child
notes: Member-State option to lower age to not below 13.
tl_reason: Consent to a child's ISS processing, verified with available technology, often online; a signed parental declaration still works. Conflict: digital object vs plain act. Test: yes.

right: Right to exercise data subject rights by providing additional identifying information
description: Where the controller cannot identify the data subject, it must inform them if possible, and the data subject can still exercise Arts 15-20 by supplying information enabling identification.
exercise: Provide additional information to the controller; controller may not refuse to act unless it shows it cannot identify the data subject (Art. 12(2)).
quote: Articles 15 to 20 shall not apply except where the data subject, for the purpose of exercising his or her rights under those articles, provides additional information
tl_reason: Identifying info may be a technical identifier (cookie or device ID) for pseudonymous data, but plain details often suffice. Conflict: ability sometimes needed. Test: mostly yes.

right: Right to a response to a data subject request within one month
description: Receive information on action taken on requests under Arts 15-22 without undue delay and within one month (extendable by two months with reasons); free of charge as a rule.
exercise: Response within 1 month of receipt (+2 months for complex cases, notified within 1 month); electronic reply to electronic requests; free of charge unless manifestly unfounded/excessive (Art. 12(5)); oral information on request (Art. 12(1)).
quote: The controller shall provide information on action taken on a request under Articles 15 to 22 to the data subject without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request.
tl_reason: Electronic reply to electronic requests, but the reply is plain information; a letter request still works. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of reasons for not acting on a request and of remedies
description: If the controller does not act on a request, the data subject must be told why and informed of the possibility to complain to a supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy.
exercise: Without delay and at the latest within one month of receipt of the request.
quote: the controller shall inform the data subject without delay and at the latest within one month of receipt of the request of the reasons for not taking action
tl_reason: Plain-language reasons and remedies, delivered by any means including electronic. No mechanism needed. Test: yes.

right: Right to information where personal data are collected from the data subject
description: Receive, at the time of collection, the controller's identity, purposes, legal basis, recipients, transfers, retention period, existence of rights, automated decision-making logic, and information before any further processing for a new purpose.
exercise: At time of collection; before further processing for another purpose (Art. 13(3)); not required where data subject already has the information.
quote: the controller shall, at the time when personal data are obtained, provide the data subject with all of the following information
tl_reason: Privacy notice information, usually online but usable on paper in plain language. Test: yes.

right: Right to information where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject
description: Receive information about processing of data obtained from third parties, including categories of data and their source, plus the same core information as under Art. 13.
exercise: Within a reasonable period, at the latest one month after obtaining the data, or at first communication or first disclosure; exceptions in Art. 14(5).
quote: Where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject, the controller shall provide the data subject with the following information
tl_reason: Plain-language information on data sources and processing; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right of access
description: Obtain confirmation whether personal data are processed and access to the data plus information on purposes, categories, recipients, retention, rights, source and automated decision-making.
exercise: Request to the controller; free of charge; reply within 1 month (Art. 12).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning him or her are being processed
tl_reason: Object is the personal dataset, but a letter request works and access plus information can be given in plain form. Conflict: digital object vs plain result.

right: Right to be informed of safeguards for third-country transfers
description: Be informed of the appropriate safeguards (Art. 46) applied when personal data are transferred to a third country or international organisation.
exercise: Part of an access request to the controller.
quote: the data subject shall have the right to be informed of the appropriate safeguards pursuant to Article 46 relating to the transfer
tl_reason: Plain information on transfer safeguards, part of an access reply. No mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to obtain a copy of personal data
description: Obtain a copy of the personal data undergoing processing, in a commonly used electronic form where the request is made electronically.
exercise: First copy free; reasonable fee for further copies; must not adversely affect rights of others (Art. 15(4)).
quote: The controller shall provide a copy of the personal data undergoing processing.
tl_reason: Copy of processed data delivered in commonly used electronic form (data archive); holder must open and interpret files. Test: no.

right: Right to rectification
description: Obtain without undue delay the rectification of inaccurate personal data and completion of incomplete data, including by a supplementary statement.
exercise: Request to the controller; free of charge; reply within 1 month (Art. 12).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller without undue delay the rectification of inaccurate personal data concerning him or her.
tl_reason: Object is the stored dataset and correction is technical for the controller, but a letter request works; holder only checks the result. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
description: Obtain erasure of personal data without undue delay where e.g. data are no longer necessary, consent is withdrawn, an objection succeeds, processing is unlawful, or data were collected from a child for ISS.
exercise: Request to the controller; exceptions in Art. 17(3) (free expression, legal obligation, public health, archiving/research, legal claims).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data concerning him or her without undue delay
tl_reason: Erasure of a dataset is done technically by the controller, but a plain request works and the result needs only checking. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to have other controllers informed of an erasure request for published data
description: Where the controller made the data public and must erase them, it must take reasonable steps to inform other controllers processing the data that the data subject requests erasure of links, copies or replications.
exercise: Follows from a successful erasure request; reasonable steps taking account of technology and cost.
quote: shall take reasonable steps, including technical measures, to inform controllers which are processing the personal data that the data subject has requested the erasure
tl_reason: Object is published links, copies, replications; controller uses technical measures, but holder only makes a plain erasure request. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to restriction of processing
description: Obtain restriction of processing while accuracy is contested, where processing is unlawful but erasure is opposed, where data are needed for legal claims, or pending verification of an objection.
exercise: Request to the controller; restricted data may then only be stored or processed with consent or on limited grounds (Art. 18(2)).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller restriction of processing where one of the following applies
tl_reason: Restriction is marking data in the controller's systems; a plain request works and the holder only checks. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to be informed before a restriction is lifted
description: A data subject who obtained restriction must be informed by the controller before the restriction is lifted.
quote: A data subject who has obtained restriction of processing pursuant to paragraph 1 shall be informed by the controller before the restriction of processing is lifted.
tl_reason: Plain notice before a restriction is lifted; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to have recipients notified of rectification, erasure or restriction and to be told who they are
description: Controller must pass on rectifications, erasures and restrictions to each recipient, and on request tell the data subject who those recipients are.
exercise: On request of the data subject; notification to recipients unless impossible or disproportionate.
quote: The controller shall inform the data subject about those recipients if the data subject requests it.
tl_reason: Plain list of recipients on request; controller-to-recipient notification needs nothing from holder. Test: yes.

right: Right to data portability
description: Receive personal data provided to a controller in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and transmit them to another controller without hindrance.
exercise: Only for automated processing based on consent or contract; not for public-interest tasks (Art. 20(3)).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to receive the personal data concerning him or her, which he or she has provided to a controller, in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format
tl_reason: Data in structured machine-readable format to be taken to another controller; holder must handle and transfer files. Test: no.

right: Right to direct controller-to-controller transmission
description: Have personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another when exercising portability, where technically feasible.
exercise: Where technically feasible.
quote: the data subject shall have the right to have the personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another, where technically feasible
tl_reason: Direct technical transmission between controllers; holder operates across two services. Without the transfer mechanism the right cannot be used. Test: no.

right: Right to object to processing based on public interest or legitimate interests
description: Object at any time, on grounds relating to one's particular situation, to processing based on Art. 6(1)(e) or (f), including profiling; controller must stop unless it shows compelling legitimate grounds.
exercise: At any time; right must be explicitly brought to the data subject's attention at the latest at first communication (Art. 21(4)).
quote: The data subject shall have the right to object, on grounds relating to his or her particular situation, at any time to processing of personal data concerning him or her
tl_reason: Object is processing incl. profiling, but objection on personal grounds works by letter; nothing comes back. Conflict: digital object vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right to object to direct marketing
description: Object at any time to processing for direct marketing, including related profiling; data must then no longer be processed for that purpose (Art. 21(3)).
exercise: At any time; unconditional; must be presented clearly and separately (Art. 21(4)).
quote: the data subject shall have the right to object at any time to processing of personal data concerning him or her for such marketing
tl_reason: Opt-out of marketing processing and profiling is often a click, but no mechanism is required and a letter works. Conflict: digital object vs plain request.

right: Right to object by automated means
description: In the context of information society services, exercise the right to object through automated means using technical specifications (e.g. browser signals).
exercise: Via technical specifications in the context of information society services.
quote: the data subject may exercise his or her right to object by automated means using technical specifications
tl_reason: Objection expressed by automated means using technical specifications (e.g. browser signal); holder must find and configure software. Without it, no automated objection. Test: no.

right: Right to object to processing for research or statistical purposes
description: Object, on grounds relating to one's particular situation, to processing for scientific or historical research or statistics, unless necessary for a public-interest task.
quote: the data subject, on grounds relating to his or her particular situation, shall have the right to object to processing of personal data concerning him or her
tl_reason: Objection to research processing of data; plain reasoned request works, nothing returned. Conflict: digital object vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects
description: Not be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects.
exercise: Exceptions for contract necessity, authorisation by law, or explicit consent (Art. 22(2)).
quote: The data subject shall have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling
tl_reason: Object is software behaviour (solely automated decision), but it is a prohibition invoked by plain request; no mechanism to operate. Conflict: digital object vs no mechanism.

right: Right to human intervention, to express one's view and to contest an automated decision
description: Where automated decisions are allowed on contract or consent grounds, obtain human intervention by the controller, express one's point of view and contest the decision.
exercise: Applies in the cases of Art. 22(2)(a) and (c).
quote: at least the right to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller, to express his or her point of view and to contest the decision
tl_reason: Contesting an automated decision concerns software behaviour, but human review is requested and delivered in plain terms. Conflict: digital object vs plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed about a restriction of data subject rights
addressee: controller (per Union or Member State legislative measure)
description: Legislative measures restricting GDPR rights must, where relevant, provide for the data subject's right to be informed of the restriction unless prejudicial to its purpose.
exercise: Depends on the restricting Union or national law.
quote: the right of data subjects to be informed about the restriction, unless that may be prejudicial to the purpose of the restriction
notes: Must be provided for in the Union/Member State law that restricts rights.
tl_reason: Plain information about a legislative restriction of rights, per national law; no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to the essence of the joint controller arrangement
description: Have the essence of the arrangement between joint controllers (who handles which obligations and rights) made available.
quote: The essence of the arrangement shall be made available to the data subject.
tl_reason: Essence of joint-controller arrangement made available, typically in a privacy notice; plain text. Test: yes.

right: Right to exercise rights against each joint controller
description: Exercise GDPR rights in respect of and against any of the joint controllers, regardless of their internal arrangement.
exercise: Against any joint controller; arrangement may designate a contact point (Art. 26(1)).
quote: the data subject may exercise his or her rights under this Regulation in respect of and against each of the controllers
tl_reason: Choice of addressee among joint controllers; purely legal, no technical element.

right: Right to be notified of a personal data breach
description: Be informed without undue delay, in clear and plain language, of a personal data breach likely to result in a high risk, including likely consequences, measures taken and DPO contact.
exercise: Not required if data were encrypted, risk mitigated, or disproportionate effort (then public communication); supervisory authority may order notification (Art. 34(4)).
quote: the controller shall communicate the personal data breach to the data subject without undue delay
tl_reason: Breach notice in clear and plain language; any channel works. Test: yes.

right: Protection of the data protection officer against dismissal or penalty
description: The DPO may not be dismissed or penalised for performing their tasks and receives no instructions on how to exercise them.
quote: He or she shall not be dismissed or penalised by the controller or the processor for performing his tasks.
tl_reason: Employment-type protection of the DPO; no technical element.

right: Right to contact the data protection officer
description: Contact the controller's or processor's DPO about any issue related to the processing of one's data and the exercise of GDPR rights.
exercise: Where a DPO has been designated; contact details published (Art. 37(7)) and given in Arts 13/14.
quote: Data subjects may contact the data protection officer with regard to all issues related to processing of their personal data and to the exercise of their rights under this Regulation.
tl_reason: Contact with the DPO via published details, often email, but a letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to complain to a code of conduct monitoring body
description: Lodge a complaint about infringements of an approved code of conduct with the accredited monitoring body, whose complaint procedures must be transparent to data subjects.
exercise: Only where an approved code with an accredited monitoring body applies; not for public authorities (Art. 41(6)).
quote: established procedures and structures to handle complaints about infringements of the code or the manner in which the code has been, or is being, implemented by a controller or processor
tl_reason: Complaint to a code-of-conduct monitoring body by ordinary means; no mechanism.

right: Right to enforce binding corporate rules as a data subject
addressee: group of undertakings bound by BCRs
description: BCRs must confer enforceable rights on data subjects, including complaint, court action and redress and compensation for breaches of the BCRs.
exercise: Against the EU-established member accepting liability (Art. 47(2)(f)); complaint to SA or courts under Art. 79.
quote: the right to lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority and before the competent courts of the Member States in accordance with Article 79, and to obtain redress
tl_reason: Enforcing BCRs through complaint, courts and compensation; no technical element.

right: Right to be informed of a transfer based on compelling legitimate interests
description: Where a one-off transfer relies on the controller's compelling legitimate interests, the data subject must be informed of the transfer and of those interests.
exercise: In addition to Arts 13/14 information.
quote: inform the data subject of the transfer and on the compelling legitimate interests pursued
notes: Second subparagraph of Art. 49(1).
tl_reason: Plain information on a transfer and the interests pursued; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of risks before consenting to a third-country transfer
description: A transfer based on consent without adequacy or safeguards requires explicit consent after being informed of the possible risks.
exercise: Before consenting; not applicable to public authorities exercising public powers (Art. 49(3)).
quote: the data subject has explicitly consented to the proposed transfer, after having been informed of the possible risks of such transfers
tl_reason: Plain information on transfer risks before consenting; channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to information from the supervisory authority on exercising rights
description: Ask a supervisory authority for information about how to exercise data subject rights.
exercise: On request; free of charge (Art. 57(3)) unless manifestly unfounded or excessive (Art. 57(4)).
quote: upon request, provide information to any data subject concerning the exercise of their rights under this Regulation
tl_reason: Information from a supervisory authority on request by ordinary means; no technical element.

right: Right to due process and judicial remedy against supervisory authority measures
rightholder: controller, processor or other person subject to the supervisory authority's powers
description: The exercise of investigative and corrective powers, including fines (Art. 83(8)), is subject to safeguards including effective judicial remedy and due process.
exercise: Under Union and Member State procedural law.
quote: shall be subject to appropriate safeguards, including effective judicial remedy and due process, set out in Union and Member State law in accordance with the Charter
notes: See also Art. 83(8) for fines.
tl_reason: Due process and judicial remedy against authority measures; no technical element.

right: Right of a complainant to receive the decision on a dismissed or rejected complaint from the local authority
addressee: supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged
description: In cross-border cases, a complainant is informed of the decision by the authority where they complained, and a dismissal or rejection is adopted and notified to them by that authority (enabling a local challenge).
exercise: Notification by the local supervisory authority; partial dismissals handled under Art. 60(9).
quote: the supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged shall adopt the decision and notify it to the complainant
tl_reason: Procedural notification of a complaint decision by the authority; no technical element.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority
description: Lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority, in particular in the Member State of habitual residence, workplace or alleged infringement, if processing infringes the GDPR.
exercise: Free of charge (Art. 57(3)); authority must facilitate e.g. with an electronic complaint form (Art. 57(2)).
quote: every data subject shall have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority
tl_reason: Authority must offer a complaint form that can also be completed electronically, without excluding other means. Letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of the progress and outcome of a complaint
description: Be informed by the supervisory authority of the progress and outcome of the complaint, including the possibility of a judicial remedy.
quote: The supervisory authority with which the complaint has been lodged shall inform the complainant on the progress and the outcome of the complaint
tl_reason: Procedural information on complaint progress from the authority; no technical element.

right: Right to an effective judicial remedy against a binding decision of a supervisory authority
rightholder: any natural or legal person concerned
addressee: courts of the Member State of the supervisory authority
description: Challenge in court a legally binding decision of a supervisory authority that concerns the person.
exercise: Before the courts of the Member State where the authority is established (Art. 78(3)).
quote: each natural or legal person shall have the right to an effective judicial remedy against a legally binding decision of a supervisory authority concerning them
tl_reason: Judicial remedy before courts; no technical element.

right: Right to a judicial remedy against supervisory authority inaction
addressee: courts of the Member State of the supervisory authority
description: Go to court where the competent supervisory authority does not handle a complaint or does not inform the data subject within three months of progress or outcome.
exercise: After three months without handling/information.
quote: where the supervisory authority which is competent pursuant to Articles 55 and 56 does not handle a complaint or does not inform the data subject within three months
tl_reason: Judicial remedy against authority inaction; no technical element.

right: Right to an effective judicial remedy against a controller or processor
description: Bring court proceedings against a controller or processor where rights under the GDPR have been infringed by non-compliant processing.
exercise: Courts where the controller/processor has an establishment, or where the data subject habitually resides (Art. 79(2)), unless the defendant is a public authority exercising public powers.
quote: each data subject shall have the right to an effective judicial remedy where he or she considers that his or her rights under this Regulation have been infringed
tl_reason: Court action against controller or processor; no technical element.

right: Right to mandate a not-for-profit body to act on one's behalf
description: Mandate a qualifying not-for-profit body to lodge complaints, bring judicial remedies and (where national law allows) claim compensation on one's behalf.
exercise: Body must be properly constituted, have public-interest objectives and be active in data protection.
quote: The data subject shall have the right to mandate a not-for-profit body, organisation or association
tl_reason: Mandate covers only complaints, court actions and compensation; signed by ordinary means, no mechanism. Test: yes. Differs from Table A DELEGATE.

right: Right of qualified bodies to complain and sue without a mandate
description: Where a Member State so provides, a qualified body may lodge complaints and seek judicial remedies independently of any data subject's mandate.
exercise: Only in Member States that opt in.
quote: has the right to lodge, in that Member State, a complaint with the supervisory authority which is competent pursuant to Article 77
notes: Member-State option.
tl_reason: Standing of qualified bodies to complain and sue; no technical element.

right: Right to compensation
rightholder: any person who has suffered damage
description: Receive compensation for material or non-material damage resulting from an infringement of the GDPR; joint controllers/processors are each liable for the entire damage (Art. 82(4)).
exercise: Court proceedings in courts competent under Art. 79(2) (Art. 82(6)); exemption only if not in any way responsible (Art. 82(3)).
quote: Any person who has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of an infringement of this Regulation shall have the right to receive compensation from the controller or processor
tl_reason: Compensation claim; no technical element.

right: Right of recourse between controllers and processors
rightholder: controller or processor that paid full compensation
addressee: other controllers or processors involved in the same processing
description: A controller or processor that paid full compensation may claim back from co-responsible controllers or processors their share of the compensation.
exercise: In proportion to responsibility under the conditions of Art. 82(2).
quote: that controller or processor shall be entitled to claim back from the other controllers or processors involved in the same processing
tl_reason: Recourse between liable controllers and processors; contractual-type claim, no technical element.

right: Right to use self-chosen pseudonyms in electronic transactions
description: Use of pseudonyms chosen by the user in electronic transactions may not be prohibited.
exercise: Subject to Union or national rules requiring identification.
quote: the use of pseudonyms that are chosen by the user shall not be prohibited
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Covers electronic transactions only, but no mechanism is required; choosing a pseudonym is just entering a name. Mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to obtain a European Digital Identity Wallet
rightholder: natural and legal persons in the Union
description: Every Member State must provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet so that natural and legal persons can access public and private services cross-border while keeping control over their data.
exercise: Wallet provided by, under mandate of, or recognised by the Member State (Art. 5a(2)); due within 24 months of the implementing acts.
quote: each Member State shall provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet within 24 months of the date of entry into force of the implementing acts
notes: Inserted by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183; deadline tied to implementing acts (no fixed date in text).
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object is a software wallet the State must provide; without it the right does not exist. Test: no.

right: Right to control and selectively disclose identity data through the wallet
description: Users can request, obtain, select, combine, store, delete, share and present person identification data and attestations under their sole control, with selective disclosure, to authenticate online and offline.
exercise: Through the wallet functionalities; user-friendly, transparent and traceable by the user.
quote: securely request, obtain, select, combine, store, delete, share and present, under the sole control of the user, person identification data
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Selective disclosure and presentation run only through wallet functions across relying parties. Test: no.

right: Right to generate and use pseudonyms within the wallet
description: The wallet must let users generate pseudonyms and store them encrypted and locally.
quote: generate pseudonyms and store them encrypted and locally within the European Digital Identity Wallet
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Pseudonyms are generated and stored encrypted in the wallet software and presented to relying parties. Test: no.

right: Right to exchange identity data and attestations wallet-to-wallet
description: Users can authenticate another person's wallet and securely receive and share identification data and attestations between two wallets.
quote: securely authenticate another person’s European Digital Identity Wallet, and receive and share person identification data
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Wallet-to-wallet authentication and exchange is a software function across devices. Test: no.

right: Right to a transaction log and dashboard of relying parties and data exchanged
description: Users can access a log of all wallet transactions via a common dashboard, including an up-to-date list of relying parties connected to and the data exchanged.
exercise: Via the wallet's common dashboard.
quote: access a log of all transactions carried out through the European Digital Identity Wallet via a common dashboard
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Transaction log via the wallet dashboard; holder must interpret logged data exchanges. Test: no.

right: Right to request erasure by a relying party directly from the wallet
description: Users can easily request, from the wallet dashboard, that a relying party erase their personal data under GDPR Art. 17.
exercise: Dashboard function; common protocol required by Art. 5a(5)(a)(ix).
quote: easily request the erasure by a relying party of personal data pursuant to Article 17 of the Regulation (EU) 2016/679
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Mandated dashboard function with common protocol to request erasure of digitally held data. Test: no for this channel.

right: Right to report a relying party to the data protection authority from the wallet
description: Users can easily report a relying party to the competent data protection authority when they receive an allegedly unlawful or suspicious data request.
exercise: Dashboard function; common protocol required by Art. 5a(5)(a)(x).
quote: easily report a relying party to the competent national data protection authority, where an allegedly unlawful or suspicious request for data is received
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Mandated dashboard reporting function, but a complaint to the DPA by letter still works and the outcome is plain. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to sign or seal with qualified electronic signatures/seals through the wallet
description: The wallet must enable users to sign with qualified electronic signatures or seal with qualified electronic seals.
quote: sign by means of qualified electronic signatures or seal by means of qualified electronic seals
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Qualified electronic signing is purely a technical function whose output is used elsewhere. Test: no.

right: Right to download one's wallet data, attestations and configurations
description: Users can download, as far as technically feasible, their data, electronic attestations of attributes and configurations.
quote: download, to the extent technically feasible, the user’s data, electronic attestation of attributes and configurations
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Download of wallet data, attestations and configurations; digital output to handle. Test: no.

right: Right to exercise data portability through the wallet
description: The wallet must enable users to exercise their data portability rights.
quote: exercise the user’s rights to data portability
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Wallet must enable portability; data must be moved to another service. Test: no.

right: Right to be informed whether a relying party is permitted to access an attestation
description: For attestations with embedded disclosure policies, the wallet must inform the user whether the requesting relying party or wallet user has permission to access the attestation.
quote: inform the user that the relying party or the user of the European Digital Identity Wallet requesting that electronic attestation of attributes has the permission to access such attestation
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Wallet evaluates embedded disclosure policy (software behaviour), but the result is a plain yes/no permission notice. Ability criterion weak.

right: Right to sign with qualified electronic signatures free of charge
description: All natural persons can sign with qualified electronic signatures by default and free of charge through the wallet.
exercise: Member States may limit free use to non-professional purposes.
quote: offer all natural persons the ability to sign by means of qualified electronic signatures by default and free of charge
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Default, free qualified e-signature through the wallet; signing is a technical function. Test: no.

right: Right to be informed of wallet security breaches
description: Users must be informed without delay of any security breach that may have compromised their wallet or its contents, in particular suspension or revocation.
exercise: Without delay.
quote: Member State shall inform users, without delay, of any security breach that could have entirely or partially compromised their European Digital Identity Wallet or its contents
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Breach notification is plain information; a letter would do and nothing technical is asked. Test: yes.

right: Right to verify relying parties' identity free of charge
description: Member States must provide free validation mechanisms allowing users to verify the authenticity and validity of the identity of registered relying parties.
exercise: Free of charge.
quote: allow users to verify the authenticity and validity of the identity of relying parties registered in accordance with Article 5b
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Free validation mechanism to check relying-party identity; holder checks a technical result. Test: no.

right: Right to have one's wallet revoked on request
description: The validity of a wallet can be revoked upon the explicit request of the user.
exercise: Explicit request of the user; revocation free of charge for natural persons (Art. 5a(13)).
quote: upon the explicit request of the user
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object (wallet validity) is digital, but revocation follows a plain explicit request and nothing technical returns. Mechanism vs test conflict.

right: Right to request technical support and report problems
description: Wallet providers must let users easily request technical support and report technical problems or other incidents affecting wallet use.
quote: Providers of European Digital Identity Wallets shall ensure that users can easily request technical support and report technical problems
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Support requests and problem reports work by any channel; reply is plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to free issuance, use and revocation of the wallet
description: Issuance, use and revocation of the wallet are free of charge for all natural persons.
quote: The issuance, use and revocation of the European Digital Identity Wallets shall be free of charge to all natural persons.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object is a software wallet, but the entitlement itself is a pricing rule needing nothing technical. Criteria conflict.

right: Right to full control over wallet use and data (no profiling or data combination without request)
description: Users have full control over their wallet and its data; the provider may not collect non-necessary usage data or combine wallet data with data from other services unless the user expressly requests it.
exercise: Combination only on the user's express request; logical separation of data.
quote: Users shall have full control of the use of and of the data in their European Digital Identity Wallet.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: User controls wallet data through its functions; combination only on express in-wallet request. Test: no.

right: Right to voluntary use and non-discrimination of non-users
addressee: public and private service providers; employers; Member States
description: Using the wallet is voluntary; persons who do not use it may not be restricted or disadvantaged in accessing services, the labour market or business, and other identification means must remain available.
quote: The use of European Digital Identity Wallets shall be voluntary. Access to public and private services, access to the labour market and freedom to conduct business shall not in any way be restricted
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Right not to use the wallet and keep other identification means; nothing technical required.

right: Right not to be tracked or profiled through wallet attestations
description: The wallet framework must prevent attestation issuers or others from obtaining data that allows tracking, linking or correlating user behaviour, unless the user explicitly authorises it; unlinkability must be enabled where identification is not needed.
exercise: Only with the user's explicit authorisation.
quote: to obtain data that allows transactions or user behaviour to be tracked, linked or correlated
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Unlinkability is software behaviour, but holder need do nothing except optionally authorise tracking. Ability criterion conflicts.

right: Right to compensation for damage related to European Digital Identity Wallets
addressee: Member State / wallet provider / party operating authentication
description: The eID liability regime of Art. 11 applies mutatis mutandis to wallets, so persons harmed by failures can claim damages.
exercise: In accordance with national liability rules (Art. 11(4)).
quote: Article 11 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the European Digital Identity Wallet.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Damages claim under national liability rules; no technical element.

right: Right of persons with disabilities to accessible wallets
description: Wallets must be accessible to persons with disabilities on an equal basis with other users, per the European Accessibility Act.
quote: European Digital Identity Wallets shall be made accessible for use, by persons with disabilities, on an equal basis with other users
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object is the wallet interface's accessibility; usable only by operating the wallet. Test: no.

right: Right not to be asked for data beyond the relying party's registered use
description: Relying parties may not request from users any data other than that indicated in their registration.
exercise: Users can report breaches via Art. 5a(4)(d)(iii).
quote: Relying parties shall not request users to provide any data other than that indicated pursuant to paragraph 2, point (c).
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Concerns wallet data requests, but the duty is a prohibition on relying parties; holder need only notice over-requests. Ability conflicts.

right: Right to know the identity of the relying party
description: Relying parties that intend to rely on wallets must identify themselves to the user.
quote: Where relying parties intend to rely upon European Digital Identity Wallets, they shall identify themselves to the user.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Identification occurs within the wallet protocol, but the result is a plain identity usable without technical means. Test partly yes.

right: Right to use pseudonyms with relying parties
description: Relying parties may not refuse pseudonyms where identification of the user is not legally required.
quote: Relying parties shall not refuse the use of pseudonyms, where the identification of the user is not required by Union or national law.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Relying parties must accept wallet-generated pseudonyms in authentication flows. Test: no.

right: Right to be informed of wallet suspension, withdrawal or re-establishment
description: Affected users must be informed when wallets are suspended or withdrawn after a security breach, and when provision is re-established (Art. 5e(2)-(3)).
exercise: Without undue delay.
quote: The Member State shall inform the users affected, the single points of contact designated pursuant to Article 46c(1), the relying parties and the Commission accordingly.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Notice of suspension or re-establishment is plain information; letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to use the wallet to access online public services
description: Where electronic identification is required for an online public service, Member States must also accept the European Digital Identity Wallet.
quote: Where Member States require electronic identification and authentication to access an online service provided by a public sector body, they shall also accept European Digital Identity Wallets
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Wallet authentication to online public services; operated across services. Test: no.

right: Right to use the wallet with private services requiring strong authentication
addressee: private relying parties (except micro and small enterprises)
description: Private relying parties legally or contractually required to use strong user authentication (transport, energy, banking, health, telecoms etc.) must accept the wallet at the user's voluntary request.
exercise: Upon the voluntary request of the user; within 36 months of the implementing acts.
quote: only upon the voluntary request of the user, also accept European Digital Identity Wallets that are provided in accordance with this Regulation
notes: Micro and small enterprises excluded.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Wallet authentication with private relying parties; operated across services. Test: no.

right: Right to use the wallet to log in to very large online platforms
addressee: providers of very large online platforms (DSA Art. 33)
description: VLOPs requiring user authentication must accept and facilitate wallet-based authentication at the user's request, limited to the minimum data necessary.
exercise: Upon the voluntary request of the user; minimum data necessary.
quote: accept and facilitate the use of European Digital Identity Wallets that are provided in accordance with this Regulation for user authentication only upon the voluntary request of the user
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Wallet-based login to very large online platforms; operated across services. Test: no.

right: Right to use notified eID means from another Member State for online public services
rightholder: holder of a notified electronic identification means
description: Notified eID means issued in one Member State must be recognised in another Member State to access online public services requiring substantial or high assurance.
exercise: Scheme must be on the Commission list and meet the required assurance level.
quote: the electronic identification means issued in another Member State shall be recognised in the first Member State for the purposes of cross-border authentication for that service online
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Cross-border use of notified eID means for online services; purely technical authentication. Test: no.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by failures of notified eID schemes
addressee: notifying Member State; party issuing the eID means; party operating the authentication procedure
description: Persons suffering damage in a cross-border transaction caused intentionally or negligently by failures of the notifying State, issuer or authentication operator can claim damages.
exercise: Applied in accordance with national liability rules (Art. 11(4)).
quote: The notifying Member State shall be liable for damage caused intentionally or negligently to any natural or legal person due to a failure to comply with its obligations
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Damages claim under national liability rules; no technical element.

right: Right of wallet providers and eID issuers to interoperability with gatekeeper features
rightholder: providers of European Digital Identity Wallets and issuers of notified eID means (as DMA business users)
description: Gatekeepers must give wallet providers and eID issuers free and effective interoperability with, and access to, the same operating system, hardware and software features.
exercise: Free of charge; per DMA Art. 6(7).
quote: gatekeepers shall in particular allow them effective interoperability with, and, for the purposes of interoperability, access to, the same operating system, hardware or software features
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Access to OS, hardware and software features of gatekeepers; requires building interoperable software. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by trust service providers
description: Anyone who suffers material or non-material damage from an infringement by a trust service provider can seek compensation.
exercise: Claimant proves intent/negligence of non-qualified providers; for qualified providers fault is presumed; no liability beyond limitations notified in advance (Art. 13(2)); national liability rules apply.
quote: Any natural or legal person who has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of an infringement of this Regulation by a trust service provider shall have the right to seek compensation
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Compensation claim against trust service provider; no technical element.

right: Right to accessible and plain-language eID and trust services
rightholder: persons with disabilities, elderly people and persons with limited access to digital technologies
description: eID means, trust services and related end-user products must be provided in plain, intelligible language and meet accessibility requirements.
quote: shall be made available in plain and intelligible language, in accordance with the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object is the accessibility of eID means and trust-service products; used only by operating them. Test: no.

right: Right to be notified of security breaches by non-qualified trust service providers
description: Non-qualified trust service providers must notify identifiable affected individuals of security breaches or disruptions with significant impact.
exercise: Without undue delay, at most 24 hours after awareness.
quote: notifying the supervisory body, the identifiable affected individuals, the public if it is of public interest
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Breach notification is plain information; a letter would do. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information on qualified trust service terms
rightholder: any person seeking to use a qualified trust service
description: Before contracting, the provider must inform the person, publicly and individually, of the precise terms and conditions and limitations of the service.
exercise: Before entering the contract.
quote: inform, in a clear, comprehensive and easily accessible manner, in a publicly accessible space and individually any person seeking to use a qualified trust service of the precise terms and conditions
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Pre-contractual terms information; plain language, any channel works. Test: yes.

right: Right to consent before stored data are made publicly retrievable
rightholder: person to whom the data relates
description: Data stored by a qualified trust service provider may be publicly retrievable only with the consent of the person concerned.
quote: they are publicly available for retrieval only where the consent of the person to whom the data relates has been obtained
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object is public retrievability of stored data, but consent can be given by plain means. Mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to be notified of security breaches by qualified trust service providers
description: Qualified trust service providers must notify identifiable affected individuals of security breaches or disruptions with significant impact.
exercise: Without undue delay and within 24 hours of the incident.
quote: notify the supervisory body, the identifiable affected individuals, other relevant competent bodies where applicable
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Breach notification is plain information; a letter would do. Test: yes.

right: Right to have a requested certificate revocation published within 24 hours
rightholder: holder of a qualified certificate (or qualified attestation of attributes, Art. 24(4a))
description: When a qualified certificate is revoked following a request, the provider must register and publish the revocation status within 24 hours of the request; revocation is effective on publication.
exercise: Request to the provider; publication within 24 hours.
quote: publish the revocation status of the certificate in a timely manner, and in any event within 24 hours after the receipt of the request
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Object (certificate revocation status) is digital, but revocation follows a plain request; holder need not handle output. Test conflicts.

right: Right of relying parties to free certificate validity and revocation information
addressee: qualified trust service provider issuing qualified certificates
description: Relying parties can obtain, free of charge and at any time, automated per-certificate information on the validity or revocation status of qualified certificates.
exercise: Automated, free of charge, also beyond the certificate's validity period.
quote: qualified trust service providers issuing qualified certificates shall provide to any relying party information on the validity or revocation status of qualified certificates issued by them
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Automated per-certificate validity and revocation status (OCSP-type service) queried by software. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to use advanced/qualified electronic signatures for online public services
description: Where an online public service requires an advanced electronic signature, Member States must recognise advanced and qualified signatures in the reference formats, and may not demand more than a qualified signature cross-border.
quote: If a Member State requires an advanced electronic signature to use an online service offered by, or on behalf of, a public sector body, that Member State shall recognise advanced electronic signatures
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Advanced or qualified e-signatures must be accepted for online public services; signing is purely technical. Test: no.

right: Right to use advanced/qualified electronic seals for online public services
description: Where an online public service requires an advanced electronic seal, Member States must recognise advanced and qualified seals in the reference formats, and may not demand more than a qualified seal cross-border.
quote: If a Member State requires an advanced electronic seal in order to use an online service offered by, or on behalf of, a public sector body, that Member State shall recognise advanced electronic seals
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Advanced or qualified e-seals must be accepted for online public services; sealing is purely technical. Test: no.

right: Right to have qualified website authentication certificates recognised and displayed by browsers
rightholder: website operators holding a qualified certificate for website authentication
description: Browser providers must recognise qualified website authentication certificates and display the attested identity data in a user-friendly manner.
exercise: Precautionary measures only under Art. 45a.
quote: Qualified certificates for website authentication issued in accordance with paragraph 1 of this Article shall be recognised by providers of web-browsers.
notes: Micro and small browser providers exempt during their first five years.
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Browsers must recognise and display qualified website certificates; operator must deploy the certificate. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right of certificate holders to be notified of browser precautionary measures
rightholder: entity to whom the website certificate was issued
description: If a browser takes precautionary measures against a certificate, it must notify its concerns and measures in writing to the certificate holder (and others).
exercise: Without undue delay, in writing; supervisory body investigates (Art. 45a(4)).
quote: to the Commission, the competent supervisory body, the entity to whom the certificate was issued and to the qualified trust service provider that issued that certificate
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Written notice of browser measures; plain information, letter suffices. Test: yes.

right: Right to have attributes verified against public authentic sources at the user's request
addressee: Member States (authentic sources) / qualified trust service providers
description: Member States must enable qualified attestation providers to verify, at the user's request, attributes (at least those in Annex VI) against public-sector authentic sources.
exercise: At the request of the user; within 24 months of the implementing acts.
quote: measures are taken to allow qualified trust service providers of electronic attestations of attributes to verify those attributes by electronic means at the request of the user
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Electronic verification of attributes against authentic sources yields an electronic attestation used in the wallet. Test: no.

right: Right to obtain attestations of attributes in any Member State's wallet
addressee: providers of electronic attestations of attributes
description: Attestation providers must let wallet users request, obtain, store and manage attestations regardless of which Member State provided the wallet.
quote: shall provide European Digital Identity Wallet users with the possibility to request, obtain, store and manage the electronic attestation of attributes irrespective of the Member State
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Request, store and manage electronic attestations in any Member State's wallet. Test: no.

right: Right to be informed of an order to suspend or cease a wallet
description: When a supervisory body orders a wallet provider to suspend or cease provision, it must inform wallet users without undue delay.
exercise: Without undue delay.
quote: The supervisory body shall inform the supervisory bodies of other Member States, the Commission, relying parties and users of the European Digital Identity Wallet without undue delay of the decision
entry_current_status: In force, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (European Digital Identity Wallets)
tl_reason: Notice of a suspension order is plain information; letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information (contracts other than distance or off-premises)
description: Before being bound by an on-premises contract, the consumer must receive clear information on the main characteristics, trader identity, total price, delivery and complaint handling, the legal guarantee, durability guarantees, software updates, duration and termination, functionality, interoperability and reparability.
exercise: Provided by the trader before conclusion unless apparent from the context; Member States may exempt day-to-day transactions performed immediately (Art. 5(3)).
quote: Before the consumer is bound by a contract other than a distance or an off-premises contract, or any corresponding offer, the trader shall provide the consumer with the following information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: On-premises pre-contractual information; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information (distance and off-premises contracts)
description: Before a distance or off-premises contract, the consumer must receive detailed information including trader contact details, total price, any price personalisation by automated decision-making, withdrawal conditions and the model withdrawal form, legal guarantee, after-sales services, duration, out-of-court redress and reparability.
exercise: Information forms an integral part of the contract (Art. 6(5)); on paper or durable medium for off-premises contracts (Art. 7(1)); key items shown directly before an online order (Art. 8(2)); burden of proof on the trader (Art. 6(9)).
quote: Before the consumer is bound by a distance or off-premises contract, or any corresponding offer, the trader shall provide the consumer with the following information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Pre-contractual information often shown online; plain content, paper works. Test: yes.

right: Right not to bear undisclosed charges or return costs
description: If the trader did not inform the consumer of additional charges or other costs, or of the cost of returning goods, the consumer does not have to bear them.
exercise: Invoked against the trader when charged.
quote: the consumer shall not bear those charges or costs
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Not bearing undisclosed charges; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to specific information when buying on an online marketplace
description: Before concluding a contract on an online marketplace, the consumer must be told the main ranking parameters, whether the third-party seller is a trader, that EU consumer rights do not apply if it is not, and how contractual obligations are shared between the seller and the marketplace.
exercise: Provided by the marketplace provider in a way appropriate to the means of distance communication.
quote: the provider of the online marketplace shall, without prejudice to Directive 2005/29/EC, provide the consumer with the following information in a clear and comprehensible manner
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2019/2161. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Information on marketplace ranking parameters concerns software behaviour, but is plain-language and needs no technical means. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to a copy or confirmation of an off-premises contract
description: For off-premises contracts the consumer receives a copy of the signed contract or a confirmation, including any consent and acknowledgement relating to loss of the withdrawal right.
exercise: On paper or, if the consumer agrees, another durable medium.
quote: The trader shall provide the consumer with a copy of the signed contract or the confirmation of the contract on paper or, if the consumer agrees, on another durable medium
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Copy of contract on paper or durable medium. Test: yes.

right: Right not to be bound by an online order without a clearly labelled payment button
description: For online orders that involve payment, key information must be shown directly before ordering and the order button must state 'order with obligation to pay' or equivalent; if not, the consumer is not bound by the contract or order.
exercise: Invoked against the trader; also applies to passenger transport and package travel (Art. 3(3)).
quote: If the trader has not complied with this subparagraph, the consumer shall not be bound by the contract or order.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Applies to online order buttons, but non-bindingness is invoked by plain statement. Test: yes.

right: Right to be told the caller's identity and commercial purpose in telephone sales
description: When a trader phones a consumer to conclude a distance contract, the trader must disclose at the start its identity (and that of any principal) and the commercial purpose of the call.
exercise: At the beginning of the call; Member States may require written confirmation before the consumer is bound (Art. 8(6)).
quote: disclose his identity and, where applicable, the identity of the person on whose behalf he makes that call, and the commercial purpose of the call
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Caller identity disclosure in phone sales; no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to confirmation of a distance contract on a durable medium
description: After a distance contract, the consumer receives a confirmation on a durable medium containing the pre-contractual information and any consent or acknowledgement on loss of the withdrawal right.
exercise: Within a reasonable time, at the latest on delivery of goods or before performance of the service begins.
quote: The trader shall provide the consumer with the confirmation of the contract concluded, on a durable medium within a reasonable time after the conclusion of the distance contract
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Confirmation of distance contract on durable medium, usually email; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right of withdrawal from distance and off-premises contracts
description: The consumer may withdraw from a distance or off-premises contract within 14 days without giving reasons and without costs other than direct return costs and those in Arts 13(2) and 14.
exercise: Period runs from conclusion (services, utilities, online digital content) or from physical possession of goods (Art. 9(2)); extended by up to 12 months if the consumer was not informed (Art. 10); Member States may extend to 30 days for unsolicited home visits and excursions (Art. 9(1a)); exercised by the model form or any unequivocal statement sent before expiry (Art. 11); exceptions in Art. 16.
quote: the consumer shall have a period of 14 days to withdraw from a distance or off-premises contract, without giving any reason
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Withdrawal by model form or any statement, often online; letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to withdraw using an online withdrawal function
description: For distance contracts concluded through an online interface, the consumer can withdraw through a prominently displayed, continuously available 'withdraw from contract here' function followed by a 'confirm withdrawal' function, and receives an acknowledgement of receipt on a durable medium.
exercise: Online withdrawal statement with name, contract details and the electronic means for the confirmation; submission before the period expires is timely (Art. 11a(5)); also applies to distance financial services contracts (Art. 3(1b)).
quote: For distance contracts concluded by the means of an online interface, the trader shall ensure that the consumer can also withdraw from the contract by using a withdrawal function.
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Trader must provide 'withdraw from contract here' function; this right is the button itself. Test: no.

right: Right to reimbursement of all payments after withdrawal
description: After withdrawal the trader must refund all payments, including standard delivery costs, within 14 days of being informed, using the same means of payment and without fees for the consumer.
exercise: Trader may withhold the refund until goods are received back or proof of dispatch is supplied (Art. 13(3)); extra cost of a non-standard delivery chosen by the consumer is not refunded (Art. 13(2)).
quote: The trader shall reimburse all payments received from the consumer, including, if applicable, the costs of delivery without undue delay and in any event not later than 14 days
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Refund after withdrawal; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to retrieve user-generated content after withdrawal from a digital content or service contract
description: After withdrawal, the consumer can obtain the non-personal content they provided or created while using the digital content or service, free of charge and in a commonly used, machine-readable format; the trader must otherwise stop using it.
exercise: Request to the trader (Art. 13(6)); within a reasonable time; exceptions for content with no utility outside the service, relating only to the consumer's activity, or aggregated (Art. 13(5)); personal data governed by the GDPR (Art. 13(4)).
quote: The consumer shall be entitled to retrieve that digital content free of charge, without hindrance from the trader, within a reasonable time and in a commonly used and machine-readable format.
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2019/2161. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Content returned in commonly used machine-readable format for reuse elsewhere; result unusable without technical means. Test: no.

right: Right to bear no cost for performance during the withdrawal period in specified cases
description: The consumer pays nothing for services, utilities or online digital content supplied during the withdrawal period if the trader failed to give the required information or did not obtain the consumer's express request, consent, acknowledgement or confirmation.
exercise: Invoked against the trader after withdrawal; no other liability for exercising withdrawal (Art. 14(5)); no liability for diminished value of goods if not informed of the withdrawal right (Art. 14(2)).
quote: The consumer shall bear no cost for:
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: No payment for performance during withdrawal period; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Automatic cost-free termination of ancillary contracts on withdrawal
description: When the consumer withdraws from a distance or off-premises contract, any ancillary contracts end automatically without cost to the consumer.
exercise: Follows automatically from withdrawal; detailed rules set by Member States (Art. 15(2)).
quote: any ancillary contracts shall be automatically terminated, without any costs for the consumer
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Automatic termination of ancillary contracts. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information for distance financial services contracts
description: In good time before a distance financial services contract, the consumer receives information on the trader, the service, total price, risks, personalised pricing, withdrawal right, early termination, applicable law, languages, out-of-court redress and guarantee funds.
exercise: On a durable medium and easy to read (Art. 16a(6)); layered information must be viewable and printable as one document (Art. 16a(7)); reduced set for voice telephony with the consumer's agreement, remainder immediately after conclusion (Art. 16a(4)); burden of proof on the trader (Art. 16a(8)).
quote: In good time before the consumer is bound by a distance contract, or any corresponding offer, the trader shall provide the consumer, in a clear and comprehensible manner
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Distance financial-services information on durable medium; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to be told of trader identity, commercial purpose and call recording in financial services phone calls
description: In trader-initiated phone calls about financial services, the trader's identity and commercial purpose must be made clear at the start, and the consumer must be told if the call is or may be recorded.
exercise: At the beginning of the call.
quote: When a call is being recorded, or might be recorded, the trader shall also notify the consumer that this is the case.
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Phone-call disclosures; no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to a withdrawal reminder when information was given less than one day before conclusion
description: If pre-contractual information reached the consumer less than a day before a distance financial services contract was concluded, the trader must send a reminder of the right to withdraw and how to do it.
exercise: Reminder on a durable medium between one and seven days after conclusion.
quote: Member States shall require that the trader sends a reminder to the consumer of the possibility to withdraw from the distance contract and of the procedure to follow for withdrawing
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Withdrawal reminder on durable medium in distance context; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right of consumers with disabilities to pre-contractual information in an accessible format
description: Consumers with disabilities, including visual impairment, can obtain the financial services pre-contractual information in an appropriate and accessible format.
exercise: On request to the trader.
quote: The information referred to in paragraph 1 shall be provided upon request in an appropriate and accessible format to consumers with disabilities, including those with a visual impairment.
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Accessible-format information on request; format need not be digital. Test: yes.

right: Right of withdrawal from distance financial services contracts
description: The consumer may withdraw from a distance financial services contract within 14 calendar days (30 for personal pension operations) without penalty and without giving reasons.
exercise: Period runs from conclusion or from receipt of terms and information if later; if information was not received, it ends 12 months and 14 days after conclusion (no end date if not informed of the withdrawal right); timely if sent before expiry (Art. 16b(3)); online withdrawal function available (Art. 11a); exceptions for market-fluctuation services, short travel/baggage insurance and fully performed contracts (Art. 16b(2)); sector-specific Union acts prevail (Art. 16b(6)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that the consumer has a period of 14 calendar days to withdraw from a contract without penalty and without giving any reason.
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Withdrawal by statement, online function optional; letter works. Test: yes.

right: Right to be released from ancillary contracts on withdrawal from a financial services contract
description: When the consumer withdraws from a distance financial services contract, they are not bound by related ancillary service contracts, and terminating them costs nothing.
exercise: Follows from withdrawal under Art. 16b.
quote: the consumer shall not be bound by the ancillary contract if the consumer exercises his or her right of withdrawal in accordance with this Article
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Release from ancillary contracts; automatic. Test: yes.

right: Right to a refund within 30 days after withdrawal from a financial services contract
description: After withdrawal the trader must return all sums received within 30 calendar days, keeping only a proportionate, non-penal amount for services actually provided.
exercise: The consumer can be charged only if duly informed of the amount and if performance began at the consumer's request (Art. 16c(1), (3)); Member States may exclude any payment for insurance contracts (Art. 16c(2)).
quote: return to the consumer any sums the trader has received from him or her in accordance with the distance contract, except for the amount referred to in paragraph 1
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Refund after withdrawal; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to adequate explanations before a financial services contract
description: Before conclusion, the consumer receives free explanations of the pre-contractual information, the contract's essential characteristics and its specific effects (including consequences of payment default) so they can judge whether it suits their needs and finances.
