exercise: Free of charge, before conclusion; manner and extent may be specified by Member States (Art. 16d(2)); burden of proof on the trader (Art. 16d(4)).
quote: traders are required to provide adequate explanations to the consumer concerning the proposed financial services contracts
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Explanations before distance financial contract; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to request human intervention when online tools are used
description: Where the trader uses online tools for distance financial services, the consumer can request and obtain human intervention at the pre-contractual stage and, in justified cases, after conclusion.
exercise: Request to the trader; in the same language as the pre-contractual information.
quote: the consumer shall have a right to request and to obtain human intervention at the pre-contractual stage, and in justified cases after the distance contract has been concluded
notes: Inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673, applicable from 19 June 2026. Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Object is online/automated tools, but request is plain and result is human contact. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to delivery of goods within the agreed time or 30 days
description: Unless otherwise agreed, the trader must deliver goods by transferring physical possession or control to the consumer without undue delay and within 30 days of conclusion.
exercise: Enforced through the termination right in Art. 18(2) and other national remedies (Art. 18(4)).
quote: the trader shall deliver the goods by transferring the physical possession or control of the goods to the consumer without undue delay, but not later than 30 days from the conclusion of the contract
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Delivery of goods; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate the contract for late delivery
description: If goods are not delivered on time, the consumer may set an additional period and terminate if delivery still fails; termination is immediate where the trader refused delivery or the date was essential. The trader must then refund all sums paid.
exercise: Call on the trader to deliver within an appropriate additional period, then terminate; refund without undue delay (Art. 18(3)); other national remedies remain (Art. 18(4)).
quote: If the trader fails to deliver the goods within that additional period of time, the consumer shall be entitled to terminate the contract.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Termination for late delivery; contract remedy. Test: yes.

right: Protection against payment-method fees above cost
description: Traders may not charge consumers fees for using a given means of payment that exceed the trader's own cost.
exercise: Invoked against the trader; also applies to financial services, passenger transport and package travel.
quote: Member States shall prohibit traders from charging consumers, in respect of the use of a given means of payment, fees that exceed the cost borne by the trader for the use of such means.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Ban on excessive payment fees; no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Risk passes to the consumer only on physical possession
description: When the trader dispatches goods, risk of loss or damage stays with the trader until the consumer (or a third party they name, other than the carrier) takes physical possession, unless the consumer chose a carrier the trader did not offer.
exercise: Invoked against the trader if goods are lost or damaged in transit.
quote: the risk of loss of or damage to the goods shall pass to the consumer when he or a third party indicated by the consumer and other than the carrier has acquired the physical possession of the goods
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Passing of risk; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to contact the trader by phone at no more than the basic rate
description: When calling a trader's telephone line about a concluded contract, the consumer is not obliged to pay more than the basic rate.
exercise: Applies to post-contract hotlines; telecom providers may still charge for the call.
quote: the consumer, when contacting the trader is not bound to pay more than the basic rate
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Phone hotline at basic rate; no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to refuse extra payments without express consent (no pre-ticked boxes)
description: Any extra payment beyond the main price requires the consumer's express consent; consent inferred from default options the consumer must reject entitles the consumer to a refund.
exercise: Claim reimbursement from the trader.
quote: has inferred it by using default options which the consumer is required to reject in order to avoid the additional payment, the consumer shall be entitled to reimbursement of this payment
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Pre-ticked boxes mostly online, but refund claimed by plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right of consumer and professional organisations to take enforcement action
rightholder: consumer organisations and professional organisations having a legitimate interest (as determined by national law)
addressee: national courts or competent administrative bodies
description: Consumer organisations and professional organisations with a legitimate interest can go to court or to administrative bodies to ensure the national rules transposing the Directive are applied.
exercise: Standing determined by national law.
quote: may take action under national law before the courts or before the competent administrative bodies to ensure that the national provisions transposing this Directive are applied
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Public bodies also listed but not recorded.
tl_reason: Enforcement action by organisations; judicial. Test: yes.

right: Exemption from payment for unsolicited goods or services (inertia selling)
description: The consumer owes nothing for unsolicited supply of goods, utilities or digital content or unsolicited services, and silence does not count as consent.
exercise: Invoked against the trader.
quote: The consumer shall be exempted from the obligation to provide any consideration in cases of unsolicited supply
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: No payment for unsolicited supply; contract rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to supply of the digital content or digital service
description: The trader must supply the digital content or service, unless otherwise agreed without undue delay after conclusion, by making it available or accessible to the consumer or a facility they chose.
exercise: Burden of proof of supply on the trader (Art. 12(1)); remedy in Art. 13. Applies also where the consumer provides personal data instead of a price (Art. 3(1)).
quote: Unless the parties have agreed otherwise, the trader shall supply the digital content or digital service without undue delay after the conclusion of the contract.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Object is digital content made available to consumer or chosen facility; result unusable without technical means. Test: no.

right: Right to digital content or services in conformity with the contract
description: The digital content or service must meet the contract's requirements and objective standards of fitness, functionality, compatibility, accessibility, continuity and security, come with expected accessories and instructions, and be the latest version (Arts 7-9).
exercise: Trader liable for non-conformity at supply (at least two years where national law sets a period) or throughout continuous supply (Art. 11); burden of proof on the trader for one year or the supply period (Art. 12); remedies in Art. 14.
quote: The trader shall supply to the consumer digital content or a digital service that meets the requirements set out in Articles 7, 8 and 9, where applicable
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Object is software behaviour (functionality, compatibility, security); holder must check technical result. Test: no.

right: Right to updates, including security updates
description: The consumer must be informed of and supplied with updates, including security updates, needed to keep the content or service in conformity, for the contract period or the period the consumer can reasonably expect.
exercise: Trader not liable for defects caused solely by the consumer's failure to install an update it was informed about (Art. 8(3)).
quote: The trader shall ensure that the consumer is informed of and supplied with updates, including security updates, that are necessary to keep the digital content or digital service in conformity
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Trader must supply updates; holder must install them; duty only technically fulfillable. Test: no.

right: Right to conformity remedies where third-party rights restrict use
description: If a violation of a third party's rights (e.g. intellectual property) prevents or limits use of the content or service, the consumer can use the lack-of-conformity remedies.
exercise: Remedies under Art. 14, unless national law provides for nullity or rescission instead.
quote: Member States shall ensure that the consumer is entitled to the remedies for lack of conformity provided for in Article 14
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Remedies for legal (IP) non-conformity; contract remedy. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate for failure to supply
description: If the trader fails to supply, the consumer calls on it to supply and may terminate if it still fails; immediate termination where the trader has refused or the supply date was essential (Art. 13(2)).
exercise: Statement to the trader (Art. 15); refund and other effects under Arts 16-18.
quote: within an additional period of time, as expressly agreed to by the parties, the consumer shall be entitled to terminate the contract
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Termination statement for non-supply of digital content; plain statement works. Test: yes.

right: Right to have digital content or services brought into conformity
description: In case of non-conformity, the consumer can require the trader to bring the content or service into conformity unless that is impossible or disproportionately costly.
exercise: Free of charge, within a reasonable time after the consumer informs the trader, and without significant inconvenience (Art. 14(3)).
quote: The consumer shall be entitled to have the digital content or digital service brought into conformity, unless this would be impossible
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Fixing digital content is only possible technically; holder must check fix works. Test: no.

right: Right to a proportionate price reduction
description: Where bringing into conformity is impossible, disproportionate, not done, unsuccessful, or the defect is serious, a paying consumer can obtain a price reduction proportionate to the loss in value (for the non-conformity period in continuous supply).
exercise: Statement to the trader; refund within 14 days, same means of payment, no fee (Art. 18).
quote: The consumer shall be entitled to either a proportionate reduction of the price in accordance with paragraph 5
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Price reduction; money claim. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate the contract for lack of conformity
description: In the same situations (Art. 14(4)) the consumer can terminate the contract; where a price was paid, only if the non-conformity is not minor, with the burden of proof on the trader.
exercise: Statement to the trader expressing the decision to terminate (Art. 15); effects under Arts 16-18.
quote: the consumer shall be entitled to terminate the contract only if the lack of conformity is not minor
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Where the consumer 'pays' with data, termination is available even for minor defects.
tl_reason: Termination statement for digital content contract; plain statement works. Test: yes.

right: Right to reimbursement on termination
description: On termination the trader refunds all sums paid; for continuous supply, the part of the price for the non-conformity period plus any prepaid amount for the remaining term.
exercise: Within 14 days of being informed, same means of payment, no fee (Art. 18).
quote: In the event of termination of the contract, the trader shall reimburse the consumer for all sums paid under the contract.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Reimbursement on termination; money claim. Test: yes.

right: Right to retrieve user-generated content after termination
description: After termination, the consumer can obtain the non-personal content they provided or created, free of charge, without hindrance, within a reasonable time and in a commonly used, machine-readable format; the trader must otherwise stop using it.
exercise: Request to the trader; exceptions for content with no utility outside the service, relating only to the consumer's activity, or aggregated (Art. 16(3)); personal data under the GDPR (Art. 16(2)).
quote: The consumer shall be entitled to retrieve that digital content free of charge, without hindrance from the trader, within a reasonable time and in a commonly used and machine-readable format.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: Content returned in commonly used machine-readable format for reuse; result needs technical means. Test: no.

right: Right not to pay for use during the period of non-conformity
description: After termination the consumer owes nothing for using the content or service during the period before termination when it was not in conformity.
exercise: Invoked against the trader on termination.
quote: The consumer shall not be liable to pay for any use made of the digital content or digital service in the period, prior to the termination of the contract
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law
tl_reason: No payment for non-conforming period; money rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate free of charge after a detrimental modification
description: If the trader modifies content or a service supplied over time and this more than minimally harms the consumer's access or use, the consumer can terminate free of charge; the consumer must be informed in advance on a durable medium of the change and this right.
exercise: Within 30 days of the information or the modification, whichever is later; not available if the trader lets the consumer keep the unmodified version at no extra cost (Art. 19(4)); Arts 15-18 apply.
quote: the consumer shall be entitled to terminate the contract free of charge within 30 days of the receipt of the information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies only to contracts concluded from 1 January 2022 (Art. 24(2)).
tl_reason: Triggered by software modification, but termination is a plain statement. Test: yes.

right: Trader's right of redress against liable persons in the chain of transactions
addressee: persons liable in previous links of the chain of commercial transactions
description: A trader held liable to a consumer for failure to supply or non-conformity caused by someone earlier in the chain can pursue remedies against that person.
exercise: Against whom, which actions and conditions are determined by national law.
quote: the trader shall be entitled to pursue remedies against the person or persons liable in the chain of commercial transactions
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies only to contracts concluded from 1 January 2022 (Art. 24(2)).
tl_reason: Trader recourse in commercial chain. Test: yes.

right: Right of consumer, professional and data-protection organisations to take enforcement action
rightholder: consumer organisations, professional organisations, and not-for-profit data-protection bodies under Art. 80 GDPR (as determined by national law)
addressee: national courts or competent administrative bodies
description: Consumer organisations, professional organisations and not-for-profit data-protection bodies can go to court or administrative bodies to ensure the transposing national rules are applied.
exercise: Standing determined by national law.
quote: may take action under national law before the courts or before the competent administrative bodies to ensure that the national provisions transposing this Directive are applied
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Public bodies also listed but not recorded.
tl_reason: Enforcement action by organisations; judicial. Test: yes.

right: Consumer-law liability of marketplaces that create the impression they supply the item
addressee: online platform allowing distance contracts with traders
description: A consumer can hold a marketplace liable under consumer protection law, with no hosting exemption, where the platform made an average consumer believe it (or someone under its control) supplied the item or information.
exercise: Claim under applicable consumer protection law; hosting safe harbour of Art. 6(1) unavailable.
quote: Paragraph 1 shall not apply with respect to the liability under consumer protection law of online platforms that allow consumers to conclude distance contracts with traders
notes: Carve-out from the hosting liability exemption; substantive liability comes from national/Union consumer law.
tl_reason: Consumer-law liability claim; no technical element.

right: Right to be informed of an authority order to act against one's content
description: Recipients whose content is targeted by a national order to act against illegal content must be told of the order and its effect, with a statement of reasons, redress possibilities and territorial scope.
exercise: At the latest when effect is given to the order (or at the time set by the issuing authority).
quote: providers of intermediary services shall inform the recipient of the service concerned of the order received and to the effect given to it
tl_reason: Plain information on an authority order and its effect. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of an authority order to disclose information about oneself
description: Recipients about whom an authority orders the provider to supply information must be informed of the order and its effect, with a statement of reasons and redress possibilities.
exercise: At the latest when effect is given to the order (or at the time set by the issuing authority).
quote: providers of intermediary services shall inform the recipient of the service concerned of the order received and the effect given to it
tl_reason: Plain information on a disclosure order. Test: yes.

right: Right to a single point of contact for users
description: Recipients can communicate directly and rapidly with the provider by electronic means through a single point of contact, choosing the means of communication, which may not rely solely on automated tools.
exercise: Contact details must be public, easily accessible and up to date (Art. 12(2)).
quote: Providers of intermediary services shall designate a single point of contact to enable recipients of the service to communicate directly and rapidly with them
tl_reason: Law requires an electronic communication channel, but the message and reply are non-technical; electronic-channel criterion conflicts with test.

right: Right to clear terms and conditions on content-moderation restrictions
description: Recipients are entitled to terms and conditions that set out, in clear and plain language, any restrictions on use of the service, content-moderation policies and tools (incl. algorithmic decision-making and human review) and the internal complaint rules.
exercise: In the T&Cs, publicly available in machine-readable form; services aimed at or mainly used by minors must explain conditions in a way minors understand (Art. 14(3)).
quote: Providers of intermediary services shall include information on any restrictions that they impose in relation to the use of their service
notes: Art. 14(3) child-friendly explanation folded in.
tl_reason: Clear terms and conditions are plain information; machine-readability serves others. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of significant changes to terms and conditions
description: Recipients must be informed of any significant change to the provider's terms and conditions.
quote: Providers of intermediary services shall inform the recipients of the service of any significant change to the terms and conditions.
tl_reason: Notice of significant changes is plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to diligent, objective and proportionate enforcement of terms and conditions
description: Restrictions under the T&Cs must be applied and enforced diligently, objectively and proportionately, with due regard to recipients' fundamental rights such as freedom of expression and media pluralism.
exercise: Can be relied on in internal complaints, out-of-court settlement, complaints to the DSC and court.
quote: Providers of intermediary services shall act in a diligent, objective and proportionate manner in applying and enforcing the restrictions referred to in paragraph 1
tl_reason: Standard of conduct for enforcing terms; no mechanism or technical ability.

right: Right to a concise summary of terms and conditions incl. remedies (VLOPs/VLOSEs)
description: Users of very large platforms and search engines receive a concise, easily accessible, machine-readable summary of the T&Cs, including available remedies and redress mechanisms; the T&Cs must be published in all official languages of the Member States where the service is offered (Art. 14(6)).
quote: shall provide recipients of services with a concise, easily-accessible and machine-readable summary of the terms and conditions, including the available remedies and redress mechanisms
notes: Only VLOPs/VLOSEs; applies 4 months after designation (Art. 33(6), Art. 92).
tl_reason: Concise summary is read as plain text; machine-readability not needed by the holder. Test: yes.

right: Right to notify illegal content (notice and action)
description: Anyone can notify a hosting provider of specific content they consider illegal, through an easy-to-access, user-friendly electronic mechanism; the provider must process the notice in a timely, diligent, non-arbitrary and objective manner (Art. 16(6)).
exercise: Electronic submission; notice should contain reasons, exact URL, name and email (except for child sexual abuse offences) and a good-faith statement (Art. 16(2)).
quote: Providers of hosting services shall put mechanisms in place to allow any individual or entity to notify them of the presence on their service of specific items of information
tl_reason: Notice must go through an electronic mechanism with exact URL, but notice and outcome are non-technical; electronic-channel criterion conflicts with test.

right: Right of notifier to confirmation of receipt
rightholder: individual or entity that submitted a notice
description: A notifier who gave electronic contact details receives a confirmation of receipt of the notice without undue delay.
exercise: Requires electronic contact information in the notice.
quote: the provider of hosting services shall, without undue delay, send a confirmation of receipt of the notice to that individual or entity
tl_reason: Confirmation of receipt is plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right of notifier to be notified of the decision and of redress possibilities
rightholder: individual or entity that submitted a notice
description: The notifier must be told without undue delay of the provider's decision on the notified content, of the possibilities for redress, and of any use of automated means (Art. 16(6)).
quote: The provider shall also, without undue delay, notify that individual or entity of its decision in respect of the information to which the notice relates
tl_reason: Notification of decision and redress is plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to a statement of reasons for content moderation decisions
description: Users whose content is removed, demoted or restricted, whose payments are suspended, or whose service or account is suspended or terminated receive a clear and specific statement of reasons, including facts, legal or contractual ground, use of automated means and redress options.
exercise: From the date the restriction is imposed; only where electronic contact details are known; not for deceptive high-volume commercial content or Art. 9 orders.
quote: Providers of hosting services shall provide a clear and specific statement of reasons to any affected recipients of the service for any of the following restrictions
tl_reason: Explains moderation of digital content incl. automated means, but the statement is plain language deliverable by letter; digital object conflicts with test.

right: Right to lodge an internal complaint against moderation decisions
rightholder: recipient of the service, incl. notifiers
description: Users and notifiers can complain, electronically and free of charge, against decisions on notices, content removal or restriction, service or account suspension/termination and demonetisation; unfounded decisions must be reversed without undue delay (Art. 20(4)).
exercise: Within at least 6 months from being informed of the decision (Art. 20(2)); free of charge; electronic.
quote: access to an effective internal complaint-handling system that enables them to lodge complaints, electronically and free of charge, against the decision taken by the provider of the online platform
notes: Not applicable to micro/small platforms unless designated VLOPs (Art. 19).
tl_reason: Complaints must be lodged electronically in the platform system, but complaint and outcome are non-technical; electronic-channel criterion conflicts with test.

right: Right to a reasoned decision on an internal complaint
description: Complainants are informed without undue delay of the reasoned decision on their complaint and of the possibility of out-of-court dispute settlement and other redress.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall inform complainants without undue delay of their reasoned decision in respect of the information to which the complaint relates
tl_reason: Reasoned decision on the complaint is plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to complaint decisions not taken solely by automated means
description: Decisions on internal complaints must be taken under the supervision of appropriately qualified staff and not solely by automated means.
quote: are taken under the supervision of appropriately qualified staff, and not solely on the basis of automated means
tl_reason: Object is automated decision-making, but the human-supervision guarantee asks nothing technical of the holder and the result is plain; ability criterion fails.

right: Right to select a certified out-of-court dispute settlement body
rightholder: recipient of the service, incl. notifiers
addressee: provider of online platform; certified ODS body
description: Users and notifiers addressed by platform moderation decisions can take the dispute to any certified out-of-court dispute settlement body, including where the internal complaint was not resolved; the platform must engage in good faith.
exercise: Free of charge or nominal fee for the recipient (Art. 21(5)); decision within 90 days (extendable to 180); non-binding; platform may refuse if same dispute already resolved.
quote: shall be entitled to select any out-of-court dispute settlement body that has been certified in accordance with paragraph 3 of this Article in order to resolve disputes relating to those decisions
notes: Information on ODS access must be easily accessible on the platform interface.
tl_reason: ODS bodies offer online access, but a plain submission works and the decision is non-technical. Test: yes.

right: Right to contest platform decisions before a court at any stage
description: Recipients may at any stage bring court proceedings to contest platform moderation decisions, irrespective of internal complaint or out-of-court settlement.
exercise: Under applicable national procedural law.
quote: the right of the recipient of the service concerned to initiate, at any stage, proceedings to contest those decisions by the providers of online platforms before a court
notes: Third subparagraph of Art. 21(1); framed as 'without prejudice' to that right.
tl_reason: Court proceedings; no technical element.

right: Right of a dispute settlement body to apply for certification
description: A body meeting the independence, expertise, remuneration, accessibility, efficiency and fair-procedure conditions can apply to the DSC of its establishment for certification as an out-of-court dispute settlement body.
exercise: Application to DSC of establishment; certification up to 5 years, renewable.
quote: certify the body, at its request, where the body has demonstrated that it meets all of the following conditions
tl_reason: Certification application to the DSC; no technical element.

right: Right to reimbursement of dispute settlement fees and expenses
rightholder: recipient of the service, incl. notifiers
description: If the ODS body decides in the recipient's favour, the platform bears all fees and reimburses the recipient's other reasonable expenses; if it decides against, the recipient need not reimburse the platform's costs unless acting manifestly in bad faith.
exercise: Fees must be disclosed before the procedure; free or nominal fee for recipients.
quote: the provider of the online platform shall bear all the fees charged by the out-of-court dispute settlement body, and shall reimburse that recipient
tl_reason: Reimbursement of fees and expenses; no technical element.

right: Right of a certified ODS body to react before revocation
description: Before revoking a certification, the DSC must give the body an opportunity to react to the investigation findings and the intended revocation.
quote: the Digital Services Coordinator shall afford that body an opportunity to react to the findings of its investigation
tl_reason: Procedural right to react before revocation; no technical element.

right: Right of trusted flaggers to priority processing of notices
description: Notices from trusted flaggers within their area of expertise must be given priority and decided without undue delay.
exercise: Via Art. 16 notice mechanisms.
quote: notices submitted by trusted flaggers, acting within their designated area of expertise, through the mechanisms referred to in Article 16, are given priority
tl_reason: Priority via the Art. 16 electronic notice channel; technology incidental to the priority right; holder is a trusted flagger. Test: yes.

right: Right to apply for trusted flagger status
description: An entity with expertise in detecting illegal content, independent of platforms and acting diligently can apply for trusted flagger status.
exercise: Application to DSC of the Member State of establishment.
quote: The status of ‘trusted flagger’ under this Regulation shall be awarded, upon application by any entity, by the Digital Services Coordinator
tl_reason: Application for trusted flagger status to the DSC; no technical element.

right: Right of trusted flagger to react before revocation of status
description: Before revoking trusted flagger status, the DSC must let the entity react to the investigation findings and the intended revocation.
quote: the Digital Services Coordinator shall afford the entity an opportunity to react to the findings of its investigation and its intention to revoke the entity’s status as trusted flagger
tl_reason: Procedural right to react before revocation; no technical element.

right: Right to a prior warning and case-by-case assessment before suspension for misuse
rightholder: recipient of the service; notifier; complainant
description: Users who frequently post manifestly illegal content, or who frequently file manifestly unfounded notices or complaints, may only be suspended for a reasonable period after a prior warning and an individual, objective assessment based on published criteria.
exercise: Policy, examples and suspension duration must be set out in the T&Cs (Art. 23(4)).
quote: Providers of online platforms shall suspend, for a reasonable period of time and after having issued a prior warning, the provision of their services
tl_reason: Prior warning and individual assessment before suspension; plain information, nothing technical. Test: yes.

right: Right not to be subjected to deceptive or manipulative interface design (dark patterns)
description: Platforms must not design or operate their interfaces so as to deceive or manipulate users or otherwise impair their ability to make free and informed decisions.
exercise: Enforceable via complaint (Art. 53) and compensation (Art. 54).
quote: Providers of online platforms shall not design, organise or operate their online interfaces in a way that deceives or manipulates the recipients of their service
notes: Protective prohibition; does not apply to practices covered by UCPD or GDPR (Art. 25(2)).
tl_reason: Object is interface design, fulfillable only technically, but protection is passive: no mechanism to operate or ability needed; ability criterion fails.

right: Right to identify advertisements, advertiser and targeting parameters
description: For each ad shown to them, users must be able to see in real time that it is an ad, on whose behalf it is shown, who paid for it, and the main targeting parameters and how to change them.
exercise: Directly and easily accessible from the advertisement.
quote: the recipients of the service are able to identify, in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner and in real time, the following
tl_reason: Per-ad real-time information reachable from the ad interface; not obtainable by letter, holder interprets targeting parameters. Test: no.

right: Right to declare one's content as commercial communication
description: Users who post content get a functionality to declare that it is or contains commercial communications, which the platform then labels for other users.
exercise: Via the platform functionality.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall provide recipients of the service with a functionality to declare whether the content they provide is or contains commercial communications.
tl_reason: Platform must provide a functionality to declare commercial content, which labels it; the right is the interface option. Test: no.

right: Right not to be shown ads based on profiling using sensitive data
description: Platforms may not present advertisements based on profiling that uses special categories of personal data (GDPR Art. 9(1)).
quote: Providers of online platforms shall not present advertisements to recipients of the service based on profiling as defined in Article 4, point (4), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679
notes: Protective prohibition.
tl_reason: Object is ad-targeting software behaviour, but the ban is passive; holder operates nothing; ability criterion fails.

right: Right to information on recommender system parameters and options
description: Platforms must explain in their T&Cs the main parameters of their recommender systems, why information is suggested, and any options for users to modify or influence those parameters.
exercise: In the terms and conditions.
quote: the main parameters used in their recommender systems, as well as any options for the recipients of the service to modify or influence those main parameters
tl_reason: Object is recommender software, but the explanation sits in plain-language terms and conditions needing no mechanism; mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to select and modify the preferred recommender option at any time
description: Where several recommender options exist, users can select and change their preferred option at any time through a functionality directly accessible where content is ranked.
exercise: Directly and easily accessible in the relevant section of the interface.
quote: make available a functionality that allows the recipient of the service to select and to modify at any time their preferred option
tl_reason: Functionality to select the recommender option must exist in the interface; without it the right does not exist. Test: no.

right: Right of minors not to receive profiling-based advertising
rightholder: recipient of the service who is a minor
description: Platforms may not present profiling-based advertisements to users they know with reasonable certainty to be minors.
quote: Providers of online platform shall not present advertisements on their interface based on profiling as defined in Article 4, point (4), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 using personal data
notes: Protective prohibition; no obligation to process extra data to assess age (Art. 28(3)).
tl_reason: Object is ad-targeting software behaviour, but the ban protects minors passively; no mechanism or ability; ability criterion fails.

right: Right of traders to complain about refusal or suspension of access to a marketplace
addressee: provider of online platform allowing distance contracts
description: A trader refused access to, or suspended from, a marketplace under the trader-traceability rules may use the internal complaint system and out-of-court dispute settlement.
exercise: Via Arts 20 and 21.
quote: the trader concerned shall have the right to lodge a complaint as provided for in Articles 20 and 21 of this Regulation
notes: Without prejudice to P2B Regulation Art. 4.
tl_reason: Trader uses the Art. 20/21 complaint routes; complaint and outcome non-technical; holder is a business. Test: yes.

right: Right to trader identity information on marketplace listings
addressee: provider of online platform allowing distance contracts
description: Consumers can see the trader's name, address, telephone, email, trade register details and compliance self-certification on the interface where the product or service is presented.
quote: shall make the information referred to in paragraph 1, points (a), (d) and (e) available on its online platform to the recipients of the service
tl_reason: Trader details displayed on the interface are plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to information about illegal products or services purchased
addressee: provider of online platform allowing distance contracts
description: Consumers who bought an illegal product or service through a marketplace in the previous six months must be told that it is illegal, the trader's identity and the relevant means of redress.
exercise: Directly where contact details are held; otherwise via public notice on the interface (Art. 32(2)).
quote: that provider shall inform, insofar as it has their contact details, consumers who purchased the illegal product or service through its services
notes: Article heading: 'Right to information'.
tl_reason: Notification about an illegal purchase is plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right of a provider to submit views before designation as VLOP/VLOSE
rightholder: provider of online platform or search engine
description: Where the Commission relies on other or additionally requested information, the provider has 10 working days to comment on preliminary findings and the intended designation.
exercise: 10 working days.
quote: the Commission shall give the provider of the online platform or of the online search engine concerned 10 working days in which to submit its views
notes: Applies from 16 Nov 2022 (Art. 93(2)).
tl_reason: Provider's procedural right before the Commission; no technical element.

right: Right to choose a recommender option not based on profiling
description: Users of very large platforms and search engines must be offered, for each recommender system, at least one option that is not based on profiling.
quote: shall provide at least one option for each of their recommender systems which is not based on profiling as defined in Article 4, point (4), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679
notes: Only VLOPs/VLOSEs; applies 4 months after designation (Art. 33(6), Art. 92).
tl_reason: Non-profiling recommender option must exist in the software; without it the right does not exist. Test: no.

right: Right of VLOP/VLOSE to request amendment of a researcher data-access request
description: Within 15 days a provider may ask the DSC to amend a vetted-researcher data request where it lacks access to the data or access would create significant security or confidentiality vulnerabilities, proposing alternatives.
exercise: Within 15 days of the request; DSC decides within 15 days.
quote: may request the Digital Services Coordinator of establishment, to amend the request
notes: Only VLOPs/VLOSEs; applies 4 months after designation (Art. 33(6), Art. 92).
tl_reason: Provider's procedural request to the DSC; no technical element.

right: Right of researchers to apply for vetted-researcher status and data access
addressee: Digital Services Coordinator; provider of VLOP/VLOSE
description: Researchers affiliated to a research organisation, independent of commercial interests and meeting data-security and publication conditions, can apply to obtain vetted status and a reasoned data-access request to a VLOP/VLOSE for systemic-risk research.
exercise: Application to the DSC of establishment or of the research organisation's Member State (Art. 40(9)).
quote: Upon a duly substantiated application from researchers, the Digital Services Coordinator of establishment shall grant such researchers the status of ‘vetted researchers’
notes: Only VLOPs/VLOSEs; applies 4 months after designation (Art. 33(6), Art. 92).
tl_reason: Resulting data access runs through interfaces or APIs, but the application is procedural and researchers are not the governed party; holder criterion fails.

right: Right of vetted researchers to react before termination of access
description: Before terminating data access, the DSC must allow the vetted researcher to react to its findings and the intended termination.
quote: Before terminating the access, the Digital Services Coordinator shall allow the vetted researcher to react to the findings of its investigation
notes: Only VLOPs/VLOSEs; applies 4 months after designation (Art. 33(6), Art. 92).
tl_reason: Procedural right to react before termination of access; no technical element.

right: Right of researchers to access publicly accessible platform data
rightholder: researchers, incl. those affiliated to not-for-profit bodies
description: Researchers meeting independence, funding-disclosure, data-security and necessity conditions get access without undue delay, including real-time where feasible, to publicly accessible data for systemic-risk research.
quote: shall give access without undue delay to data, including, where technically possible, to real-time data, provided that the data is publicly accessible in their online interface by researchers
notes: Only VLOPs/VLOSEs; applies 4 months after designation (Art. 33(6), Art. 92).
tl_reason: Access to (real-time) platform data needs technical means, but researchers are not the governed party; holder criterion fails.

right: Right to submit observations and participate in proceedings on access restriction
rightholder: provider; intended addressees; third parties with a legitimate interest
addressee: Digital Services Coordinator; competent judicial authority
description: Before a DSC requests a court to order temporary restriction of access to a service, interested parties may submit written observations, and the provider, addressees and third parties with a legitimate interest may take part in the court proceedings.
exercise: Observation period of at least two weeks.
quote: any other third party demonstrating a legitimate interest shall be entitled to participate in the proceedings before the competent judicial authority
tl_reason: Participation in proceedings on access restriction; no technical element.

right: Rights of defence in national enforcement proceedings
description: Investigatory and enforcement measures by DSCs must respect private life and the rights of defence, including the right to be heard and access to the file, and are subject to an effective judicial remedy for all affected parties.
exercise: Under national procedural law.
quote: those measures shall only be taken in accordance with the right to respect for private life and the rights of defence, including the rights to be heard and of access to the file
tl_reason: Rights of defence in enforcement proceedings; no technical element.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with the Digital Services Coordinator
rightholder: recipient of the service; mandated body, organisation or association
description: Users (or bodies mandated by them) can complain about any provider's infringement of the DSA to the DSC where they are located or established, which assesses it and may forward it to the DSC of establishment.
exercise: Complaint to DSC of the Member State where the recipient is located or established.
quote: shall have the right to lodge a complaint against providers of intermediary services alleging an infringement of this Regulation
tl_reason: Complaint to the DSC by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right of complaint parties to be heard and informed of complaint status
description: Both the complainant and the provider concerned have the right to be heard and to receive appropriate information on the status of the complaint during the proceedings.
exercise: In accordance with national law.
quote: During these proceedings, both parties shall have the right to be heard and receive appropriate information about the status of the complaint, in accordance with national law.
tl_reason: Hearing and status information in complaint proceedings; no technical element.

right: Right to compensation
description: Users can seek compensation from providers for damage or loss suffered because of the provider's infringement of its DSA obligations.
exercise: Under Union and national law (national courts).
quote: Recipients of the service shall have the right to seek, in accordance with Union and national law, compensation from providers of intermediary services
tl_reason: Compensation claim; no technical element.

right: Right to be heard before Commission decisions
rightholder: provider of VLOP/VLOSE; other person under Art. 67(1)
description: Before a non-compliance, fine or periodic penalty decision, the provider or other person concerned may comment on the Commission's preliminary findings and intended measures; decisions may rest only on objections they could comment on.
exercise: Observations within a period set by the Commission, at least 14 days (Art. 79(2)).
quote: the Commission shall give the provider of the very large online platform or of the very large online search engine concerned or other person referred to in Article 67(1) the opportunity of being heard
notes: Chapter IV Section 4; applies from 16 Nov 2022.
tl_reason: Right to be heard by the Commission; no technical element.

right: Right of access to the Commission's file
rightholder: parties concerned (provider of VLOP/VLOSE; other person under Art. 67(1))
description: Parties to Commission proceedings may access the Commission's file under negotiated disclosure terms, excluding confidential information and internal documents, subject to business secrets.
exercise: Negotiated disclosure; Commission decides terms in case of disagreement.
quote: They shall be entitled to have access to the Commission's file under the terms of a negotiated disclosure
notes: Chapter IV Section 4; applies from 16 Nov 2022.
tl_reason: Access to the Commission's file; procedural, no technical element.

right: Right to Court of Justice review of Commission fines
rightholder: provider of VLOP/VLOSE or other person fined
addressee: Court of Justice of the European Union
description: Decisions imposing fines or periodic penalty payments can be challenged before the CJEU, which has unlimited jurisdiction to cancel, reduce or increase them.
exercise: Action under Art. 261/263 TFEU.
quote: the Court of Justice of the European Union has unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions by which the Commission has imposed fines or periodic penalty payments
notes: Chapter IV Section 4; applies from 16 Nov 2022.
tl_reason: Court review of fines; no technical element.

right: Right to mandate a representative body
description: Users may mandate a not-for-profit body, organisation or association with a legitimate interest in DSA compliance to exercise their DSA rights on their behalf.
exercise: Body must be not-for-profit, properly constituted under Member State law, with DSA compliance among its statutory objectives.
quote: recipients of intermediary services shall at least have the right to mandate a body, organisation or association to exercise the rights conferred by this Regulation on their behalf
notes: Chapter IV Section 5 (applies from 16 Nov 2022); without prejudice to Directive (EU) 2020/1828.
tl_reason: Mandate is an ordinary legal act; no mechanism or technical ability, even if delegated rights are technical. Test: yes.

right: Priority handling of complaints filed by representative bodies
description: Internal complaints filed by mandated representative bodies on behalf of users must be processed and decided with priority and without undue delay.
exercise: Via Art. 20(1) mechanisms.
quote: Providers of online platforms shall take the necessary technical and organisational measures to ensure that complaints submitted by bodies, organisations or associations referred to in paragraph 1
notes: Chapter IV Section 5.
tl_reason: Priority handling within the electronic complaint system; technology incidental; holder is an organisation. Test: yes.

right: Representative actions for DSA infringements
description: By adding the DSA to Annex I of the Representative Actions Directive, qualified entities can bring injunctive and redress actions on behalf of consumers for DSA infringements harming their collective interests.
exercise: Through qualified entities under national law transposing Directive (EU) 2020/1828.
quote: In Annex I to Directive (EU) 2020/1828, the following point is added:
notes: Amendment to Directive (EU) 2020/1828.
tl_reason: Representative actions through qualified entities; no technical element.

right: Right to rebut the gatekeeper presumption
description: An undertaking meeting the thresholds can submit substantiated arguments that it nevertheless does not satisfy the qualitative gatekeeper criteria.
exercise: With the notification under Art. 3(3); may lead to a market investigation under Art. 17(3).
quote: The undertaking providing core platform services may present, with its notification, sufficiently substantiated arguments to demonstrate that, exceptionally, although it meets all the thresholds
tl_reason: Procedural rebuttal before the Commission; no technical element.

right: Right to request reconsideration of a designation decision
description: A designation decision can be reconsidered, amended or repealed on request where facts changed substantially or it relied on incomplete, incorrect or misleading information.
exercise: Request to the Commission.
quote: The Commission may, upon request or on its own initiative, reconsider, amend or repeal at any moment a designation decision adopted pursuant to Article 3
notes: The text does not specify who may make the request.
tl_reason: Reconsideration request to the Commission; no technical element.

right: Right to refuse or withdraw consent to combination and cross-use of personal data
description: Gatekeepers may process end users' data for ads based on third-party services, combine or cross-use data across services, or sign users in to combine data only after a specific choice and GDPR consent.
exercise: Specific choice presented; consent may be refused or withdrawn; after refusal or withdrawal, the request may not be repeated for the same purpose more than once a year.
quote: unless the end user has been presented with the specific choice and has given consent within the meaning of Article 4, point (11), and Article 7 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679
notes: Gatekeeper obligations apply 6 months after the service is listed in the designation decision (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Gatekeeper must present a specific choice in the interface; refusal or withdrawal is a single choice. Test: no. Consistency pass: no interface function required; refusing or a letter still works.

right: Right to offer different prices or conditions through other channels
description: Business users can offer the same products to end users via other intermediaries or their own sites at different prices or conditions (no parity clauses).
quote: The gatekeeper shall not prevent business users from offering the same products or services to end users through third-party online intermediation services
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Commercial freedom (no parity clauses); no technical element.

right: Right to promote offers to and contract with end users outside the platform
description: Business users can, free of charge, communicate and promote offers to end users acquired on the platform or elsewhere and conclude contracts with them, whether or not via the gatekeeper's services.
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow business users, free of charge, to communicate and promote offers, including under different conditions, to end users acquired via its core platform service
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Commercial freedom to promote offers and contract; no technical element.

right: Right to access content acquired outside the platform via business-user apps
description: End users can access and use content, subscriptions and features through a business user's app on the gatekeeper's platform, even if acquired outside the platform.
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow end users to access and use, through its core platform services, content, subscriptions, features or other items, by using the software application of a business user
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Gatekeeper must permit using externally acquired content in business-user apps; usable only by operating apps across services. Test: no.

right: Right to raise non-compliance with public authorities and courts
description: Gatekeepers may not prevent or restrict business users or end users from raising non-compliance issues with any public authority, including national courts.
exercise: Lawful contractual complaint-handling mechanisms remain possible.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not directly or indirectly prevent or restrict business users or end users from raising any issue of non-compliance with the relevant Union or national law by the gatekeeper
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Freedom to raise issues with authorities and courts; no technical element.

right: Right not to be required to use the gatekeeper's identification, browser engine or payment services
description: End users and business users cannot be forced to use the gatekeeper's identification service, web browser engine, payment service or in-app payment system when using business users' services.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not require end users to use, or business users to use, to offer, or to interoperate with, an identification service, a web browser engine or a payment service
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Object is software (ID, browser engine, payment), but protection is passive and alternatives depend on business users; ability criterion conflicts.

right: Right not to be required to subscribe to further core platform services
description: Access to one core platform service may not be made conditional on subscribing to or registering with another of the gatekeeper's core platform services.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not require business users or end users to subscribe to, or register with, any further core platform services
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Ban on tying registration to further services; holder operates nothing, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right of advertisers to daily price and fee information
rightholder: advertisers and third parties authorised by them
description: Advertisers can obtain, for each ad, the price and fees paid, the publisher's remuneration (subject to publisher consent, otherwise the daily average) and the metrics used.
exercise: Upon request; daily; free of charge.
quote: upon the advertiser’s request, with information on a daily basis free of charge, concerning each advertisement placed by the advertiser
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Object is per-ad transaction data, but the law only requires information on request without a technical format; mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right of publishers to daily remuneration and fee information
rightholder: publishers and third parties authorised by them
description: Publishers can obtain, for each ad displayed, the remuneration received and fees paid, the advertiser's price (subject to consent, otherwise the daily average) and the metrics used.
exercise: Upon request; daily; free of charge.
quote: upon the publisher’s request, with free of charge information on a daily basis, concerning each advertisement displayed on the publisher’s inventory
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Object is per-ad remuneration data, but the law only requires information on request without a technical format; mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Protection against the gatekeeper's use of business users' non-public data in competition
description: Gatekeepers may not use non-public data generated or provided by business users (and their customers) on the platform to compete against them.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not use, in competition with business users, any data that is not publicly available that is generated or provided by those business users
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Restriction on the gatekeeper's internal data use; holder operates nothing, no mechanism.

right: Right to un-install software applications
description: End users can easily un-install apps on the gatekeeper's operating system, except apps essential for the device or OS that cannot be offered standalone by third parties.
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow and technically enable end users to easily un-install any software applications on the operating system of the gatekeeper
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Gatekeeper must technically enable uninstalling; exercised only through the device interface. Test: no.

right: Right to change default settings
description: End users can easily change default settings on the gatekeeper's operating system, virtual assistant and web browser that steer them to the gatekeeper's own products.
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow and technically enable end users to easily change default settings on the operating system, virtual assistant and web browser of the gatekeeper
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Default settings must be technically changeable; the right is a setting. Test: no.

right: Right to a choice screen for search engine, virtual assistant and browser
description: At first use, end users are prompted to choose their default online search engine, virtual assistant or web browser from a list of main available providers.
exercise: Prompt at first use of the listed search engine, virtual assistant or browser.
quote: prompting end users, at the moment of the end users’ first use of an online search engine, virtual assistant or web browser of the gatekeeper listed in the designation decision
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Choice screen in the interface; a single choice that cannot exist without it. Test: no.

right: Right to install and use third-party apps and app stores (sideloading) and set them as default
rightholder: end users; providers of software applications and app stores
description: Third-party apps and app stores can be installed, used and accessed outside the gatekeeper's store, and end users can easily set them as default when prompted.
exercise: Gatekeeper may take strictly necessary, proportionate and duly justified integrity and security measures.
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow and technically enable the installation and effective use of third-party software applications or software application stores
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Gatekeeper must technically enable third-party apps and stores; holder installs and operates them. Test: no.

right: Right to non-discriminatory ranking (no self-preferencing)
rightholder: third parties offering services or products (business users)
description: Gatekeepers may not rank, index or crawl their own products more favourably than similar third-party products and must apply transparent, fair and non-discriminatory ranking conditions.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not treat more favourably, in ranking and related indexing and crawling, services and products offered by the gatekeeper itself than similar services or products of a third party.
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Object is ranking and indexing software, but protection is passive for business users; no mechanism to operate; ability criterion fails.

right: Right to switch between apps and services
description: Gatekeepers may not technically or otherwise restrict end users from switching between and subscribing to different apps and services, including internet access services.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not restrict technically or otherwise the ability of end users to switch between, and subscribe to, different software applications and services
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Switching apps and services is done only technically; gatekeeper must not technically restrict it. Test: no.

right: Right to interoperability with operating system and virtual assistant features
rightholder: providers of services and hardware; business users; alternative providers of ancillary services
description: Third-party service and hardware providers get free, effective interoperability with the same OS, hardware and software features available to the gatekeeper's own services and hardware.
exercise: Free of charge; gatekeeper may take strictly necessary and duly justified integrity measures.
quote: The gatekeeper shall allow providers of services and providers of hardware, free of charge, effective interoperability with, and access for the purposes of interoperability to
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Interoperability with OS and hardware features requires technical integration, but holders are third-party providers, not the governed party; holder criterion fails.

right: Right of advertisers and publishers to performance measuring tools and verification data
rightholder: advertisers, publishers and third parties authorised by them
description: Advertisers and publishers get access to the gatekeeper's performance measuring tools and the aggregated and non-aggregated data needed to verify ad inventory independently.
exercise: Upon request; free of charge.
quote: upon their request and free of charge, with access to the performance measuring tools of the gatekeeper and the data necessary for advertisers and publishers to carry out their own
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Access to measuring tools and verification data; result is data to check, unusable without technical means. Test: no.

right: Right to data portability
rightholder: end users and third parties authorised by them
description: End users can port data they provided or generated on the core platform service, with free tools and continuous, real-time access.
exercise: Upon request; free of charge; continuous and real-time access.
quote: The gatekeeper shall provide end users and third parties authorised by an end user, at their request and free of charge, with effective portability of data provided by the end user
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Continuous real-time portability through tools; data must be taken to another service. Test: no.

right: Right of business users to access data generated on the platform
rightholder: business users and third parties authorised by them
description: Business users get free, high-quality, continuous and real-time access to aggregated and non-aggregated data generated through their use of the platform and their customers' engagement.
exercise: Upon request; free of charge; personal data only where directly connected to the end users' use of the business user's offer and the end user opts in by consent.
quote: The gatekeeper shall provide business users and third parties authorised by a business user, at their request, free of charge, with effective, high-quality, continuous and real-time access to
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Continuous real-time data access implies API-based access by business users; unusable without technical means. Test: no.

right: Right of rival search engines to access search data on FRAND terms
rightholder: third-party undertakings providing online search engines
description: Competing search engines can obtain ranking, query, click and view data from the gatekeeper's search engine on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms.
exercise: Upon request; personal data anonymised.
quote: any third-party undertaking providing online search engines, at its request, with access on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms to ranking, query, click and view data
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Access to ranking, query, click and view data is technical, but holders are rival search engines, not the governed party; holder criterion fails.

right: Right to FRAND access conditions to app stores, search engines and social networks
description: Business users get fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory general conditions of access to the gatekeeper's app stores, search engines and social networks.
exercise: Published general conditions of access, assessed by the Commission.
quote: The gatekeeper shall apply fair, reasonable, and non-discriminatory general conditions of access for business users to its software application stores
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: FRAND access conditions are commercial terms; no technical element.

right: Right to an alternative dispute settlement mechanism
description: The gatekeeper's published access conditions must include an alternative dispute settlement mechanism available to business users.
quote: For that purpose, the gatekeeper shall publish general conditions of access, including an alternative dispute settlement mechanism.
notes: Applies to app stores, search engines and social networks listed in the designation decision.
tl_reason: Alternative dispute settlement; no technical element.

right: Right to terminate a core platform service without undue difficulty
description: General termination conditions may not be disproportionate, and termination must be possible without undue difficulty.
quote: The gatekeeper shall ensure that the conditions of termination can be exercised without undue difficulty.
notes: Applies 6 months after listing (Art. 3(10)).
tl_reason: Termination without undue difficulty; contract termination online, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to request interoperability of messaging services
rightholder: providers of number-independent interpersonal communications services offering or intending to offer services in the Union
description: Rival messaging providers can request interoperability with the gatekeeper's messaging service's basic functionalities, phased in over time, with the same security level including end-to-end encryption.
exercise: Request after the reference offer is published (Art. 7(4)); free of charge; reasonable requests met within 3 months; functionalities phased per Art. 7(2).
quote: any provider of number-independent interpersonal communications services offering or intending to offer such services in the Union may request interoperability
notes: Only messaging services listed in the designation decision.
tl_reason: Messaging interoperability requires technical integration, but holder is a competing provider, not the governed party; holder criterion fails.

right: Right to request an extension of interoperability deadlines
description: A gatekeeper can ask for an exceptional extension of interoperability deadlines where needed for effective interoperability and security.
exercise: Reasoned request to the Commission.
quote: The Commission may, exceptionally, upon a reasoned request by the gatekeeper, extend the time limits for compliance under paragraph 2 or 5
tl_reason: Gatekeeper's request for deadline extension; no technical element for a governed party.

right: Right of end users to choose whether to use interoperable messaging features
rightholder: end users of the gatekeeper's and the requesting provider's messaging services
description: End users remain free to decide whether to use the interoperable basic functionalities.
quote: shall remain free to decide whether to make use of the interoperable basic functionalities that may be provided by the gatekeeper pursuant to paragraph 1
notes: Only personal data strictly necessary for interoperability may be exchanged (Art. 7(8)).
tl_reason: End users choose in the interface whether to use interoperable features; the choice exists only as a software option. Test: no.
author_note: Art. 7(7) DMA: family changed from 'consent & objection'; the level stays CLICK.

right: Right to request a compliance specification dialogue
description: A gatekeeper can ask the Commission to assess whether its intended or implemented measures for Articles 6 and 7 are effective.
exercise: Reasoned submission plus non-confidential version; Commission has discretion to engage.
quote: A gatekeeper may request the Commission to engage in a process to determine whether the measures that that gatekeeper intends to implement or has implemented
tl_reason: Gatekeeper's request for a specification dialogue; procedural.

right: Right to request suspension of an obligation on economic-viability grounds
description: A gatekeeper can request exceptional suspension of a specific obligation where compliance would endanger the economic viability of its EU operation, including provisional suspension in urgent cases.
exercise: Reasoned request; decision within 3 months of a complete request; reviewed annually.
quote: Where the gatekeeper demonstrates in a reasoned request that compliance with a specific obligation laid down in Article 5, 6 or 7
tl_reason: Gatekeeper's suspension request; procedural.

right: Right to request an exemption on public health or public security grounds
description: A gatekeeper can request an exemption from a specific obligation on public health or public security grounds, including provisional suspension in urgent cases.
exercise: Reasoned request; decision within 3 months of a complete request.
quote: The Commission may, acting on a reasoned request by a gatekeeper or on its own initiative, adopt an implementing act setting out its decision, to exempt that gatekeeper
tl_reason: Gatekeeper's exemption request; procedural.

right: Right of business users to obtain end-user consent directly on equal terms
description: Where consent is needed for compliance, the gatekeeper must let business users obtain it directly (or provide anonymised data) and may not make it more burdensome than for its own services.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not make the obtaining of that consent by the business user more burdensome than for its own services.
tl_reason: Business freedom to obtain consent on equal terms; market-access rule, holder a business.

right: Right not to be penalised or manipulated for exercising DMA rights and choices
description: Gatekeepers may not degrade service conditions or quality for users exercising their DMA rights or choices, or make exercising them unduly difficult, including through non-neutral choices or manipulative interface design.
quote: The gatekeeper shall not degrade the conditions or quality of any of the core platform services provided to business users or end users who avail themselves of the rights or choices laid down
tl_reason: Object is service quality and choice-interface design, but protection is passive; holder operates nothing; ability criterion fails.

right: Right of interested third parties to comment on preliminary findings, remedies and commitments
description: Interested third parties can comment on the Commission's published non-confidential summaries of envisaged remedies and commitments (also of specification measures under Art. 8(6)).
exercise: Comments within the reasonable timeframe set by the Commission.
quote: Interested third parties may submit their comments within a reasonable timeframe which shall be set by the Commission.
notes: Equivalent comment opportunity in specification proceedings (Art. 8(6)).
tl_reason: Comments in Commission proceedings; no technical element.

right: Right to inform authorities about gatekeeper practices
rightholder: any third party, including business users, competitors, end users and their representatives
addressee: national competent authority or the Commission
description: Anyone can inform the national competent authority or the Commission about gatekeeper practices within the Regulation's scope.
exercise: Information to the national authority or directly to the Commission; authorities have full discretion and no duty to follow up (Art. 27(2)).
quote: may inform the national competent authority of the Member State, enforcing the rules referred to in Article 1(6), or the Commission directly, about any practice or behaviour by gatekeepers
notes: No enforceable follow-up.
tl_reason: Informing authorities by ordinary means; no technical element.

right: Right to be heard
rightholder: gatekeeper, undertaking or association of undertakings concerned
description: Before key decisions (specification, suspension, exemption, market investigations, interim measures, commitments, non-compliance, fines), the party concerned can comment on preliminary findings and envisaged measures.
exercise: Written observations within the time limit set in the preliminary findings, at least 14 days; decisions may rely only on objections the party could comment on.
quote: the Commission shall give the gatekeeper or undertaking or association of undertakings concerned the opportunity of being heard on:
tl_reason: Right to be heard before the Commission; procedural.

right: Rights of defence and right of access to the Commission's file
rightholder: gatekeeper, undertaking or association of undertakings concerned
description: The party concerned has full rights of defence and may access the Commission's file under terms of disclosure, excluding business secrets of others, confidential information and internal documents.
exercise: Access under terms of disclosure; disputes settled by Commission decision.
quote: The gatekeeper, undertaking or association of undertakings concerned shall be entitled to have access to the Commission's file under terms of disclosure
tl_reason: Rights of defence and file access; procedural.

right: Right to bring representative actions for consumers
addressee: national courts or administrative authorities (against gatekeepers)
description: Qualified entities can bring representative actions under the Representative Actions Directive against gatekeeper infringements that harm consumers' collective interests.
exercise: Under national law transposing Directive (EU) 2020/1828.
quote: Directive (EU) 2020/1828 shall apply to the representative actions brought against infringements by gatekeepers of provisions of this Regulation that harm or may harm the collective interests
notes: Cross-reference extending Directive 2020/1828 (see also Art. 52).
tl_reason: Representative actions by qualified entities; no technical element.

right: Right to report breaches with whistleblower protection
description: Persons who report breaches of the DMA enjoy the reporting channels and protection against retaliation of the Whistleblower Directive.
exercise: Under national law transposing Directive (EU) 2019/1937.
quote: Directive (EU) 2019/1937 shall apply to the reporting of all breaches of this Regulation and the protection of persons reporting such breaches.
notes: Cross-reference extending Directive 2019/1937 (see also Art. 51).
tl_reason: Whistleblower reporting channels and protection; no technical element.

right: Right to have Commission decisions reviewed by the Court of Justice
rightholder: undertakings subject to Commission decisions (gatekeepers and others)
addressee: Court of Justice of the European Union
description: Undertakings can challenge Commission decisions before the Court of Justice, which has unlimited jurisdiction over fines and periodic penalty payments and may cancel, reduce or increase them.
exercise: Action before the CJEU (Arts 261 and 263 TFEU).
quote: the Court of Justice has unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions by which the Commission has imposed fines or periodic penalty payments
notes: Arts 21(3) and 23(6) expressly require information decisions and inspection decisions to indicate 'the right to have the decision reviewed by the Court of Justice'.
tl_reason: Court review of Commission decisions; no technical element.

right: Right to carry out text and data mining for scientific research
rightholder: research organisations and cultural heritage institutions
description: Make reproductions and extractions of lawfully accessible works for text and data mining for scientific research, without authorisation.
exercise: Copies stored securely and retainable for research incl. verification (Art. 3(2)); rightholders may apply proportionate security measures (Art. 3(3)); contrary contract terms unenforceable (Art. 7(1)).
quote: for reproductions and extractions made by research organisations and cultural heritage institutions in order to carry out, for the purposes of scientific research, text and data mining
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Mandatory, contract-proof exception.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: TDM inherently requires software the holder runs, but no duty-bearer mechanism (mere copyright exception) and holder is a research organisation, not governed party.

right: Rightholders' right to reserve text and data mining (opt-out)
addressee: persons carrying out text and data mining
description: Exclude their works from the general TDM exception (Art. 4(1)) by an express reservation, e.g. machine-readable means for online content, so TDM then requires authorisation.
exercise: Reservation in an appropriate manner (machine-readable for online content).
