quote: has not been expressly reserved by their rightholders in an appropriate manner, such as machine-readable means in the case of content made publicly available online
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Reservation for online content must be machine-readable and respected by TDM users; without it the opt-out has no effect. Test: no.

right: Right to use works digitally for illustration for teaching
rightholder: educational establishments, their teaching staff and pupils/students
description: Use works digitally, including cross-border, for illustration for teaching to the extent justified by the non-commercial purpose.
exercise: Under the establishment's responsibility, on premises or via a secure electronic environment; source and author indicated; Member States may give priority to available licences (Art. 5(2)); contrary contract terms unenforceable (Art. 7(1)).
quote: in order to allow the digital use of works and other subject matter for the sole purpose of illustration for teaching, to the extent justified by the non-commercial purpose to be achieved
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Mandatory, contract-proof exception.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Exception covers digital use via a secure electronic environment (technical), but holder runs it, no duty-bearer mechanism; holder is educational, not governed party.

right: Right to fair compensation for teaching uses
description: Receive fair compensation for digital teaching uses under Art. 5(1) where the Member State so provides.
quote: Member States may provide for fair compensation for rightholders for the use of their works or other subject matter pursuant to paragraph 1.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Member-State option.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Fair compensation for teaching uses; remuneration, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of cultural heritage institutions to make preservation copies
description: Make copies of works permanently in their collections, in any format or medium, to the extent necessary for preservation.
exercise: Contrary contract terms unenforceable (Art. 7(1)).
quote: in order to allow cultural heritage institutions to make copies of any works or other subject matter that are permanently in their collections, in any format or medium, for purposes of preservation
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Mandatory, contract-proof exception.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Preservation copies in any format or medium; copyright exception, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Exception beneficiaries' right to the means to benefit from Arts 3-6 despite technological measures
rightholder: beneficiaries of the exceptions in Arts 3-6
description: Obtain the means needed to benefit from the TDM, teaching and preservation exceptions where technological measures would prevent it (Art. 6(4) InfoSoc applied).
exercise: Absent voluntary measures by rightholders.
quote: The first, third and fifth subparagraphs of Article 6(4) of Directive 2001/29/EC shall apply to Articles 3 to 6 of this Directive.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Means to bypass TPMs for TDM, teaching, preservation (technical), but via Member State measures, means unspecified, beneficiaries mostly institutions.

right: Rightholders' right to opt out of out-of-commerce works licensing and exception
addressee: collective management organisations; cultural heritage institutions
description: Exclude works at any time, easily and effectively, from extended collective licences or the exception for out-of-commerce works, generally or in specific cases, even after use has begun.
exercise: Information on the option on the EUIPO portal at least 6 months before use (Art. 10).
quote: Member States shall provide that all rightholders may, at any time, easily and effectively, exclude their works or other subject matter from the licensing mechanism set out in paragraph 1
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Opt-out from out-of-commerce licensing by notice; EUIPO portal only informs; no technical mechanism required. Test: yes.

right: Right to opt out of extended collective licensing
rightholder: rightholders who have not mandated the CMO
description: Exclude works at any time, easily and effectively, from an extended collective licensing mechanism.
quote: rightholders who have not authorised the organisation granting the licence may at any time easily and effectively exclude their works or other subject matter from the licensing mechanism
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies where the Member State introduces extended collective licensing (Member-State option).
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Opt-out from extended collective licensing by notice to CMO; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to use a negotiation mechanism for video-on-demand licensing
rightholder: parties seeking to conclude VoD licensing agreements (rightholders, VoD service providers)
addressee: impartial body or mediators designated by the Member State
description: Obtain assistance from an impartial body or mediators, including proposals, when facing difficulties licensing audiovisual works for VoD.
quote: may rely on the assistance of an impartial body or of mediators.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Assistance of impartial body or mediators for VoD licensing; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Press publishers' right for online uses
rightholder: publishers of press publications established in a Member State
description: Authorise or prohibit reproduction and making available of their press publications online by information society service providers.
exercise: Not for private/non-commercial use by individuals, hyperlinking, or individual words/very short extracts; expires 2 years after publication (Art. 15(4)).
quote: Member States shall provide publishers of press publications established in a Member State with the rights provided for in Article 2 and Article 3(2) of Directive 2001/29/EC
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Only press publications first published on or after 6 June 2019.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Press publishers' exclusive right for online uses; IP right on digital topic, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Authors' right to a share of press publishers' revenues
rightholder: authors of works incorporated in press publications
description: Receive an appropriate share of the revenues press publishers obtain from information society service providers.
quote: Member States shall provide that authors of works incorporated in a press publication receive an appropriate share of the revenues that press publishers receive
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Share of publishers' revenues; remuneration, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Publishers' claim to a share of compensation for uses under exceptions
rightholder: publishers to whom an author transferred or licensed a right
description: Be entitled to a share of compensation (e.g. private copying levies) for uses under exceptions to the transferred or licensed right.
quote: such a transfer or licence constitutes a sufficient legal basis for the publisher to be entitled to a share of the compensation
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Member-State option.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Publishers' share of compensation; remuneration, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Rightholders' authorisation right vis-à-vis online content-sharing service providers
rightholder: rightholders (authors and related rightholders under Art. 3 InfoSoc)
description: Require OCSSPs to obtain their authorisation (e.g. licence) to give the public access to works uploaded by users; licences also cover non-commercial users (Art. 17(2)).
exercise: Absent authorisation the OCSSP is liable unless it meets the best-efforts conditions of Art. 17(4).
quote: An online content-sharing service provider shall therefore obtain an authorisation from the rightholders referred to in Article 3(1) and (2) of Directive 2001/29/EC
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Authorisation (licence) right against content-sharing platforms; IP right, no technical mechanism for holder. Test: yes.

right: Rightholders' notice-and-takedown and staydown
description: Send a sufficiently substantiated notice to have works disabled or removed and future uploads prevented, and provide information so specific works are kept unavailable.
exercise: Requests must be duly justified (Art. 17(9)); lighter regime for new small OCSSPs (Art. 17(6)).
quote: acted expeditiously, upon receiving a sufficiently substantiated notice from the rightholders, to disable access to, or to remove from their websites, the notified works or other subject matter
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Substantiated notice to platform works by any means; filtering is platform technology, holder handles no technical output. Test: yes.

right: Users' right to rely on quotation and parody exceptions when uploading
description: Upload and share user-generated content relying on quotation, criticism, review, caricature, parody or pastiche; cooperation must not block non-infringing content.
exercise: Backed by complaint, out-of-court and judicial redress (Art. 17(9)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that users in each Member State are able to rely on any of the following existing exceptions or limitations when uploading and making available content generated by users
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Mandatory user right.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Right to upload via the platform's interface without non-infringing content being blocked by filters (software behaviour). Without the upload mechanism, no exercise. Test: no.

right: Rightholders' right to information from OCSSPs
description: Receive, on request, adequate information on how the OCSSP's practices under Art. 17(4) work and, where licensed, on the use of their content.
exercise: On request.
quote: Member States shall provide that online content-sharing service providers provide rightholders, at their request, with adequate information on the functioning of their practices
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Object is functioning of platform content-recognition practices (software behaviour), but plain request and plain answer suffice; holder is rightholder.

right: Users' right to a complaint and redress mechanism
description: Complain to the OCSSP about the disabling or removal of their uploaded content and have complaints processed without undue delay.
exercise: Rightholders must justify removal requests.
quote: online content-sharing service providers put in place an effective and expeditious complaint and redress mechanism that is available to users of their services
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Platform must provide complaint mechanism over removed uploads (digital object), but channel not specified as electronic and a plain complaint works. Conflict: test partly yes.

right: Users' right to human review of removal decisions
description: Have decisions to disable access to or remove uploaded content reviewed by a human.
exercise: Within the complaint mechanism.
quote: decisions to disable access to or remove uploaded content shall be subject to human review
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Object is an often automated removal decision (software behaviour), but human review is requested plainly and the outcome is a plain decision. Conflict: digital object versus test yes.

right: Users' access to out-of-court redress
description: Settle disputes over removed content impartially through out-of-court mechanisms, without losing legal protection.
quote: Member States shall also ensure that out-of-court redress mechanisms are available for the settlement of disputes.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Out-of-court redress body for disputes; ordinary dispute procedure, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Users' right of access to court to assert an exception
description: Go to a court or other judicial authority to assert the use of an exception or limitation.
quote: Member States shall ensure that users have access to a court or another relevant judicial authority to assert the use of an exception or limitation to copyright and related rights.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Access to court to assert an exception; judicial remedy, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Users' right to be informed of exceptions in terms and conditions
description: Be informed in the OCSSP's terms and conditions that they may use works under exceptions and limitations.
quote: Online content-sharing service providers shall inform their users in their terms and conditions that they can use works and other subject matter under exceptions or limitations
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Information on exceptions in online terms and conditions; plain-language information, no technical handling. Test: yes.

right: Right to appropriate and proportionate remuneration
addressee: party to whom rights are licensed or transferred
description: Receive appropriate and proportionate remuneration when licensing or transferring exclusive exploitation rights.
exercise: Mechanisms set by Member States (Art. 18(2)); not for computer-program authors (Art. 23(2)).
quote: they are entitled to receive appropriate and proportionate remuneration.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Appropriate remuneration from licensees; remuneration/contract right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to regular information on exploitation and revenues
addressee: licensees/transferees or their successors in title
description: Receive at least annually up-to-date, relevant and comprehensive information on the exploitation of their works, revenues generated and remuneration due.
exercise: Proportionality limits (Art. 19(3)-(4)); collective agreements may apply (Art. 19(5)); not for CMOs (Art. 19(6)); contrary contract terms unenforceable (Art. 23(1)).
quote: authors and performers receive on a regular basis, at least once a year, and taking into account the specificities of each sector, up to date, relevant and comprehensive information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies to licence/transfer agreements from 7 June 2022 (Art. 27).
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Annual information on exploitation and revenues; plain reporting, no technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to additional information from sub-licensees
rightholder: authors and performers or their representatives
addressee: sub-licensees; first contractual counterpart (identity of sub-licensees)
description: On request, obtain additional information from sub-licensees where the first counterpart lacks it, and learn the sub-licensees' identity.
exercise: Request directly or via the contractual counterpart, as Member States provide.
quote: authors and performers or their representatives shall, at their request, receive from sub-licensees additional information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Applies from 7 June 2022 (Art. 27).
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Additional information from sub-licensees on request; plain information, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Contract adjustment mechanism (bestseller clause)
rightholder: authors and performers or their representatives
addressee: contractual counterpart or its successors in title
description: Claim additional, appropriate and fair remuneration where the agreed remuneration is disproportionately low compared to subsequent revenues.
exercise: Absent comparable collective-bargaining mechanism; not against CMOs (Art. 20(2)); ADR available (Art. 21); contrary contract terms unenforceable (Art. 23(1)).
quote: authors and performers or their representatives are entitled to claim additional, appropriate and fair remuneration from the party with whom they entered into a contract
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Contract adjustment claim for additional remuneration; contract right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to alternative dispute resolution on transparency and contract adjustment
rightholder: authors and performers (and their representative organisations at their request)
description: Submit disputes on transparency (Art. 19) or contract adjustment (Art. 20) to a voluntary ADR procedure, which representative organisations may start at an author's request.
quote: disputes concerning the transparency obligation under Article 19 and the contract adjustment mechanism under Article 20 may be submitted to a voluntary, alternative dispute resolution procedure.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Voluntary ADR on transparency and contract adjustment; procedural, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right of revocation for lack of exploitation
rightholder: authors and performers who licensed/transferred rights exclusively
description: Revoke in whole or part an exclusive licence or transfer, or end its exclusivity, where the work is not exploited.
exercise: After a reasonable time; notify the counterpart and set a deadline for exploitation (Art. 22(3)); excluded if lack of exploitation is remediable by the author (Art. 22(4)); derogation only via collective agreements (Art. 22(5)).
quote: the author or performer may revoke in whole or in part the licence or the transfer of rights where there is a lack of exploitation of that work or other protected subject matter.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
table_entry: Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive
tl_reason: Revocation of licence for non-exploitation by notice; contract right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to have funds safeguarded and ring-fenced from the institution's creditors
description: Funds that users hand to a payment or e-money institution must be kept segregated (or covered by insurance or a guarantee) and insulated from the claims of the institution's other creditors, in particular on insolvency.
exercise: Relied on in insolvency of the institution under national law.
quote: they shall be insulated in accordance with national law in the interest of the payment service users against the claims of other creditors of the payment institution or electronic money institution
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Safeguarding of user funds in insolvency; nothing to exercise or operate.

right: Right to a timely, reasoned decision on an authorisation application
rightholder: applicant for authorisation as a payment institution
description: An applicant must be told within 3 months whether authorisation is granted, and must be given reasons if it is refused.
exercise: 3 months from receipt of the (complete) application.
quote: the competent authorities shall inform the applicant whether the authorisation is granted or refused. The competent authority shall give reasons where it refuses an authorisation.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Reasoned decision on an authorisation application; administrative procedure, no technical element.

right: Right to reasons for withdrawal of authorisation
description: Withdrawal of a payment institution's authorisation must be reasoned and communicated to those concerned.
exercise: Withdrawal only on the grounds listed in Art. 13(1).
quote: The competent authority shall give reasons for any withdrawal of an authorisation and shall inform those concerned accordingly.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Reasons for withdrawal of authorisation; administrative procedure, no technical element.

right: Right to contest competent authority decisions before the courts
description: Decisions of competent authorities concerning a payment institution, and failures to act, can be challenged in court.
exercise: Under national procedural law; also covers failure to act (Art. 25(2)).
quote: in respect of a payment institution pursuant to the laws, regulations and administrative provisions adopted in accordance with this Directive may be contested before the courts
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Judicial review of supervisory decisions; no technical element.

right: Right to justified and communicated supervisory measures
description: Supervisory measures involving penalties or restrictions on passporting must be properly justified and communicated to the institution.
quote: shall be properly justified and communicated to the payment institution concerned
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Supervisory measures must be justified and communicated; administrative procedure, no technical element.

right: Right of payment service providers to objective, non-discriminatory access to payment systems
rightholder: authorised or registered payment service providers that are legal persons
description: Access rules of payment systems must be objective, non-discriminatory and proportionate; restrictive or discriminatory participation rules are prohibited.
exercise: Does not apply to intra-group systems (Art. 35(2)).
quote: the rules on access of authorised or registered payment service providers that are legal persons to payment systems are objective, non-discriminatory and proportionate
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Non-discriminatory access rules to payment systems; market access for providers, no mechanism the governed party operates.

right: Right to request indirect participation in a designated payment system on equal terms
rightholder: authorised or registered payment service provider
addressee: participant in a payment system designated under Directive 98/26/EC
description: Where a participant lets one non-participant PSP pass transfer orders through the system, it must offer the same opportunity to other PSPs on request, and give full reasons for any rejection.
exercise: Request to the participant; full reasons for rejection.
quote: that participant shall, when requested, give the same opportunity in an objective, proportionate and non-discriminatory manner to other authorised or registered payment service providers
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Indirect participation in a payment system on request; market access for providers, no technical element for users.

right: Right of payment institutions to access credit institutions' payment account services
description: Payment institutions must get access to banks' payment account services on an objective, non-discriminatory and proportionate basis, sufficient to provide their services.
exercise: Credit institution must give the competent authority duly motivated reasons for any rejection.
quote: Member States shall ensure that payment institutions have access to credit institutions’ payment accounts services on an objective, non-discriminatory and proportionate basis.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Access of payment institutions to bank account services; market access, no technical element.

right: Right to receive required information free of charge
description: Providers may not charge for providing the information required by Title III.
exercise: Charges only for additional or more frequent information, or other means of transmission, requested by the user; must be reasonable and cost-based (Art. 40(2)-(3)).
quote: The payment service provider shall not charge the payment service user for providing information under this Title.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Ban on charging for required information; price rule, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information for single payment transactions
description: Before being bound by a single payment contract, the user must have the Art. 45 information (identifier needed, maximum execution time, all charges, exchange rate), in clear language, on paper or durable medium on request.
exercise: Before contract; immediately after execution if concluded at a distance (Art. 44(2)).
quote: At the payment service user’s request, the payment service provider shall provide the information and conditions on paper or on another durable medium.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Pre-contractual information on paper or durable medium; electronic delivery optional, content plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to identification and contact details of a payment initiation service provider before initiation
description: Before initiating a payment, a PISP must give the payer its name, head office and agent/branch address, contact details and the contact details of the competent authority.
exercise: Prior to initiation.
quote: payment initiation service providers shall, prior to initiation, provide the payer with, or make available to the payer, the following clear and comprehensive information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Provider identity and contact details before initiation, usually on screen; plain information that could be given otherwise. Test: yes.

right: Right to confirmation and transaction details after initiation via a payment initiation service
description: Immediately after initiation the PISP must confirm successful initiation and provide a reference, the amount and any PISP charges.
exercise: Immediately after initiation.
quote: the payment initiation service provider shall, immediately after initiation, provide or make available all of the following data to the payer and, where applicable, the payee
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Confirmation, reference and charges after initiation; plain data delivered electronically, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to information after receipt of a payment order (single payment)
description: The payer must receive a reference, the amount, charges, exchange rate used and date of receipt immediately after the order is received.
exercise: Immediately after receipt of the payment order.
quote: Immediately after receipt of the payment order, the payer’s payment service provider shall provide the payer with or make available to the payer
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Transaction information after receipt of the order, provided or made available; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right of the payee to information after execution (single payment)
description: The payee must receive a reference, the amount, charges, exchange rate and credit value date immediately after execution.
exercise: Immediately after execution.
quote: Immediately after the execution of the payment transaction, the payee’s payment service provider shall provide the payee with, or make available to, the payee
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Payee transaction information after execution, provided or made available; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information before a framework contract
description: In good time before signing a framework contract (e.g. account or card contract), the user must receive on paper or durable medium the Art. 52 information on the provider, the service, charges, communication, safeguards, liability, refunds, changes, termination and redress.
exercise: In good time before being bound; immediately after conclusion if concluded at a distance (Art. 51(2)).
quote: the payment service provider provide the payment service user on paper or on another durable medium with the information and conditions specified in Article 52
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Framework-contract information on paper or durable medium; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to receive the framework contract terms on request at any time
description: During the contract the user can ask for the contract terms and Art. 52 information on paper or durable medium.
exercise: On request, at any time during the contractual relationship.
quote: At any time during the contractual relationship the payment service user shall have a right to receive, on request, the contractual terms of the framework contract
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Contract terms on request on paper or durable medium; plain request and result. Test: yes.

right: Right to advance notice of changes to the framework contract and to accept or reject them
description: Proposed changes to the contract or conditions must be notified at least 2 months before they apply, and the user can accept or reject them.
exercise: Notice on paper or durable medium at least 2 months ahead; deemed acceptance only if agreed and the user does not object.
quote: The payment service user can either accept or reject the changes before the date of their proposed date of entry into force.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Change notice on paper or durable medium; acceptance or rejection by plain statement. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate free of charge when rejecting proposed contract changes
description: A user who rejects the proposed changes may terminate the framework contract free of charge with effect at any time before the changes would apply.
exercise: Before the date the changes would have applied.
quote: the payment service user has the right to terminate the framework contract free of charge and with effect at any time until the date when the changes would have applied
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Free termination when rejecting changes; contract right, no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to terminate the framework contract at any time
description: The user may terminate a framework contract at any time, with at most 1 month's agreed notice; termination is free of charge once the contract has run for 6 months.
exercise: Notice of at most 1 month; any charge in the first 6 months must be appropriate and cost-based (Art. 55(2)).
quote: The payment service user may terminate the framework contract at any time, unless the parties have agreed on a period of notice. Such a period shall not exceed 1 month.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Member States may provide more favourable provisions (Art. 55(6)). Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Termination of the framework contract at any time; contract right, notice by any means. Test: yes.

right: Right to at least 2 months' notice of termination by the provider
description: The provider can terminate an open-ended framework contract only if the contract allows it and with at least 2 months' notice.
exercise: Notice on paper or durable medium.
quote: the payment service provider may terminate a framework contract concluded for an indefinite period by giving at least 2 months’ notice
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Minimum notice period for termination by the provider; contract protection, nothing to operate.

right: Right to pay regular charges only pro rata and to a refund of prepaid charges on termination
description: Regular charges are payable only proportionally up to termination; charges paid in advance must be reimbursed proportionally.
exercise: On termination.
quote: If such charges are paid in advance, they shall be reimbursed proportionally.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Pro-rata charges and refund of prepaid charges on termination; monetary contract right.

right: Right to information on execution time and charges before an individual payment, on request
description: Before a payment under a framework contract, the payer can ask for the maximum execution time and the charges, with a breakdown.
exercise: On request for the specific transaction.
quote: a payment service provider shall, at the payer’s request for this specific payment transaction, provide explicit information on all of the following
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Execution time and charges on request; plain request and answer, often via online banking. Test: yes.

right: Right of the payer to information on each individual payment transaction
description: After each debit the payer must receive the reference, amount, charges or interest, exchange rate and debit value date.
exercise: Without undue delay after debit.
quote: the payer’s payment service provider shall provide the payer, without undue delay and in the same way as laid down in Article 51(1), with all of the following information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Post-debit transaction information on paper or durable medium; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to a free monthly statement on request
description: The framework contract must let the payer require the transaction information at least monthly, free of charge, in a storable form.
exercise: On request; Member States may require monthly paper statements (Art. 57(3)).
quote: the payer may require the information referred to in paragraph 1 to be provided or made available periodically, at least once a month, free of charge
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Monthly statement in storable form, paper or electronic; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right of the payee to information on each individual payment transaction
description: After execution the payee must receive a reference identifying the transaction and payer, the amount credited, charges, exchange rate and credit value date.
exercise: Without undue delay after execution.
quote: the payee’s payment service provider shall provide the payee without undue delay in the same way as laid down in Article 51(1) with all of the following information
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Payee transaction information on paper or durable medium; plain content. Test: yes.

right: Right to disclosure of charges and exchange rate before currency conversion at ATM or point of sale
addressee: party offering the currency conversion service (ATM operator, merchant/payee)
description: Where currency conversion is offered at an ATM, at the point of sale or by the payee, all charges and the exchange rate must be disclosed first, and the payer agrees on that basis.
exercise: Before initiation of the transaction.
quote: the party offering the currency conversion service to the payer shall disclose to the payer all charges as well as the exchange rate to be used for converting the payment transaction
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Charges and exchange rate shown on ATM or terminal before conversion; plain disclosure, agreement needs no technical skill. Test: yes.

right: Right to be told of surcharges or reductions before paying, and to pay only disclosed charges
addressee: payee; payment service provider; other party involved
description: Any charge or reduction for using a payment instrument must be disclosed before initiation, and the payer only has to pay charges whose full amount was made known in advance.
exercise: Prior to initiation of the payment.
quote: The payer shall only be obliged to pay for the charges referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 if their full amount was made known prior to the initiation of the payment transaction.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out of Title III (Art. 38(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Disclosure of surcharges and liability only for disclosed charges; price rule, no mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Right not to be charged for information and corrective or preventive measures
description: Providers may not charge for meeting their Title IV information obligations or for corrective and preventive measures, except the specified cases (refusal, revocation, recovery), where charges must be agreed and cost-based.
quote: The payment service provider shall not charge the payment service user for fulfilment of its information obligations or corrective and preventive measures under this Title
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Ban on charging for information and corrective measures; price rule.

right: Payee's freedom to surcharge, offer reductions or steer payers to a payment instrument
description: A merchant's provider may not stop it from charging, offering a discount or steering customers towards a particular payment instrument, subject to limits.
exercise: Surcharges capped at direct costs; banned for regulated cards and SEPA payments (Art. 62(4)); Member States may prohibit or limit (Art. 62(5)).
quote: The payment service provider shall not prevent the payee from requesting from the payer a charge, offering him a reduction or otherwise steering him towards the use of a given payment instrument.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Merchant freedom to surcharge, discount or steer; commercial freedom, no technical element.

right: Right not to be surcharged for regulated card payments and SEPA credit transfers or direct debits
description: Payees may not surcharge payments made with cards whose interchange fees are regulated (e.g. consumer debit/credit cards) or with euro credit transfers and direct debits under the SEPA Regulation.
quote: the payee shall not request charges for the use of payment instruments for which interchange fees are regulated under Chapter II of Regulation (EU) 2015/751
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Surcharge ban for regulated cards and SEPA payments; price rule.

right: Right to withdraw consent to a payment transaction or series of transactions
description: The payer can withdraw consent at any time up to irrevocability; withdrawing consent to a series makes future transactions unauthorised.
exercise: No later than the moment of irrevocability (Art. 80).
quote: Consent may be withdrawn by the payer at any time, but no later than at the moment of irrevocability in accordance with Article 80.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Withdrawal of payment consent via online banking or plain notice; object is a payment, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to control funds-availability confirmations to card issuers through explicit consent
description: A bank may confirm to a third-party card issuer that funds are available only if the payer gave explicit prior consent; the answer is a simple yes/no and funds may not be blocked.
exercise: Consent before the first confirmation request (Art. 65(1)(c)).
quote: the payer has given explicit consent to the account servicing payment service provider to respond to requests from a specific payment service provider
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Consent governs automated funds-confirmation requests between providers (digital object), but consent can be given plainly and nothing returns. Mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right to know which provider requested a funds confirmation and the answer given
description: The payer can ask the bank to identify the card-issuing provider that requested confirmation and the answer it gave.
exercise: On request.
quote: The payer may request the account servicing payment service provider to communicate to the payer the identification of the payment service provider and the answer provided.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Object is a record of automated confirmation requests, but a plain request works and the answer is plain. Test conflicts with digital object.

right: Right to use a payment initiation service
description: Payers may use a third-party payment initiation service for online-accessible accounts; the bank must treat such orders without discrimination as to timing, priority or charges.
exercise: Only for payment accounts accessible online; requires the payer's explicit consent (Art. 66(2)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that a payer has the right to make use of a payment initiation service provider to obtain payment services as referred to in point (7) of Annex I.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Use of third-party payment initiation software on online accounts; bank must permit interface access. Without the interface the right cannot exist. Test: no.

right: Right of payment initiation service providers to access payer accounts without a contract and without discrimination
description: PISPs can initiate payments from payers' online accounts without a contract with the bank; the bank must communicate securely, provide initiation and execution information and not discriminate (Art. 66(4)); PISPs may rely on the bank's authentication procedures (Art. 97(5)).
exercise: Bank may deny access only for objectively justified, evidenced fraud-related reasons (Art. 68(5)).
quote: shall not be dependent on the existence of a contractual relationship between the payment initiation service providers and the account servicing payment service providers
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Interface access to online accounts is purely technical, but the holder is a provider, not the governed party. Holder criterion conflicts.

right: Right to use an account information service
description: Users may have a third-party account information service access their online payment accounts; the AISP may only access designated accounts and use the data for the service requested.
exercise: Only for payment accounts accessible online; AISP acts only on the user's explicit consent (Art. 67(2)).
quote: Member States shall ensure that a payment service user has the right to make use of services enabling access to account information as referred to in point (8) of Annex I.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Use of third-party account information software over the bank's interface; possible only technically. Test: no.

right: Right of account information service providers to access account data without a contract and without discrimination
description: AISPs can access account information without a contract with the bank; the bank must communicate securely and treat their data requests without discrimination (Art. 67(3)).
exercise: Bank may deny access only for objectively justified, evidenced fraud-related reasons (Art. 68(5)).
quote: shall not be dependent on the existence of a contractual relationship between the account information service providers and the account servicing payment service providers
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Technical access to account data through the bank's interface, but the holder is a provider, not the governed party. Holder criterion conflicts.

right: Right to be informed of the blocking of a payment instrument and the reasons
description: If the provider blocks a card or other instrument, it must tell the payer and give reasons, where possible in advance and at the latest immediately afterwards.
exercise: Unless disclosure would compromise objectively justified security reasons or is prohibited by law.
quote: the payment service provider shall inform the payer of the blocking of the payment instrument and the reasons for it in an agreed manner
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Notice of blocking and reasons in an agreed manner; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to unblocking or replacement of a blocked payment instrument
description: Once the reasons for blocking cease, the provider must unblock the instrument or replace it.
exercise: User may request unblocking through means available at all times (Art. 70(1)(c)).
quote: The payment service provider shall unblock the payment instrument or replace it with a new payment instrument once the reasons for blocking no longer exist.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Unblocking or replacement requested via provider channels, including phone; result needs no technical skill. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed when the bank denies a third-party provider access to the account
description: If the bank denies an AISP or PISP access to the payer's account for fraud-related reasons, it must inform the payer and give reasons; access must be restored once the reasons cease.
exercise: Where possible before denial, at the latest immediately thereafter.
quote: the account servicing payment service provider shall inform the payer that access to the payment account is denied and the reasons therefor in the form agreed
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Reasons for denying the user's chosen third-party software access (digital object), but the notice is plain language. Test conflicts with digital object.

right: Right to report loss, theft or misuse at any time, free of charge, and to obtain proof of the report
addressee: payment service provider issuing the instrument
description: Issuers must provide means to notify loss, theft or misuse (or request unblocking) at all times, free of charge, and on request give proof of the notification for 18 months; they must then prevent further use.
exercise: Notification free of charge, only replacement costs may be charged (Art. 70(1)(d)); further use prevented (Art. 70(1)(e)).
quote: on request, the payment service provider shall provide the payment service user with the means to prove, for 18 months after notification, that the payment service user made such a notification
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Loss notification by any means at all times, phone included; proof on request. Technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Protection from the risk of sending payment instruments and security credentials
addressee: payment service provider issuing the instrument
description: The issuer bears the risk if a card or credentials are intercepted or misused while being sent to the user.
quote: The payment service provider shall bear the risk of sending a payment instrument or any personalised security credentials relating to it to the payment service user.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Risk allocation for sending cards and credentials; liability rule.

right: Right to rectification of unauthorised or incorrectly executed payment transactions
addressee: payment service provider (account servicing PSP where a PISP is involved)
description: A user who notifies the provider of an unauthorised or incorrectly executed transaction in time is entitled to have it rectified.
exercise: Notify without undue delay and at the latest 13 months after the debit date; the time limit does not apply if the provider failed to give the Title III information; with PIS, claim from the bank (Art. 71(2)).
quote: The payment service user shall obtain rectification of an unauthorised or incorrectly executed payment transaction from the payment service provider only if the payment service user notifies
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may agree different time limits (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Rectification after timely notification; contract remedy, notification by any means. Test: yes.

right: Burden of proof on the provider when a user disputes a transaction
addressee: payment service provider (incl. payment initiation service provider)
description: If the user denies authorising a transaction or claims faulty execution, the provider must prove authentication, correct recording and absence of technical failure; use of the instrument alone does not prove authorisation, fraud or gross negligence.
quote: it is for the payment service provider to prove that the payment transaction was authenticated, accurately recorded, entered in the accounts and not affected by a technical breakdown
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Burden-of-proof rule in payment disputes; procedural, holder operates nothing.

right: Right to an immediate refund of unauthorised payment transactions
addressee: payer's payment service provider (account servicing PSP where PIS used)
description: The provider must refund an unauthorised transaction and restore the account, with the original value date, by the end of the next business day after noting or being notified of it.
exercise: Exception only if the provider has reasonable grounds to suspect fraud and reports them in writing to the national authority; for PIS-initiated transactions the bank refunds (Art. 73(2)).
quote: the payer’s payment service provider refunds the payer the amount of the unauthorised payment transaction immediately, and in any event no later than by the end of the following business day
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Subject to timely notification (Art. 71).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Refund of unauthorised transactions; monetary remedy.

right: Liability cap of EUR 50 for lost, stolen or misappropriated payment instruments
description: The payer bears at most EUR 50 of losses from unauthorised use of a lost, stolen or misappropriated instrument, and nothing if the loss was undetectable or caused by the provider's staff or agents; unlimited only for fraud or intentional/grossly negligent breach.
quote: the payer may be obliged to bear the losses relating to any unauthorised payment transactions, up to a maximum of EUR 50
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Member States may reduce liability further. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: EUR 50 liability cap; monetary rule.

right: No liability where the provider does not require strong customer authentication
description: If the payer's provider did not require strong customer authentication, the payer bears no loss unless it acted fraudulently.
quote: Where the payer’s payment service provider does not require strong customer authentication, the payer shall not bear any financial losses unless the payer has acted fraudulently.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: No liability where strong authentication was not required; liability rule, holder operates nothing.

right: No liability for use after notification or where no notification means were provided
description: The payer bears no loss from use of a lost or stolen instrument after notifying it, or if the provider did not offer means to notify at all times, unless the payer acted fraudulently.
quote: The payer shall not bear any financial consequences resulting from use of the lost, stolen or misappropriated payment instrument after notification
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: No liability after notification; liability rule.

right: Right to have card funds blocked only with consent to the exact amount and released promptly
description: For card payments of unknown final amount (e.g. hotels, fuel), funds may only be blocked if the payer consented to the exact amount, and must be released without undue delay once the amount is known.
exercise: Release at the latest immediately after receipt of the payment order (Art. 75(2)).
quote: the payer’s payment service provider may block funds on the payer’s payment account only if the payer has given consent to the exact amount of the funds to be blocked
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Consent to the exact blocked amount, given at terminal or checkout; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to a refund of authorised payee-initiated transactions that exceed reasonable expectations
description: The payer can get a full refund of an executed payee-initiated payment (e.g. card pre-authorisation, direct debit) if the exact amount was not specified and it exceeded what the payer could reasonably expect.
exercise: Request within 8 weeks of debit (Art. 77(1)); provider must refund or justify refusal and indicate complaint/ADR bodies within 10 business days (Art. 77(2)); may be excluded where consent was given directly to the PSP and information was given 4 weeks ahead (Art. 76(3)).
quote: a payer is entitled to a refund from the payment service provider of an authorised payment transaction which was initiated by or through a payee and which has already been executed
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Payer bears burden of proving the conditions on request. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Refund of payee-initiated transactions on request; monetary remedy.

right: Unconditional right to a refund of SEPA direct debits
description: For euro direct debits under the SEPA Regulation, the payer is entitled to a refund without conditions.
exercise: Within 8 weeks from the debit date; the provider may not refuse (Art. 77).
quote: the payer has an unconditional right to a refund within the time limits laid down in Article 77 of this Directive
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Unconditional direct-debit refund; monetary remedy.

right: Right to be notified of the refusal of a payment order, with reasons and how to correct errors
description: If the provider refuses to execute or initiate a payment it must notify the refusal, if possible the reasons, and the procedure for correcting factual mistakes.
exercise: At the earliest opportunity and within the execution periods (Art. 83); a reasonable fee may be agreed only for objectively justified refusals.
quote: the refusal and, if possible, the reasons for it and the procedure for correcting any factual mistakes that led to the refusal shall be notified to the payment service user
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Notice of refusal with reasons and correction procedure; plain information via agreed channel. Test: yes.

right: Right to execution of authorised payment orders meeting the contract conditions
addressee: payer's account servicing payment service provider
description: Where all framework contract conditions are met, the bank may not refuse an authorised payment order, however initiated (directly, via PISP or by the payee).
exercise: Unless prohibited by other Union or national law.
quote: the payer’s account servicing payment service provider shall not refuse to execute an authorised payment order
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Bank may not refuse authorised orders; service obligation, nothing technical for the holder.

right: Right to revoke a direct debit until the end of the business day before debiting
description: For a direct debit, the payer can revoke the payment order up to the end of the business day before the agreed debit day, without prejudice to refund rights.
exercise: By end of the business day preceding the agreed debit day.
quote: in the case of a direct debit and without prejudice to refund rights the payer may revoke the payment order at the latest by the end of the business day preceding the day agreed for debiting the funds
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Revocation of a direct debit online or by plain notice; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to revoke a future-dated payment order
description: Where execution was agreed for a specific future day, the user can revoke the order up to the end of the preceding business day.
exercise: By end of the business day preceding the agreed day.
quote: the payment service user may revoke a payment order at the latest by the end of the business day preceding the agreed day
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Revocation of a future-dated order online or by plain notice; technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to have the full amount transferred without deductions
addressee: payer's and payee's payment service providers and intermediaries
description: Providers and intermediaries must transfer the full amount without deducting charges; if other charges are deducted, the relevant provider must ensure the payee receives the full amount.
exercise: Payee may agree that its own provider deducts its charges, shown separately (Art. 81(2)).
quote: to transfer the full amount of the payment transaction and refrain from deducting charges from the amount transferred
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Full amount transferred without deductions; monetary rule.

right: Right to execution within one business day
description: For payments in scope (euro and national currency), the amount must reach the payee's provider by the end of the next business day after receipt of the order (one more day for paper orders).
exercise: Applies to transactions within Art. 82; longer periods for other transactions max. 4 business days if agreed.
quote: the amount of the payment transaction will be credited to the payee’s payment service provider’s account by the end of the following business day
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Execution time limit; service standard, holder operates nothing.

right: Right of consumers to immediate availability of cash placed on their payment account
description: Cash a consumer pays into their account in the account currency must be made available and value dated immediately; for non-consumers at the latest the next business day.
quote: the payment service provider shall ensure that the amount is made available and value dated immediately after receipt of the funds
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Immediate availability of deposited cash; monetary rule.

right: Right to correct value dating and immediate availability of received funds
addressee: payee's and payer's payment service providers
description: Funds must be value dated no later than the day the payee's provider is credited and be at the payee's disposal immediately; the payer's account may not be debit value dated before the actual debit.
exercise: Not at the parties' disposal even for non-covered transactions (Art. 82(2)).
quote: the amount of the payment transaction is at the payee’s disposal immediately after that amount is credited to the payee’s payment service provider’s account
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Value dating and availability of funds; monetary rule.

right: Right to recovery assistance and information where an incorrect unique identifier was used
addressee: payer's payment service provider (with cooperation of payee's PSP)
description: If a payment went to the wrong account because of an incorrect IBAN, the provider must make reasonable efforts to recover the funds and, if that fails, give the payer on written request all information needed to sue for recovery.
exercise: Written request; a recovery charge may apply if agreed (Art. 88(4)).
quote: the payer’s payment service provider shall provide to the payer, upon written request, all information available to the payer’s payment service provider and relevant to the payer
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Recovery efforts and information on written request for a legal claim; no technical element. Test: yes.

right: Right to a refund for non-executed or defective payer-initiated transactions
description: The payer's provider is liable for correct execution and must refund the amount of a non-executed or defective transaction and restore the account, unless it proves the payee's provider received the funds (then the payee's provider must credit the payee immediately).
exercise: Without undue delay; value date no later than the debit date; subject to Art. 71 notification.
quote: it shall, without undue delay, refund to the payer the amount of the non-executed or defective payment transaction
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Refund for non-executed or defective transactions; monetary remedy.

right: Right to have a non-executed or defective transaction traced free of charge
description: Regardless of liability, the provider must on request try immediately to trace a failed or defective transaction and report the outcome, free of charge.
exercise: On request.
quote: on request, make immediate efforts to trace the payment transaction and notify the payer of the outcome. This shall be free of charge for the payer.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Tracing on request with outcome notified; plain request and answer. Test: yes.

right: Payee's right to correct transmission and handling of payee-initiated transactions
description: The payee's provider is liable to the payee for correctly transmitting payee-initiated orders (e.g. direct debits) and for making funds available with correct value date; otherwise the payer's provider is liable to the payer.
exercise: Immediate re-transmission; correct value dating.
quote: be liable to the payee for correct transmission of the payment order to the payment service provider of the payer in accordance with Article 83(3)
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Payee's provider liable for transmitting payee-initiated orders; liability rule.

right: Right to compensation for charges and interest caused by non-execution or defective execution
description: Providers are liable to their users for charges they are responsible for and for interest the user incurs because of non-execution or defective or late execution.
quote: payment service providers shall be liable to their respective payment service users for any charges for which they are responsible, and for any interest to which the payment service user is subject
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Compensation for charges and interest; monetary remedy.

right: Right to a refund from the bank for failed payments initiated through a payment initiation service
description: If a PIS-initiated payment is not executed or is defective, the payer's bank must refund the amount and restore the account; the PISP must compensate the bank if it is at fault.
exercise: Subject to Art. 71 notification.
quote: refund to the payer the amount of the non- executed or defective payment transaction
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Non-consumers may contract out (Art. 61(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Refund by the bank for failed PIS payments; monetary remedy.

right: Right of recourse against the provider or intermediary responsible
addressee: other payment service provider or intermediary
description: A provider that has paid under Arts 73, 89 or 90 can recover losses from the provider or intermediary to which the liability is attributable, including for failure to use strong customer authentication; PISPs must compensate banks on request (Arts 73(2), 90(2)).
quote: that payment service provider or intermediary shall compensate the first payment service provider for any losses incurred or sums paid under Articles 73, 89 and 90
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Recourse between providers; liability rule.

right: Right that providers process personal data only with explicit consent
description: Providers may only access, process and retain personal data necessary for their payment services with the user's explicit consent.
quote: Payment service providers shall only access, process and retain personal data necessary for the provision of their payment services, with the explicit consent of the payment service user.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Personal data processing otherwise governed by data protection law (Art. 94(1)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Explicit consent to personal-data processing (digital object), but consent can be given or refused plainly; no mandated interface. Test conflicts.

right: Right to be informed of major security incidents affecting one's financial interests
description: Where a major operational or security incident may affect users' financial interests, the provider must inform them without undue delay of the incident and of mitigation measures they can take.
exercise: Without undue delay.
quote: the payment service provider shall, without undue delay, inform its payment service users of the incident and of all measures that they can take to mitigate the adverse effects of the incident
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Disapplied by the DORA amendment (Art. 96(7)) for credit, payment and e-money institutions and AISPs, whose client information duty is now in DORA.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Notice of incidents and mitigation measures; plain information, channel incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to complain to the competent authority
rightholder: payment service users and other interested parties, including consumer associations
description: Users and interested parties can complain to the competent authorities about alleged infringements of national law implementing PSD2.
