exercise: Authority's reply informs of available ADR procedures (Art. 99(2)); without prejudice to court proceedings.
quote: procedures are set up which allow payment service users and other interested parties including consumer associations, to submit complaints to the competent authorities
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Complaint to the competent authority by ordinary means.

right: Right to have complaints answered by the provider within 15 business days
description: Providers must run complaint procedures for disputes on PSD2 rights and reply on paper or durable medium, addressing all points, within 15 business days.
exercise: Holding reply in exceptional cases; final reply within 35 business days; in an official language of the Member State (Art. 101(1)).
quote: Such a reply shall address all points raised, within an adequate timeframe and at the latest within 15 business days of receipt of the complaint.
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Internal complaint answered on paper or durable medium; plain request and reply. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed about a competent ADR entity
description: The provider must tell users of at least one competent ADR entity, on its website, at branches and in the general terms and conditions.
exercise: Information must explain how to access the ADR entity (Art. 101(4)).
quote: shall inform the payment service user about at least one ADR entity which is competent to deal with disputes concerning the rights and obligations arising under Titles III and IV
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law.
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: ADR information on website, at branches and in terms; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to out-of-court dispute resolution (ADR)
addressee: Member State / ADR entities; payment service providers must participate
description: Independent, impartial ADR procedures must be available for disputes between users and providers on PSD2 rights and obligations, and apply to providers; ADR bodies cooperate on cross-border disputes.
exercise: Under Directive 2013/11/EU-compliant procedures.
quote: adequate, independent, impartial, transparent and effective ADR procedures for the settlement of disputes between payment service users and payment service providers
notes: Directive: exercised via national transposition law. Member States may exclude non-consumers (Art. 61(2)).
entry_current_status: PSD2 in force; PSD3 2023/0209(COD): provisional agreement Nov 2025, formal adoption pending (OEIL: awaiting Council first-reading position)
tl_reason: Out-of-court dispute resolution; no technical element.

right: Right to direct access to product and related service data by design
rightholder: user of a connected product or related service
addressee: manufacturer of the connected product / provider of the related service
description: Connected products and related services must be designed so that product and related service data and metadata are, by default, easily, securely and freely accessible to the user, directly where feasible.
quote: are, by default, easily, securely, free of charge, in a comprehensive, structured, commonly used and machine-readable format, and, where relevant and technically feasible, directly accessible
notes: Applies to connected products and related services placed on the market after 12 September 2026 (Art. 50). Micro/small enterprises exempt (Art. 7(1)).
tl_reason: Product must be designed so data are directly accessible in machine-readable form; access only through product interfaces. Test: no.

right: Right to pre-contractual information on data generated by a connected product
addressee: seller, rentor or lessor (may be the manufacturer)
description: Before buying, renting or leasing a connected product, receive information on the type, format and volume of data generated, real-time capability, storage and how to access, retrieve or erase the data.
exercise: Before conclusion of the contract, in a clear and comprehensible manner.
quote: Before concluding a contract for the purchase, rent or lease of a connected product, the seller, rentor or lessor, which may be the manufacturer, shall provide at least the following information
tl_reason: Pre-contractual information in clear language about product data; plain, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information on data of a related service
rightholder: user (prospective recipient of a related service)
description: Before contracting for a related service, receive information on the data to be obtained, the data holder's identity and intended uses, how to request sharing with third parties, the right to complain, trade secrets and contract termination.
exercise: Before conclusion of the contract.
quote: Before concluding a contract for the provision of a related service, the provider of such related service shall provide at least the following information to the user
tl_reason: Pre-contractual information about related-service data; plain, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to readily available product and related service data
description: Where data are not directly accessible, obtain readily available data and metadata from the data holder without undue delay, free of charge, in machine-readable format and, where feasible, continuously and in real time.
exercise: Simple electronic request; no more verification information than necessary (Art. 4(5)); choices may not be made unduly difficult (Art. 4(4)); personal data of others only with a GDPR legal basis (Art. 4(12)).
quote: data holders shall make readily available data, as well as the relevant metadata necessary to interpret and use those data, accessible to the user without undue delay
notes: Limits: security restrictions (Art. 4(2)), trade secret safeguards (Art. 4(6)-(8)); no use to develop competing product (Art. 4(10)). Micro/small enterprises exempt (Art. 7(1)).
tl_reason: Readily available data delivered in machine-readable format, possibly in real time; result is data to interpret. Test: no.

right: Right to challenge security-based contractual restrictions on data access
addressee: competent authority / certified dispute settlement body
description: In a dispute over contractual restrictions on data access justified by security, complain to the competent authority or agree with the data holder to use a dispute settlement body, without prejudice to court action.
exercise: Complaint under Art. 37(5)(b) or dispute settlement under Art. 10(1); court redress available at any stage.
quote: the user may, in relation to any dispute with the data holder concerning the contractual restrictions or prohibitions referred to in paragraph 2
tl_reason: Complaint to authority or dispute settlement body. Test: yes.

right: Right to a written, substantiated decision when data sharing is withheld or refused on trade-secret grounds
description: Receive in writing and without undue delay a duly substantiated decision where the data holder withholds, suspends (Art. 4(7)) or refuses (Art. 4(8)) access on trade-secret grounds.
quote: The decision of the data holder shall be duly substantiated and provided in writing to the user without undue delay.
tl_reason: Written substantiated decision from the data holder; plain document. Test: yes.

right: Right to challenge a refusal, withholding or suspension of data sharing (user)
addressee: competent authority / certified dispute settlement body
description: Challenge a trade-secret based refusal, withholding or suspension by complaint to the competent authority, which decides whether and under which conditions sharing starts or resumes, or via dispute settlement.
exercise: Complaint under Art. 37(5)(b) or dispute settlement under Art. 10(1); court redress available at any stage.
quote: a user wishing to challenge a data holder’s decision to refuse or to withhold or suspend data sharing pursuant to paragraphs 7 and 8 may
tl_reason: Complaint to authority or dispute settlement body. Test: yes.

right: Right to control the data holder's use of non-personal product data
description: The data holder may use readily available non-personal data only on the basis of a contract with the user, may not use it to undermine the user's commercial position, and may not pass it to third parties beyond fulfilling the contract (Art. 4(14)).
quote: A data holder shall only use any readily available data that is non-personal data on the basis of a contract with the user.
tl_reason: Data holder's use of non-personal data requires a contract with the user; control is contractual, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right of the user to share data with third parties
rightholder: user, or a party acting on behalf of a user
description: Require the data holder to make readily available data and metadata available to a third party of the user's choice without undue delay, free of charge to the user, in machine-readable format and, where feasible, in real time.
exercise: Request by the user or a party acting on its behalf; data made available under Arts 8-9; gatekeepers are not eligible third parties (Art. 5(3)).
quote: Upon request by a user, or by a party acting on behalf of a user, the data holder shall make available readily available data
notes: Micro/small enterprises exempt (Art. 7(1)).
tl_reason: Data holder must make data available to a third party in machine-readable format; user directs data across services. Test: no.

right: Right of third parties to give and withdraw permission for data holder's use of insights
rightholder: third party receiving data at the user's request
description: The data holder may not use readily available data to derive insights undermining the third party's commercial position unless the third party has given permission, which it can easily withdraw at any time.
quote: unless the third party has given permission to such use and has the technical possibility to easily withdraw that permission at any time
tl_reason: Law requires a technical possibility to easily withdraw permission; exercised through it. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right of third parties to a written, substantiated decision when data sharing is withheld or refused
description: Receive in writing and without undue delay a substantiated decision where the data holder withholds, suspends (Art. 5(10)) or refuses (Art. 5(11)) sharing on trade-secret grounds.
quote: The decision of the data holder shall be duly substantiated and provided in writing to the third party without undue delay.
tl_reason: Written substantiated decision to a third party; plain business correspondence. Test: yes.

right: Right of third parties to challenge a refusal, withholding or suspension of data sharing
addressee: competent authority / certified dispute settlement body
description: Challenge the data holder's trade-secret based decision by complaint to the competent authority (which decides whether sharing starts or resumes) or via dispute settlement.
exercise: Complaint under Art. 37(5)(b) or dispute settlement under Art. 10(1); court redress available at any stage.
quote: a third party wishing to challenge a data holder’s decision to refuse or to withhold or suspend data sharing pursuant to paragraphs 10 and 11 may
tl_reason: Complaint to authority or dispute settlement body. Test: yes.

right: Right of the user to determine purposes and obtain erasure of data received by a third party
addressee: third party receiving data under Art. 5
description: The third party may process the data only for purposes and conditions agreed with the user and must erase it when no longer necessary; it may not hinder the user's choices, profile unless necessary for the requested service, pass data on without a contract with the user, or prevent a consumer from sharing the data with others (Art. 6(2)).
quote: A third party shall process the data made available to it pursuant to Article 5 only for the purposes and under the conditions agreed with the user
tl_reason: Purposes and erasure set by agreement with the user; contractual control, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Contractual terms derogating from user rights are not binding
description: Any contractual term that excludes, derogates from or varies the user's Chapter II rights to the user's detriment does not bind the user (see also Art. 8(2)).
exercise: Invoke non-binding nature against the other contracting party.
quote: Any contractual term which, to the detriment of the user, excludes the application of, derogates from or varies the effect of the user’s rights under this Chapter shall not be binding on the user.
tl_reason: Non-binding derogating contract terms; contract law. Test: yes.

right: Right of data recipients to fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms
addressee: data holder obliged to make data available
description: Where a data holder must make data available (under Art. 5 or other Union law), obtain the data under FRAND terms, transparently and without discrimination against comparable recipients (Art. 8(3)); terms derogating from Chapter III are not binding (Art. 12(2)).
quote: shall do so under fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms and conditions and in a transparent manner
notes: Chapter III applies to data-sharing obligations entering into force after 12 September 2025 (Art. 50).
tl_reason: FRAND terms for data recipients; contract right. Test: yes.

right: Right of data recipients to information showing no discrimination
description: If it considers the conditions discriminatory, obtain from the data holder, on reasoned request, information showing there has been no discrimination.
exercise: Reasoned request; answer without undue delay.
quote: the data holder shall without undue delay provide the data recipient, upon its reasoned request, with information showing that there has been no discrimination
tl_reason: Information showing no discrimination, on reasoned request; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to reasonable compensation, capped at cost for SMEs and non-profit research organisations
rightholder: data recipient (cost cap: SMEs and not-for-profit research organisations)
description: Compensation for making data available must be non-discriminatory and reasonable (Art. 9(1)); for SMEs and not-for-profit research organisations it may not exceed the costs of making the data available.
quote: any compensation agreed shall not exceed the costs referred to in paragraph 2, point (a)
tl_reason: Compensation cap for SMEs and research bodies; pricing rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to information on the basis for calculating compensation
description: Receive information on how compensation was calculated in enough detail to assess whether it complies with Art. 9(1)-(4).
quote: The data holder shall provide the data recipient with information setting out the basis for the calculation of the compensation in sufficient detail
tl_reason: Information on compensation calculation; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of access to a certified dispute settlement body (data sharing)
rightholder: users, data holders and data recipients
description: Refer disputes on access refusals and on FRAND terms for making data available to a certified dispute settlement body.
exercise: Fees disclosed in advance (Art. 10(2)); right to be heard and see the other party's submissions (Art. 10(8)); reasoned decision within 90 days (Art. 10(9)); binding only if parties agreed beforehand (Art. 10(12)); court action unaffected (Art. 10(13)).
quote: Users, data holders and data recipients shall have access to a dispute settlement body, certified in accordance with paragraph 5 of this Article
tl_reason: Access to a certified dispute settlement body. Test: yes.

right: Right to reimbursement of dispute settlement fees and expenses when successful
description: If the dispute settlement body rules for the user or data recipient (Art. 4(3), 4(9), 5(12) disputes), the data holder bears all fees and reimburses other reasonable expenses; a losing user/recipient does not reimburse the data holder unless in manifest bad faith.
quote: the data holder shall bear all the fees charged by the dispute settlement body and shall reimburse that user or that data recipient for any other reasonable expenses
tl_reason: Reimbursement of dispute settlement fees. Test: yes.

right: Right of cloud customers to access a certified dispute settlement body
description: Refer disputes on breaches of switching rights (Arts 23-31) to a certified dispute settlement body.
exercise: Same procedural guarantees as Art. 10(8)-(9).
quote: Customers and providers of data processing services shall have access to a dispute settlement body, certified in accordance with paragraph 5 of this Article
tl_reason: Dispute settlement for cloud customers. Test: yes.

right: Right of dispute settlement bodies to be certified
rightholder: dispute settlement body meeting the conditions
description: A body that demonstrates impartiality, expertise, accessibility and efficiency can request certification as a Data Act dispute settlement body.
exercise: Request to the Member State where the body is established.
quote: The Member State where the dispute settlement body is established shall, at the request of that body, certify that body where it has demonstrated that it meets all of the following conditions
tl_reason: Certification of dispute settlement bodies. Test: yes.

right: Right to require erasure, cessation and compensation after unauthorised use or disclosure of data
rightholder: data holder, trade secret holder or user
description: Where a third party or recipient obtained or used data unlawfully (Art. 11(3)), require it to erase the data, stop producing or marketing derived goods or services, inform the user, and compensate the party harmed.
exercise: Request to the infringing party; to be complied with without undue delay.
quote: the third party or data recipient shall comply, without undue delay, with the requests of the data holder and, where applicable and where they are not the same person, the trade secret holder
tl_reason: Remedy package (erasure, cessation, compensation) by request; erasure is incidental to a liability remedy. Test: yes.

right: Right of the user to be informed of unauthorised use or disclosure of data
description: Be informed of the unauthorised use or disclosure of the data and of the measures taken to stop it.
quote: to inform the user of the unauthorised use or disclosure of the data and of the measures taken to put an end to the unauthorised use or disclosure of the data
tl_reason: Information from the data recipient about unauthorised use; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Users' remedies against data recipients that manipulate choices or profile
description: Where a data recipient makes the user's choices unduly difficult or uses data for profiling (Art. 6(2)(a)-(b)), users have the same rights as data holders under Art. 11(2) (erasure, cessation, information, compensation).
quote: Where the data recipient infringes Article 6(2), point (a) or (b), users shall have the same rights as data holders under paragraph 2 of this Article.
tl_reason: Same remedy package for users; requests and compensation are non-technical. Test: yes.

right: Unfair contractual terms on data unilaterally imposed are not binding
rightholder: enterprise on which the term was unilaterally imposed
description: Unfair, unilaterally imposed terms on data access and use, liability or remedies (blacklist Art. 13(4), grey list Art. 13(5)) do not bind the enterprise; the rest of the contract remains binding if severable.
exercise: Supplier of the term bears burden of proving it was not unilaterally imposed (Art. 13(6)).
quote: which has been unilaterally imposed by an enterprise on another enterprise, shall not be binding on the latter enterprise if it is unfair
notes: Chapter IV applies to contracts concluded after 12 September 2025, and from 12 September 2027 to certain older contracts (Art. 50).
tl_reason: Unfair unilaterally imposed contract terms; contract law. Test: yes.

right: Right of data holders to be notified of onward transmission of data obtained by public bodies
addressee: public sector body, Commission, ECB or Union body
description: Be notified without undue delay when data provided on the basis of exceptional need is passed on to other public bodies or to a third party.
quote: it shall notify the data holder from whom the data was received without undue delay
tl_reason: Notification of onward transmission by public bodies; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of data holders to complain about transmission of data obtained by public bodies
description: Complain to the competent authority if the transmission or making available of its data infringes its rights under Chapter V.
quote: Where the data holder considers that its rights under this Chapter have been infringed by the transmission or making available of data, it may lodge a complaint with the competent authority
tl_reason: Complaint to competent authority. Test: yes.

right: Right of data holders to decline or seek modification of an exceptional-need data request
addressee: requesting public sector body, Commission, ECB or Union body
description: Decline or seek modification of a public-sector request if it lacks control over the data, a similar request was already made, or the request does not meet Art. 17 conditions.
exercise: Within 5 working days (public emergency) or 30 working days (other exceptional need).
quote: a data holder may decline or seek the modification of a request to make data available under this Chapter without undue delay
tl_reason: Declining or modifying a public-sector data request; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right of data holders to have a disputed request referred to the competent authority
description: Where the data holder wishes to challenge a request that cannot be resolved by modification, the matter is referred to the competent authority.
quote: where the data holder wishes to challenge the request and the matter cannot be resolved by an appropriate modification of the request, the matter shall be referred to the competent authority
tl_reason: Referral of disputed request to authority; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right of data holders to be informed of erasure of data obtained by public bodies
rightholder: data holder; individuals or organisations that received the data
addressee: public sector body, Commission, ECB or Union body
description: Be informed without undue delay once the data obtained under Chapter V have been erased.
quote: inform the data holder and individuals or organisations that received the data pursuant to Article 21(1) without undue delay that the data have been erased
tl_reason: Information that data obtained by public bodies were erased; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of data holders to public acknowledgement on request
addressee: public sector body, Commission, ECB or Union body
description: When providing data free of charge for a public emergency, obtain public acknowledgement on request.
exercise: On request of the data holder.
quote: shall provide public acknowledgement to the data holder if requested by the data holder
tl_reason: Public acknowledgement on request. Test: yes.

right: Right to fair compensation for providing data on exceptional need
addressee: public sector body, Commission, ECB or Union body
description: Receive fair compensation covering technical and organisational costs plus a reasonable margin when providing data for non-emergency exceptional needs; micro and small enterprises may claim compensation also for emergencies (Art. 20(3)).
exercise: Not for official statistics where purchase of data is not allowed by national law (Art. 20(4)); public body may complain about the level (Art. 20(5)).
quote: The data holder shall be entitled to fair compensation for making data available in compliance with a request made pursuant to Article 15(1), point (b).
tl_reason: Fair compensation for providing data; remuneration. Test: yes.

right: Right of data holders to be notified of sharing with researchers or statistical bodies
addressee: public sector body, Commission, ECB or Union body
description: Be notified of the identity of the recipient, purpose, duration and protective measures before data are shared for research or official statistics.
quote: it shall notify without undue delay the data holder from whom the data was received, stating the identity and contact details of the organisation or the individual receiving the data
tl_reason: Notification of sharing with researchers; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of data holders to complain about sharing with researchers or statistical bodies
description: Lodge a complaint with the competent authority if it disagrees with the onward sharing of its data.
quote: Where the data holder disagrees with the transmission or making available of data, it may lodge a complaint with the competent authority
tl_reason: Complaint to competent authority. Test: yes.

right: Protection against obstacles to switching cloud/data processing services
description: Providers may not impose and must remove commercial, technical, contractual and organisational obstacles to terminating contracts, concluding new ones, porting exportable data and digital assets, achieving functional equivalence and unbundling.
quote: providers of data processing services shall not impose and shall remove pre-commercial, commercial, technical, contractual and organisational obstacles, which inhibit customers from
tl_reason: Providers must remove technical obstacles to switching and porting data and assets; exercised by moving data across services. Test: no.

right: Right to a written contract setting out switching rights before signature
description: Receive a written contract clearly setting out switching rights, available before signing in a storable and reproducible form.
quote: The provider of data processing services shall make that contract available to the customer prior to signing the contract in a way that allows the customer to store and reproduce the contract.
tl_reason: Written contract in storable form before signing; plain document, technology incidental. Test: yes.

right: Right to switch data processing provider or port data to on-premises infrastructure
addressee: provider of data processing services (source provider)
description: On request, switch to another provider or port all exportable data and digital assets on-premises within a transitional period of max. 30 days, with reasonable assistance, service continuity, risk information and security, and support for the exit strategy (Art. 25(2)(b)).
exercise: Notice period max. 2 months (Art. 25(2)(d)); customer notifies choice to switch, move on-premises or erase (Art. 25(3)); contract ends on completion and customer is notified (Art. 25(2)(c)); up to 7 months if technically unfeasible (Art. 25(4)).
quote: clauses allowing the customer, upon request, to switch to a data processing service offered by a different provider of data processing services or to port all exportable data and digital assets
tl_reason: Switching provider or porting all exportable data and digital assets on-premises; only possible technically. Test: no.

right: Right to a data retrieval period of at least 30 days
description: Retrieve data for at least 30 calendar days after the end of the transitional period.
quote: a minimum period for data retrieval of at least 30 calendar days, starting after the termination of the transitional period
tl_reason: Data retrieval period; retrieving and taking data elsewhere requires technical means. Test: no.

right: Right to full erasure of exportable data and digital assets after switching
description: Obtain full erasure of all exportable data and digital assets generated by or relating directly to the customer after the retrieval period; the customer may also choose erasure instead of switching (Art. 25(3)(c)).
quote: a clause guaranteeing full erasure of all exportable data and digital assets generated directly by the customer, or relating to the customer directly
tl_reason: Object is exportable data and digital assets, but erasure can be chosen by plain notice and nothing technical is returned. Digital object conflicts with test.

right: Right to be notified and given reasons if the 30-day switching period is technically unfeasible
description: Be notified within 14 working days of the switching request, with justification, if the 30-day transitional period is unfeasible, and be offered an alternative period of max. 7 months with service continuity.
quote: the provider of data processing services shall notify the customer within 14 working days of the making of the switching request, and shall duly justify the technical unfeasibility
tl_reason: Notification and justification of technical unfeasibility; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to extend the switching transitional period once
description: Extend the transitional period once, for a period the customer considers more appropriate.
quote: clauses providing the customer with the right to extend the transitional period once for a period that the customer considers more appropriate for its own purposes
tl_reason: Extension of the transitional period by plain request. Test: yes.

right: Right to information on switching and porting procedures and data formats
description: Receive information on switching and porting procedures, methods, formats and known limitations, and a reference to an up-to-date register of data structures, formats and standards.
quote: information on available procedures for switching and porting to the data processing service, including information on available switching and porting methods and formats
tl_reason: Information on switching methods, formats and data-structure registers; deliverable as text but usable only with technical understanding. Result criterion conflicts.

right: Right to switch without switching charges
description: From 12 January 2027 no switching charges (including data egress charges) may be imposed; until then only reduced charges not exceeding directly linked costs (Art. 29(2)-(3)).
quote: From 12 January 2027, providers of data processing services shall not impose any switching charges on the customer for the switching process.
notes: Reduced, cost-based switching charges permitted from 11 January 2024 to 12 January 2027.
tl_reason: Prohibition of switching charges; pricing rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to pre-contractual information on fees, termination penalties and switching charges
rightholder: prospective customer of data processing services
description: Before contracting, receive clear information on standard service fees, early termination penalties and reduced switching charges, and on services involving highly complex or costly switching (Art. 29(5)).
quote: providers of data processing services shall provide the prospective customer with clear information on the standard service fees and early termination penalties that might be imposed
tl_reason: Pre-contractual information on fees and penalties; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to technical support for switching (functional equivalence, open interfaces)
addressee: source provider of data processing services
description: IaaS providers must take all reasonable measures so the customer achieves functional equivalence, providing capabilities, information, documentation, support and tools; other providers must offer open interfaces free of charge (Art. 30(2)).
quote: The source provider of data processing services shall facilitate the switching process by providing capabilities, adequate information, documentation, technical support
tl_reason: Provider must supply capabilities, tools and open interfaces for functional equivalence; holder operates interfaces across services. Test: no.

right: Right to export all exportable data in a machine-readable format
description: Where no interoperability standards or common specifications are published, obtain on request an export of all exportable data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format.
exercise: On request of the customer.
quote: the provider of data processing services shall, at the request of the customer, export all exportable data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format
tl_reason: Export of all exportable data in machine-readable format; result must be taken to a new environment. Test: no.

right: Right to be informed of switching obligations that do not apply to custom-built or trial services
rightholder: prospective customer of data processing services
description: Before contracting for custom-built or testing services, be told which Chapter VI obligations do not apply.
quote: the provider of data processing services shall inform the prospective customer of the obligations of this Chapter that do not apply
tl_reason: Pre-contractual information on non-applicable obligations; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of providers to seek a national opinion on, and reject, third-country access orders
rightholder: provider of data processing services addressed by a third-country decision
addressee: relevant national body or authority for international legal cooperation
description: Ask the competent national body whether the conditions for complying with a third-country order are met, and reject the request if no reply within one month or the conditions are not met.
quote: The addressee of the decision or judgment may ask the opinion of the relevant national body or authority competent for international cooperation in legal matters
tl_reason: Seeking a national opinion on third-country orders; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right of cloud customers to be informed of third-country authority access requests
description: Be informed of a third-country authority's request to access the customer's data before the provider complies.
exercise: Except for law-enforcement requests, for as long as necessary.
quote: The provider of data processing services shall inform the customer about the existence of a request of a third-country authority to access its data before complying with that request
tl_reason: Notification by the provider of a third-country access request; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to interoperability for in-parallel (multi-cloud) use with cost-capped egress charges
description: When using several providers in parallel, benefit from the switching interoperability obligations (Art. 34(1)); data egress charges may only pass on costs incurred (Art. 34(2)).
quote: the providers of data processing services may impose data egress charges, but only for the purpose of passing on egress costs incurred, without exceeding such costs
tl_reason: Interoperability for multi-cloud use is technical, but the specific entitlement is a cost cap on egress charges. Mechanism and pricing elements conflict.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with a competent authority
addressee: competent authority (Member State of habitual residence, place of work or establishment)
description: Complain if they consider their rights under the Data Act have been infringed.
exercise: Individually or collectively; data coordinator provides information on lodging complaints on request; complainant informed of progress and decision (Art. 38(2)).
quote: natural and legal persons shall have the right to lodge a complaint, individually or, where relevant, collectively, with the relevant competent authority
tl_reason: Complaint to competent authority by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right to an effective judicial remedy against binding decisions of competent authorities
rightholder: any affected natural and legal person
addressee: courts of the Member State of the competent authority
description: Challenge legally binding decisions of Data Act competent authorities in court.
exercise: Before the courts of the authority's Member State, individually or collectively through representatives (Art. 39(3)).
quote: any affected natural and legal person shall have the right to an effective judicial remedy with regard to legally binding decisions taken by competent authorities
tl_reason: Judicial remedy against authority decisions. Test: yes.

right: Right to a remedy where a competent authority fails to act on a complaint
rightholder: any affected natural and legal person
addressee: Member State (courts or impartial review body)
description: Obtain a judicial remedy or impartial review if the competent authority fails to act on a complaint.
exercise: In accordance with national law.
quote: Where a competent authority fails to act on a complaint, any affected natural and legal person shall, in accordance with national law, either have the right to an effective judicial remedy
tl_reason: Remedy for authority inaction. Test: yes.

right: Representative actions for Data Act infringements (Representative Actions Directive)
addressee: traders infringing the Data Act / national courts
description: The Data Act is added to Annex I of Directive (EU) 2020/1828, so qualified entities can bring representative actions (injunctions and redress) for consumers harmed by Data Act infringements.
exercise: Via qualified entities under national law transposing Directive (EU) 2020/1828.
quote: In Annex I to Directive (EU) 2020/1828 the following point is added:
notes: Amendment of another act (adds point 68 to Annex I of Directive (EU) 2020/1828).
tl_reason: Representative actions through qualified entities; judicial redress. Test: yes.

right: Right to access one's personal electronic health data
addressee: Member State / healthcare providers (via electronic health data access services)
description: Access, immediately after registration, free of charge and in a readable consolidated format, at least the priority categories of one's electronic health data.
exercise: Through national electronic health data access services, free of charge (Art. 4(1)); no fees may be charged (Art. 18). MS may delay access for patient-safety reasons (Art. 3(3)).
quote: Natural persons shall have the right to access at least personal electronic health data relating to them that belong to the priority categories referred to in Article 14
notes: Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Access through electronic health data access services in a consolidated format; result is health data to interpret. Test: no.

right: Right to download an electronic copy of one's health data
addressee: Member State / healthcare providers (via electronic health data access services)
description: Download free of charge an electronic copy of at least the priority categories of one's health data in the European EHR exchange format.
exercise: Through electronic health data access services.
quote: Natural persons, or their representatives referred to in Article 4(2), shall have the right to download free of charge an electronic copy
notes: Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Download of an electronic copy in the European EHR exchange format; result is a data file. Test: no.

right: Right to authorise proxies to access one's health data
description: Authorise other natural persons of one's choice to access all or part of one's health data on one's behalf, for a limited or unlimited period or specific purpose, and manage those authorisations; legal representatives may access data of persons whose affairs they administer.
exercise: Via proxy services, free of charge, electronically or on paper; persons must be informed of authorisation rights (Art. 4(3)).
quote: natural persons to authorise other natural persons of their choice to access their personal electronic health data, or part thereof, on their behalf
notes: Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Delegates access to electronic health data via proxy services, but authorisation may be given on paper. Exercise criterion conflicts with digital object.

right: Right to an easy complaint mechanism of proxy services
description: Use an easy complaint mechanism provided by the proxy services.
quote: The proxy services shall provide an easy complaint mechanism for natural persons.
notes: Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Complaint mechanism of proxy services; plain complaint. Test: yes.

right: Right to insert information in one's own EHR
addressee: Member State (electronic health data access services)
description: Add information to one's EHR, clearly marked as self-inserted; data inserted by health professionals cannot be altered directly.
exercise: Through electronic health data access services or linked applications.
quote: Natural persons, or their representatives referred to in Article 4(2), shall have the right to insert information in the EHR of those natural persons
notes: Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Inserting information into one's EHR is only possible through access services or linked applications. Test: no.

right: Right to request rectification online
addressee: controller (healthcare provider) via electronic health data access services
description: Easily request online the rectification of one's electronic health data under GDPR Art. 16; the controller may verify accuracy with a health professional.
exercise: Online via electronic health data access services; MS may enable other GDPR rights online.
quote: Electronic health data access services referred to in Article 4 shall enable natural persons to easily request online the rectification of their personal electronic health data
notes: Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Law requires an online request channel, but the rectification request and its result are non-technical; GDPR route remains. Electronic-channel criterion conflicts.

right: Right to data portability to another healthcare provider
description: Give access to, or request transmission of, all or part of one's health data to another healthcare provider of one's choice immediately, free of charge and without hindrance.
quote: Natural persons shall have the right to give access to, or to request a healthcare provider to transmit, all or part of their personal electronic health data to another healthcare provider
notes: Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Giving access to or transmitting EHR data to another provider; only possible technically. Test: no.

right: Right to cross-border transmission of health data in the European exchange format
addressee: healthcare providers in different Member States
description: Request transmission of one's health data to a provider in another Member State in the European EHR exchange format via MyHealth@EU; the receiving provider must accept and read them.
quote: Natural persons shall have the right, where the healthcare providers are located in different Member States, to request the transmission of their personal electronic health data
notes: Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Cross-border transmission in the European exchange format via MyHealth@EU. Test: no.

right: Right to transmit health data to social security or reimbursement services
description: Request one-way transmission of part of one's health data to an identified recipient in the social security or reimbursement sector, immediately and free of charge.
quote: to transmit a part of their personal electronic health data to a clearly identified recipient in the social security or reimbursement services sector
notes: Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Transmission of EHR data to a social security recipient; technical data flow. Test: no.

right: Right to transmit a downloaded copy to healthcare providers of one's choice
description: Transmit a downloaded copy of one's priority-category data to any healthcare provider, which must accept and be able to read it.
quote: they shall be able to transmit those data to healthcare providers of their choice in the European electronic health record exchange format referred to in Article 15
notes: Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Holder takes a downloaded exchange-format copy to providers of choice. Test: no.

right: Right to restrict access of health professionals to one's health data
description: Restrict health professionals' and providers' access to all or part of one's health data; the restriction is not visible to providers, and emergency overrides are logged and accessible to the person (Art. 11(5)).
exercise: Persons are told restriction may affect care; MS set rules and safeguards.
quote: Natural persons shall have the right to restrict the access of health professionals and healthcare providers to all or parts of their personal electronic health data as referred to in Article 3.
notes: Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Restriction is an access-control setting exercised through electronic health data access services (Art. 4(1)). Test: no.

right: Right to information on who accessed one's health data
addressee: Member State (electronic health data access services)
description: Obtain information, including automatic notifications, on any access to one's health data by health professionals: who, when and which data.
exercise: Free of charge, without delay, kept at least three years; MS may restrict in exceptional circumstances (Art. 9(3)).
quote: Natural persons shall have the right to obtain information, including through automatic notifications, on any access to their personal electronic health data
notes: Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Access logs and automatic notifications delivered through electronic access services; result is a log to interpret. Test: no.

right: Right to opt out of access to one's EHR in primary use (Member-State option)
description: Where national law provides for it, opt out (reversibly) of access to one's EHR data through the access services; vital-interest overrides may apply.
exercise: Per national opt-out mechanism.
quote: Member States’ laws may provide that natural persons have the right to opt out from the access to their personal electronic health data registered in an EHR system
notes: Member-State option. Applies from 26 March 2029 for patient summaries, e-prescriptions and e-dispensations; from 26 March 2031 for imaging, test results and discharge reports (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Opt-out from EHR access exercised through electronic access services; changes system access behaviour. Test: no.

right: Right to identify oneself with any recognised eID when using health data access services
addressee: Member State (electronic health data access services)
description: Use any electronic identification means recognised under eIDAS to access electronic health data access services.
quote: those natural persons shall have the right to identify themselves electronically using any electronic identification means which are recognised pursuant to Article 6 of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014
tl_reason: Identification with eIDAS electronic identification means; inherently technical. Test: no.

right: Right not to be charged for accessing or sharing one's health data
description: Healthcare providers and third parties may not charge data subjects any fee, cost or compensation for sharing or accessing their data.
quote: A healthcare provider or a third party shall not directly or indirectly charge data subjects a fee or costs, or require compensation, for sharing or accessing data.
tl_reason: No fees for accessing or sharing data; pricing rule. Test: yes.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with a digital health authority
rightholder: natural and legal persons whose rights or interests are negatively affected
description: Complain about matters under Chapter II (primary use) to the competent digital health authority.
exercise: Individually or collectively; complaints on Arts 3, 5-10 are transmitted to the GDPR supervisory authority (Art. 21(2)); complainant informed of progress, decision and any referral (Art. 21(3)); easy submission tools (Art. 21(5)); representation possible (Art. 101).
quote: natural and legal persons shall have the right to lodge a complaint in relation to the provisions laid down in this Chapter, individually or, where relevant, collectively
tl_reason: Complaint to digital health authority. Test: yes.

right: Right to have electronic prescriptions dispensed in other Member States
description: Have an electronic prescription issued in another Member State dispensed by pharmacies, including online pharmacies, which must access and accept it via MyHealth@EU.
exercise: Under the conditions of Art. 11 Directive 2011/24/EU.
quote: Member States shall ensure that pharmacies operating on their territories, including online pharmacies, are able to dispense electronic prescriptions issued in other Member States
notes: Art. 23(2)-(6) follow the staged dates of Art. 105.
tl_reason: Dispensing depends on pharmacies reading e-prescriptions via MyHealth@EU, but the patient needs no technical ability. Ability criterion conflicts.

right: Right of EHR system users to be informed of non-conformity, corrective action or recall
addressee: manufacturer of EHR systems (and importers, Art. 32(5))
description: Be informed of non-conformity of an EHR system and of any corrective action, recall or withdrawal, and of mandatory preventive maintenance (Art. 30(1)(k)).
quote: inform the distributors of their EHR systems and, where applicable, the authorised representative, importers and users of the non-conformity and of any corrective action
notes: Chapter III rules for EHR systems take effect in stages (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Notification of non-conformity or recall by EHR manufacturer; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right of EHR system users to submit complaints through manufacturer/importer channels
addressee: importers and manufacturers of EHR systems
description: Submit complaints through accessible reporting channels (manufacturer channels under Art. 30(1)(n), or importer channels) and receive communications on risks and serious incidents; importers must investigate complaints (Art. 32(9)).
quote: Importers shall establish reporting channels and ensure that they are accessible to allow users to submit complaints
notes: Chapter III rules for EHR systems take effect in stages (Art. 105).
tl_reason: Complaints through manufacturer or importer reporting channels; plain complaint. Test: yes.

right: Right of persons harmed by an EHR system to information and documentation
rightholder: affected natural person or user harmed by an EHR system
description: Where an authority finds that an EHR system caused harm to health or safety, receive information and documentation from the manufacturer.
quote: the manufacturer shall immediately provide information and documentation, as applicable, to the affected natural person or user
tl_reason: Information and documentation about an EHR system that caused harm; object is software, but documents are deliverable and usable plainly. Result criterion conflicts.

right: Right to choose which wellness-app data are shared with one's EHR
addressee: manufacturer of wellness applications claiming interoperability
description: Wellness-app data are never shared automatically with the EHR; sharing requires consent and the person chooses which categories are inserted and when; users must be informed of interoperability (Art. 48(1)).
quote: shall ensure that the natural person concerned is able to choose which categories of health data from the wellness application are to be inserted in the EHR system
notes: Art. 48 follows the staged dates of Art. 105.
tl_reason: Wellness-app manufacturer must let the person choose data categories inserted in the EHR; choice in the app interface. Test: no.

right: Right of health data holders and applicants to complain about IP/trade-secret decisions
rightholder: health data holders and health data applicants
description: Where access is refused because of a serious risk to IP, trade secrets or regulatory data protection, the applicant receives a justification; holders and applicants may lodge a complaint under Art. 81.
quote: Health data holders and health data applicants shall have the right to lodge a complaint in accordance with Article 81 of this Regulation.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Complaint to health data access body. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of significant health findings from secondary use
addressee: health data holder (via the health data access body)
description: Be informed (or have one's treating professional informed) of a significant finding about one's health discovered by a health data user.
exercise: Under conditions laid down by national law.
quote: The health data holder shall, under the conditions laid down by national law, inform the natural person or health professional treating the natural person concerned.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Being informed of significant findings under national law; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right not to be informed of significant health findings
addressee: health data holder / health data access body
description: Request not to be informed of significant health findings arising from secondary use.
quote: Natural persons shall have the right to request not to be informed of such findings.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Plain request not to be informed. Test: yes.

right: Right of health data holders to receive the share of fees covering their costs
description: Receive the part of the data permit fees that compensates their costs of compiling and preparing data for secondary use.
exercise: Holder provides a cost estimate to the health data access body.
quote: The part of the fees linked to the health data holder’s costs shall be paid to the health data holder.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Share of fees covering costs; remuneration. Test: yes.

right: Right to dispute settlement on secondary-use fees
rightholder: health data holders and health data users
addressee: certified dispute settlement body (Art. 10 Data Act)
description: If they disagree with the fee set by the health data access body, refer the matter to a Data Act dispute settlement body.
quote: Where health data holders or health data users disagree with the fee set by the health data access body, they shall have access to dispute settlement bodies
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Dispute settlement on fees. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of estimated fees and to withdraw an application
description: Be informed of estimated fees before a permit or response is issued and withdraw the application or request, paying only costs already incurred.
quote: The health data applicant shall be informed about the option to withdraw the health data access application or health data request.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Fee information and withdrawal of application; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to be heard before enforcement measures by health data access bodies
rightholder: health data users and health data holders
description: Be notified of findings of non-compliance and state views before measures such as permit revocation, exclusion or periodic penalties; receive the measures and reasons (Art. 63(5)).
exercise: Within a reasonable period not exceeding four weeks.
quote: The health data access body concerned shall give the health data user or health data holder concerned the opportunity to state their views within a reasonable period that shall not exceed four weeks.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Right to be heard before enforcement; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to procedural safeguards and judicial remedies against fines by health data access bodies
rightholder: health data holders and health data users
addressee: Member State (courts) / health data access body
description: Administrative fines imposed by health data access bodies are subject to due process and effective judicial remedies.
quote: shall be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with Union and national law, including effective judicial remedies and due process
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Procedural safeguards and judicial remedies against fines. Test: yes.

right: Right to apply for access to electronic health data for secondary use
description: Submit a health data access application for permitted purposes (Art. 53(1)), e.g. research, innovation, education or improving care.
exercise: Single application for multi-country access (Art. 67(3)); purposes (a)-(c) reserved to public bodies (Art. 53(2)).
quote: A natural or legal person may submit a health data access application for the purposes referred to in Article 53(1) to a health data access body.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Application to a health data access body; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right to a decision on a health data access application within three months
description: Obtain a decision issuing or refusing a data permit within three months of a complete application, be notified of incompleteness and allowed to complete it, and be told reasons for any extension.
exercise: Extension by up to three months with notice and reasons.
quote: the health data access body shall issue or refuse a data permit within three months of receiving a complete health data access application
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Decision deadline on applications; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to a justification for refusal of a data permit
description: Receive a justification when a data permit is refused.
quote: Where the health data access body refuses to issue a data permit, it shall provide a justification for that refusal to the health data applicant.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Justification of refusal; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right of health data users to access and process data under a data permit
description: Access and process the permitted electronic health data in a secure processing environment in accordance with the data permit.
exercise: Data made available within two months of receipt from holders (Art. 68(7)).
quote: Health data users shall have the right to access and process the electronic health data in a secure processing environment in accordance with the data permit issued to them
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Access and processing only inside a secure processing environment; requires own analysis software. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to request extension or amendment of a data permit
description: Request a one-time extension of the data permit (max. further 10 years) and, where needed, an amendment (Art. 68(13)); request storage of the dataset formula.
exercise: Justified request at least one month before expiry; possible higher fees.
quote: That duration may be extended once, for a period which does not exceed 10 years, at the request of the health data user
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Extension or amendment of a permit by request; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to submit a health data request for anonymised statistical results
description: Request a response in anonymised statistical format only (no access to underlying data).
exercise: Assessment within 3 months and response within a further 3 months where possible (Art. 69(4)).
quote: The health data applicant may submit a health data request for the purposes referred to in Article 53 with the aim of obtaining a response only in an anonymised statistical format.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Plain request answered only with anonymised statistics; result may be a data file or a plain table. Result criterion conflicts.

right: Right to opt out of secondary use of one's electronic health data
addressee: Member State / health data access bodies / health data holders
description: Opt out at any time, without reasons and reversibly, from processing of one's personal electronic health data for secondary use.
exercise: Accessible opt-out mechanism (Art. 71(2)); effective for permits approved after opt-out (Art. 71(3)); MS may provide public-interest exceptions (Art. 71(4)); complaints go to GDPR supervisory authority (Arts 65, 81(4)).
quote: Natural persons shall have the right to opt out at any time, and without providing any reason, from the processing of personal electronic health data relating to them for secondary use
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Object is processing of electronic health data, but the national opt-out mechanism may be non-electronic and a plain statement suffices. Mechanism criterion conflicts.

right: Right of health data holders to apply for trusted health data holder status (Member-State option)
addressee: Member State / health data access body
description: Where a Member State establishes the procedure, apply to be designated a trusted health data holder handling applications under a simplified procedure.
exercise: Must provide a compliant secure processing environment, expertise and guarantees.
quote: Member States may establish a procedure whereby health data holders can apply to be designated as trusted health data holders
notes: Member-State option. Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Application for trusted data holder status; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with a health data access body
rightholder: natural and legal persons whose rights or interests are negatively affected
description: Complain about matters under Chapter IV (secondary use) to a health data access body.
exercise: Individually or collectively; informed of progress and decision (Art. 81(2)); accessible tools (Art. 81(3)); opt-out complaints transmitted to GDPR supervisory authority (Art. 81(4)); representation possible (Art. 101).
quote: collectively, with a health data access body, provided that their rights or interests are negatively affected
notes: Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
tl_reason: Complaint to health data access body. Test: yes.

right: Right of health data holders to be informed of third-country access requests
addressee: digital health authorities, health data access bodies, health data users
description: Be informed of a third-country administrative authority's request to access their non-personal health data before it is complied with.
exercise: Except for law-enforcement requests, for as long as necessary.
quote: shall inform the health data holder about the existence of a request of a third-country administrative authority to access its data before complying with that request
tl_reason: Notification of a third-country access request; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to compensation for damage caused by infringements of the EHDS Regulation
rightholder: any natural or legal person that suffered material or non-material damage
description: Claim compensation for material or non-material damage resulting from an infringement of the Regulation.
exercise: In accordance with Union and national law.
quote: Any natural or legal person that has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of an infringement of this Regulation shall have the right to receive compensation
tl_reason: Compensation for damage. Test: yes.

right: Right to be represented by a not-for-profit body
addressee: Member State (digital health authorities, health data access bodies)
description: Mandate a not-for-profit data-protection organisation to lodge a complaint or exercise complaint rights under Arts 21 and 81 on one's behalf.
quote: he or she shall have the right to mandate a not-for-profit body, organisation or association, constituted in accordance with national law, having statutory public interest objectives
tl_reason: Mandating a not-for-profit body to complain; delegation without technical mechanism. Test: yes.

right: Automatic security updates with opt-out and option to postpone
addressee: manufacturer of the product with digital elements
description: Where applicable, products must install security updates automatically by default, but users get a clear, easy opt-out, notification of available updates and the option to postpone them temporarily.
exercise: Through the product's settings.
quote: with a clear and easy-to-use opt-out mechanism, through the notification of available updates to users, and the option to temporarily postpone them
notes: Essential requirement in Annex I (Art. 13(1)); main obligations apply from 11 Dec 2027 (Art. 71).
tl_reason: Opt-out and postponement of automatic updates through product settings; the right is a setting in the software. Test: no.

right: Opt-out from security logging of internal activity
addressee: manufacturer of the product with digital elements
description: Security-related recording and monitoring of internal activity (access to or modification of data, services or functions) must come with an opt-out for the user.
exercise: Through the product's settings.
quote: including the access to or modification of data, services or functions, with an opt-out mechanism for the user
notes: Essential requirement in Annex I; applies from 11 Dec 2027.
tl_reason: Opt-out from security logging via product settings; the right exists only as a software option. Test: no.

right: Secure, permanent deletion of all data and settings
addressee: manufacturer of the product with digital elements
description: Users must be able to securely and easily remove all data and settings permanently, and transfer data securely where it can be moved to other products.
exercise: Through the product's functions.
quote: provide the possibility for users to securely and easily remove on a permanent basis all data and settings
notes: Essential requirement in Annex I; applies from 11 Dec 2027.
tl_reason: Product must offer a function to remove all data and settings permanently; exercised only through it. Test: no.

right: Free security updates without delay
addressee: manufacturer of the product with digital elements
description: Available security updates must be disseminated without delay and free of charge, with advisory messages on what users should do (business users of tailor-made products may agree otherwise).
quote: they are disseminated without delay and, unless otherwise agreed between a manufacturer and a business user in relation to a tailor-made product with digital elements, free of charge
notes: Vulnerability-handling requirement in Annex I; applies from 11 Dec 2027.
tl_reason: Free security updates are software delivered to and installed on the device; cannot be fulfilled or used without technical means. Test: no.

right: Right of component maintainers to be informed of vulnerabilities and receive fixes
rightholder: person or entity manufacturing or maintaining an integrated component (incl. open-source maintainers)
description: When a manufacturer finds a vulnerability in an integrated component, including an open-source one, it must report it to whoever makes or maintains that component. It must also share any code or documentation it developed to fix it.
exercise: Report and, where available, code shared by the manufacturer, in machine-readable format where appropriate.
quote: report the vulnerability to the person or entity manufacturing or maintaining the component, and address and remediate the vulnerability
tl_reason: Vulnerability reports and fix code, possibly machine-readable, for component maintainers; using them means integrating code. Specialist holder. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right to vulnerability handling and security updates during the support period
description: Throughout the support period, the manufacturer must handle the product's vulnerabilities effectively, including by providing security updates. The support period must match the expected use time and be at least five years, unless the product is expected to be used for less.
exercise: Security updates issued by the manufacturer during the support period.
quote: Without prejudice to the second subparagraph, the support period shall be at least five years.
notes: Several details are in Annex I, which is not in the enacting-terms extract: Part II(8) says security updates are free of charge (unless otherwise agreed for tailor-made B2B products); Part I(2)(c) says automatic security updates are on by default with an opt-out; Part I(2)(m) gives secure removal of data and settings.
tl_reason: Vulnerability handling through security updates during the support period; fulfilled only as software installed on the product. Test: no.

right: Right to continued availability of issued security updates
description: Each security update released during the support period must stay available for at least 10 years after issue, or for the rest of the support period if that is longer.
exercise: Download from the manufacturer.
quote: which has been made available to users during the support period, remains available after it has been issued for a minimum of 10 years or for the remainder of the support period
tl_reason: Issued updates must stay downloadable for 10 years; holder must find, download and install them. Test: no.

right: Right to free access to the latest version of a software product
description: If a manufacturer gives security support only for the latest substantially modified version, users of earlier versions must get that version free of charge and without extra costs to adapt their hardware or software environment.
exercise: Access provided by the manufacturer.
quote: provided that the users of the versions that were previously placed on the market have access to the version last placed on the market free of charge
notes: Condition on the manufacturer's choice to support only the latest version
tl_reason: Free access to the latest software version; holder must obtain and install it. Test: no.

right: Right to a single point of contact for communicating with the manufacturer and reporting vulnerabilities
description: Users can contact the manufacturer directly and quickly through a single point of contact, for example to report vulnerabilities, using their preferred means of communication, not only automated tools.
exercise: Via the single point of contact listed in the user information (Annex II).
quote: The single point of contact shall allow users to choose their preferred means of communication and shall not limit such means to automated tools.
tl_reason: Single point of contact using the user's preferred means, not only automated tools; plain communication. Test: yes.

right: Right to user information and instructions
description: Products must come with clear information and instructions for secure installation, operation and use (Annex II), in a language users understand. These must stay available, and accessible online if published there, for at least 10 years or for the support period if longer.
exercise: On paper or electronically, with the product.
quote: Manufacturers shall keep the information and instructions to the user set out in Annex II at the disposal of users and market surveillance authorities for at least 10 years
tl_reason: Instructions on paper or electronically; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to know the end date of the support period at purchase
description: At the time of purchase, the end date of the support period (at least month and year) must be clear and easy to find, and where applicable shown on the product, its packaging or by digital means.
exercise: Shown at the time of purchase.
quote: the end date of the support period referred to in paragraph 8, including at least the month and the year, is clearly and understandably specified at the time of purchase
tl_reason: Support end date shown at purchase on product, packaging or digitally; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to be notified when the product reaches end of support
description: Where technically feasible, users must receive a notification that their product has reached the end of its support period.
exercise: Notification shown to the user.
quote: manufacturers shall display a notification to users informing them that their product with digital elements has reached the end of its support period
notes: Only where technically feasible
tl_reason: Notification must be displayed by the product software; content plain. Conflict: electronic channel required, non-technical result.

right: Right to be informed of the manufacturer's cessation of operations
addressee: manufacturer; importer (Art 19(8)) and distributor (Art 20(6)) where they become aware of it
description: Before a manufacturer stops operating and can no longer comply, it must tell users of its products by any means available and as far as possible. Importers and distributors must do the same if they learn of the cessation.
exercise: Notice by any means available, as far as possible.
quote: the users of the relevant products with digital elements placed on the market, of the impending cessation of operations
tl_reason: Notice of cessation by any available means; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed of actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents
description: Once aware of an actively exploited vulnerability or severe incident, the manufacturer must inform affected users, and where needed tell them what mitigation and corrective measures they can take. If the manufacturer does not do so in time, the CSIRT may inform users.
exercise: Information from the manufacturer, where appropriate in a structured, machine-readable format.
quote: the manufacturer shall inform the impacted users of the product with digital elements, and where appropriate all users, of that vulnerability or incident
notes: Under Art 69(3), also covers products placed on the market before 11 Dec 2027. Art 24(3) extends it to open-source software stewards.
tl_reason: Plain notice possible, but mitigation measures require technical action and information may be machine-readable. Conflict: result only sometimes technical.

right: Right to voluntarily report vulnerabilities, cyber threats, incidents and near misses
addressee: CSIRT designated as coordinator or ENISA
description: Anyone can voluntarily report vulnerabilities and cyber threats in products with digital elements (Art 15(1)), and incidents or near misses (Art 15(2)), to a CSIRT or ENISA. The CSIRT then informs the manufacturer.
exercise: Via the single reporting platform (Art 16) to a CSIRT designated as coordinator or ENISA.
quote: Manufacturers as well as other natural or legal persons may notify any vulnerability contained in a product with digital elements as well as cyber threats
notes: Art 15(2) covers incidents and near misses in the same way.
tl_reason: Report via the platform or otherwise; channel incidental, but identifying vulnerabilities presupposes technical skill. Conflict: ability technical, mechanism incidental.

right: Right of reporters to confidentiality and protection from added obligations or liability
addressee: CSIRTs designated as coordinators and ENISA
description: Information from a person who reports is kept confidential. A voluntary report creates no new obligations for the reporter, and the mere act of reporting brings no increased liability (Art 17(4)).
exercise: Applies automatically to anyone who notifies under Art 14 or 15.
quote: voluntary reporting shall not result in the imposition of any additional obligations upon a notifying natural or legal person
notes: Without prejudice to criminal investigations. See also Art 17(4).
tl_reason: Confidentiality and no added liability for reporters; legal protection. Test: yes.

right: Right of manufacturers to request delayed dissemination of a sensitive notification
description: Given how sensitive the notified information is, a manufacturer can ask the CSIRT to delay passing its notification on to other CSIRTs, on justified cybersecurity grounds and only for as long as strictly necessary.
exercise: Request made with the notification; the CSIRT decides and must justify any withholding to ENISA.
quote: upon request by the manufacturer and in light of the level of sensitivity of the notified information as indicated by the manufacturer under Article 14(2), point (a)
notes: Linked to the Art 14 notifications, which apply from 11 Sep 2026. Related: CSIRT must consult the manufacturer before informing the public (Art 17(2)); ENISA adds vulnerabilities to the EU database in agreement with the manufacturer (Art 17(5)).
tl_reason: Manufacturer requests delayed dissemination; administrative procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right of the manufacturer to consent to subcontracting by a notified body
description: A notified body may subcontract conformity-assessment activities or use a subsidiary only if the manufacturer agrees.
exercise: Manufacturer gives or withholds agreement.
quote: Activities may be subcontracted or carried out by a subsidiary only with the agreement of the manufacturer.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 11 Jun 2026 (Art 71(2))
tl_reason: Manufacturer consent to subcontracting by a notified body; contractual. Test: yes.

right: Right to appeal decisions of notified bodies
description: Manufacturers can appeal notified-body decisions, such as refusing, restricting or withdrawing a certificate, through an appeal procedure that Member States must provide.
exercise: Appeal procedure under national law.
