quote: Member States shall ensure that an appeal procedure against decisions of the notified bodies is available.
notes: Chapter IV applies from 11 Jun 2026 (Art 71(2))
tl_reason: Appeal against notified-body decisions; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right to complain to market surveillance authorities
description: Consumers can submit complaints about possible non-compliance. Authorities must tell them where to complain (Art 11 Reg (EU) 2019/1020) and how to reach mechanisms for reporting vulnerabilities, incidents and cyber threats.
exercise: Complaint to the national market surveillance authority.
quote: Market surveillance authorities shall inform consumers of where to submit complaints that could indicate non-compliance with this Regulation
tl_reason: Complaint to the market surveillance authority; ordinary complaint. Test: yes.

right: Procedural rights of economic operators in corrective measures
description: When authorities require corrective action, Art 18 of Reg (EU) 2019/1020 applies. Measures must state reasons, the operator must be told about available remedies, and the operator has the right to be heard.
exercise: Under Art 18 Reg (EU) 2019/1020 and national procedural law.
quote: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply to the corrective actions.
notes: Art 54(8) also preserves these procedural rights
tl_reason: Procedural rights in corrective measures; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right of economic operators to be consulted in the Union safeguard procedure
description: When a national measure is contested, the Commission must consult the economic operators concerned before deciding whether it is justified.
exercise: Consultation by the Commission.
quote: the Commission shall without delay enter into consultation with the relevant Member State and the economic operator or operators and shall evaluate the national measure
notes: The Commission must also consult economic operators before Union-level measures (Arts 56(4), 57(4), 57(8)), and implementing acts are communicated to them (Arts 56(6), 57(10)).
tl_reason: Consultation in the Union safeguard procedure; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to representative actions under the Representative Actions Directive
addressee: courts / administrative authorities of Member States
description: Qualified entities can bring representative actions under Directive (EU) 2020/1828 against infringements by economic operators that harm, or may harm, consumers' collective interests.
exercise: Representative action brought by a qualified entity.
quote: Directive (EU) 2020/1828 shall apply to the representative actions brought against infringements by economic operators of provisions of this Regulation
notes: Art 67 adds the CRA to Annex I of Directive (EU) 2020/1828
tl_reason: Representative action by qualified entities; judicial remedy. Test: yes.

right: Protection against AI-generated intimate or sexual imagery made without explicit consent
addressee: providers and deployers of AI systems
description: AI systems that generate or manipulate realistic intimate or sexually explicit images, video or audio of an identifiable person are prohibited unless that person has given explicit, informed consent.
exercise: Prohibition applies to placing on the market/use where such generation is the intended purpose or reasonably foreseeable without safeguards (Art. 5(1a)); breaches can be reported via Art. 85 complaint.
quote: without that person’s freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent for that generation or manipulation
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1); framed as a prohibition, the depicted person's consent is the only lawful basis.
tl_reason: Object is AI-generated imagery, but holder is not a user and acts only through plain consent or complaint. Object vs holder/ability conflict.

right: Right not to be subject to an adverse decision based solely on real-time remote biometric identification output
rightholder: person identified by real-time remote biometric identification
description: No decision producing an adverse legal effect on a person may be taken based solely on the output of a real-time remote biometric identification system used for law enforcement.
exercise: Safeguard within the authorisation regime for law-enforcement use; enforceable through national remedies.
quote: No decision that produces an adverse legal effect on a person may be taken based solely on the output of the ‘real-time’ remote biometric identification system.
tl_reason: Concerns decisions based on biometric-ID output, but safeguard is procedural; holder operates nothing. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right of deployers to receive instructions for use of high-risk AI systems
description: Deployers must receive concise, complete, correct and clear instructions for use (provider identity, characteristics, limitations, human oversight, logs) enabling them to interpret outputs and use the system appropriately.
exercise: Instructions accompany the system in digital or other format; minimum content in Art. 13(3).
quote: High-risk AI systems shall be accompanied by instructions for use in an appropriate digital format or otherwise that include concise, complete, correct and clear information
notes: Annex III high-risk systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product) high-risk systems from 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 113(c), as amended).
tl_reason: Instructions explain an AI system and its logs, but may be any format and readable without technical means. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right of deployers and distributors to be informed of non-conformity and corrective actions
description: Where a high-risk AI system is not in conformity, the provider must take corrective action (fix, withdraw, disable, recall) and inform distributors and, where applicable, deployers, authorised representatives and importers.
exercise: Immediate information by the provider once it considers the system non-conforming.
quote: They shall inform the distributors of the high-risk AI system concerned and, where applicable, the deployers, the authorised representative and importers accordingly.
notes: Annex III high-risk systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product) high-risk systems from 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 113(c), as amended).
tl_reason: Notice of non-conformity and corrective action; plain information. Test: yes.

right: Right of a new provider to information, technical access and assistance from the initial provider
rightholder: new provider (distributor, importer, deployer or third party that becomes provider)
addressee: initial provider of the AI system
description: A person who becomes provider of a high-risk AI system (e.g. by rebranding, substantial modification or change of purpose) can obtain from the initial provider technical documentation, information on known limitations and failure modes, and targeted technical access for testing.
exercise: Does not apply where the initial provider clearly specified that its system is not to be changed into a high-risk AI system; IP and trade secrets protected (Art. 25(5)).
quote: That initial provider shall closely cooperate with new providers and shall make available the necessary information and provide the reasonably expected technical access and other assistance
notes: Paragraph as amended (M1). Annex III high-risk systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product) high-risk systems from 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 113(c), as amended).
tl_reason: Initial provider must give technical documentation and targeted technical access for testing; usable only technically. Test: no. Consistency pass: holder is not the governed party.

right: Right of high-risk AI providers to contractually specified information and assistance from component suppliers
rightholder: provider of a high-risk AI system
addressee: third party supplying AI systems, models, tools, services or components
description: Providers of high-risk AI systems and their suppliers must agree in writing on the information, capabilities, technical access and assistance needed for the provider to comply with the Regulation.
exercise: Written agreement; does not apply to free and open-source components other than GPAI models; AI Office may recommend voluntary model terms.
quote: shall, by written agreement, specify the necessary information, capabilities, technical access and other assistance based on the generally acknowledged state of the art
notes: B2B right. Annex III high-risk systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product) high-risk systems from 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 113(c), as amended).
tl_reason: Contractual right to agreed information and technical access; exercised by negotiation, result partly technical. Mechanism vs exercise conflict.

right: Right of workers and their representatives to be informed before high-risk AI is used at the workplace
description: Before putting into service or using a high-risk AI system at the workplace, employers must inform workers' representatives and affected workers that they will be subject to it.
exercise: Prior information, in line with Union and national rules and practice on information of workers.
quote: deployers who are employers shall inform workers’ representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to the use of the high-risk AI system
notes: Annex III high-risk systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product) high-risk systems from 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 113(c), as amended).
tl_reason: Information concerns workplace AI system, but delivered through ordinary worker information. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right not to be subject to an adverse decision based solely on post-remote biometric identification output
rightholder: person subject to post-remote biometric identification
description: Law enforcement authorities may not take a decision producing adverse legal effects on a person based solely on the output of a post-remote biometric identification system; each use requires judicial or administrative authorisation.
exercise: Authorisation ex ante or within 48 hours; data deleted if authorisation refused.
quote: no decision that produces an adverse legal effect on a person may be taken by the law enforcement authorities based solely on the output of such post-remote biometric identification systems
notes: Annex III high-risk systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (product) high-risk systems from 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 113(c), as amended).
tl_reason: Concerns decisions based on biometric-ID output, but safeguard is procedural; holder operates nothing. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to be informed of being subject to a high-risk AI system in decision-making
addressee: deployer of Annex III high-risk AI system
description: Natural persons must be told when a deployer uses an Annex III high-risk AI system to make, or assist in making, decisions about them.
exercise: For law-enforcement use, Art. 13 of Directive (EU) 2016/680 applies instead.
quote: that make decisions or assist in making decisions related to natural persons shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system
notes: Annex III systems only; applies from 2 Dec 2027 (Art. 113(c)(i), as amended).
tl_reason: Notice that high-risk AI is used; object digital but notice is plain. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to request extension of a notified body certificate
description: Providers may ask the notified body to extend the validity of a conformity certificate for further periods based on a re-assessment.
exercise: Request to the notified body; extension up to 5 years (Annex I) or 4 years (Annex III) per period.
quote: At the request of the provider, the validity of a certificate may be extended for further periods
tl_reason: Certificate extension request to notified body. Test: yes.

right: Right to appeal decisions of notified bodies
description: Providers can appeal notified-body decisions, including on certificates issued, suspended, withdrawn or restricted; the notified body must give reasons for such decisions.
exercise: Appeal procedure to be made available against notified body decisions.
quote: An appeal procedure against decisions of the notified bodies, including on conformity certificates issued, shall be available.
tl_reason: Appeal against notified body decision. Test: yes.

right: Right to be informed when interacting with an AI system
rightholder: natural persons interacting with an AI system
description: People must be informed that they are interacting with an AI system (e.g. a chatbot) unless this is obvious from the context.
exercise: Clear and distinguishable information at the latest at first interaction, meeting accessibility requirements (Art. 50(5)); law-enforcement exception.
quote: the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system
tl_reason: Disclosure that one interacts with AI; object is software but notice is plain. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to be informed of exposure to emotion recognition or biometric categorisation
rightholder: natural persons exposed to the system
addressee: deployer of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation system
description: Persons exposed to an emotion recognition or biometric categorisation system must be informed of its operation.
exercise: Information at the latest at first exposure (Art. 50(5)); exception for systems permitted by law for criminal investigations.
quote: Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system
tl_reason: Notice of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation; object digital, notice plain. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to be informed that content is a deep fake or AI-generated public-interest text
rightholder: natural persons exposed to the content
description: Deployers must disclose that image, audio or video deep fakes, and AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest, have been artificially generated or manipulated.
exercise: Disclosure at first exposure (Art. 50(5)); lighter disclosure for evidently artistic/satirical works; text exception where human editorial control applies.
quote: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake, shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated.
tl_reason: Deep-fake disclosure on digital content; label is plain but holder must interpret content. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to contest classification as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk
description: A GPAI provider meeting the systemic-risk compute threshold may submit substantiated arguments that its model nonetheless does not present systemic risks.
exercise: Arguments submitted with the notification (within two weeks of meeting the threshold); Commission decides (Art. 52(3)).
quote: may present, with its notification, sufficiently substantiated arguments to demonstrate that, exceptionally, although it meets that requirement, the general-purpose AI model does not present
tl_reason: Provider's submission against designation; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to request reassessment of a systemic-risk designation
rightholder: provider of general-purpose AI model designated with systemic risk
description: A provider whose model was designated as having systemic risk can request the Commission to reassess the designation on the basis of new reasons.
exercise: Reasoned request with objective, detailed and new reasons; at the earliest six months after the designation or a decision maintaining it.
quote: Upon a reasoned request of a provider whose model has been designated as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk pursuant to paragraph 4, the Commission shall take the request into account
tl_reason: Reassessment request; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right of downstream providers to information and documentation on general-purpose AI models
rightholder: providers of AI systems integrating a general-purpose AI model (downstream providers)
description: Downstream providers can obtain up-to-date information and documentation (at least Annex XII elements) to understand the model's capabilities and limitations and comply with their own obligations.
exercise: Subject to protection of IP and trade secrets; not applicable to free and open-source models without systemic risk (Art. 53(2)).
quote: draw up, keep up-to-date and make available information and documentation to providers of AI systems who intend to integrate the general-purpose AI model into their AI systems
tl_reason: Model documentation explains a digital system, but is a document usable without technical means. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to written proof of sandbox activities and an exit report
rightholder: provider or prospective provider participating in an AI regulatory sandbox
description: Sandbox participants can request written proof of activities successfully carried out in the sandbox and receive an exit report, usable to demonstrate compliance in conformity assessment.
exercise: Upon request to the competent authority; exit report published only with agreement of provider and authority (Art. 57(8)).
quote: Upon request of the provider or prospective provider of the AI system, the competent authority shall provide a written proof of the activities successfully carried out in the sandbox.
tl_reason: Written proof of sandbox activities. Test: yes.

right: Right to apply for an AI regulatory sandbox and receive a decision within three months
rightholder: provider or prospective provider of an AI system
description: Sandboxes must be open to any applying provider meeting transparent and fair eligibility and selection criteria, with a decision within three months; access is free of charge for SMEs and start-ups (Art. 58(2)(d)).
exercise: Application to the national competent authority; may apply in partnership with deployers (Art. 58(2)(b)).
quote: that AI regulatory sandboxes are open to any applying provider or prospective provider of an AI system who fulfils eligibility and selection criteria, which shall be transparent and fair
notes: Principles to be implemented via Commission implementing acts.
tl_reason: Sandbox application; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Tacit approval of a real-world testing plan after 30 days
rightholder: provider or prospective provider of high-risk AI system
description: If the market surveillance authority does not answer within 30 days, the real-world testing and testing plan are deemed approved (unless national law excludes tacit approval).
exercise: Submit real-world testing plan to the MSA of the Member State where testing takes place.
quote: where the market surveillance authority has not provided an answer within 30 days, the testing in real world conditions and the real-world testing plan shall be understood to have been approved
tl_reason: Tacit approval of testing plan; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right to have AI predictions, recommendations or decisions reversed or disregarded during real-world testing
rightholder: subject of testing in real world conditions
addressee: provider / prospective provider and deployer conducting the test
description: Outputs of a high-risk AI system tested in real-world conditions must be capable of being effectively reversed and disregarded; subjects must be told how to request this (Art. 61(1)(d)).
exercise: Request according to the arrangements communicated before consent (Art. 61(1)(d)).
quote: the predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system can be effectively reversed and disregarded.
tl_reason: AI outputs must be technically reversible, but holder requests by plain means. Mechanism vs ability conflict.

right: Right to withdraw from real-world testing at any time
rightholder: subject of testing in real world conditions or legally designated representative
description: Test subjects may withdraw at any time by revoking consent, without detriment and without giving reasons.
exercise: Revocation of informed consent; does not affect activities already carried out.
quote: may, without any resulting detriment and without having to provide any justification, withdraw from the testing at any time by revoking their informed consent
tl_reason: Revoking informed consent to testing; plain statement. Test: yes.

right: Right to request deletion of personal data after withdrawing from real-world testing
rightholder: subject of testing in real world conditions or legally designated representative
description: On withdrawal, test subjects may request the immediate and permanent deletion of their personal data.
exercise: Request to the provider or prospective provider.
quote: may request the immediate and permanent deletion of their personal data
tl_reason: Object is personal dataset, but deletion is requested plainly and needs no technical use. Object vs test conflict.

right: Right to prior information and to refuse informed consent to real-world testing
rightholder: subject of testing in real world conditions
description: Participation in real-world testing requires freely given informed consent after clear information on the nature, conditions, duration, rights (including refusal and withdrawal), reversal arrangements and contact details.
exercise: Consent obtained before participation; law-enforcement exception in Art. 60(4)(i).
quote: freely-given informed consent shall be obtained from the subjects of testing prior to their participation in such testing and after their having been duly informed
notes: Art. 61(1)(c) expressly refers to 'their right to refuse to participate in, and the right to withdraw from' testing.
tl_reason: Prior information and refusal of consent; plain. Test: yes.

right: Right to a copy of the documented informed consent
rightholder: subject of testing or legal representative
description: Test subjects receive a dated and documented copy of their informed consent.
quote: The informed consent shall be dated and documented and a copy shall be given to the subjects of testing or their legal representative.
tl_reason: Copy of documented consent; plain document. Test: yes.

right: Priority access of SMEs and start-ups to AI regulatory sandboxes
rightholder: SMEs, including start-ups, with registered office or branch in the Union
description: SMEs and start-ups meeting the eligibility and selection criteria get priority access to AI regulatory sandboxes.
exercise: Application to national sandbox; eligibility and selection criteria apply.
quote: provide SMEs, including start-ups, having a registered office or a branch in the Union, with priority access to the AI regulatory sandboxes
tl_reason: Priority sandbox access; administrative. Test: yes.

right: Right of SMEs and deployers to advice and answers to queries on the AI Act
description: Member States must use or establish dedicated channels to advise SMEs, deployers and innovators and respond to their queries on implementing the Regulation, including sandbox participation.
exercise: Via national dedicated communication channels.
quote: to provide advice and respond to queries about the implementation of this Regulation, including as regards participation in AI regulatory sandboxes
tl_reason: Advice from national channels. Test: yes.

right: Right to be notified of the opening of an AI Office investigation
rightholder: operator (provider or deployer) of AI system under AI Office competence
description: When the AI Office opens an investigation into suspected non-compliance, it must notify the operator concerned.
quote: Upon starting such an investigation, the AI Office shall notify the operator of the AI system concerned.
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1); covers AI systems within Art. 75(1).
tl_reason: Notification of investigation. Test: yes.

right: Right to offer binding commitments to the AI Office
description: An operator under investigation can offer commitments to ensure compliance, which the AI Office may make binding and close the case; rejection requires a reasoned decision.
exercise: Offered during proceedings under Art. 75a(2) or in the structured dialogue (Art. 75c(3)).
quote: the operator concerned offers commitments to ensure compliance with the relevant provisions of this Regulation, the AI Office may, by decision, make those commitments binding on the operator concerned
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1).
tl_reason: Offering commitments in proceedings. Test: yes.

right: Right to receive preliminary findings before an AI Office non-compliance decision
description: Before a non-compliance decision, the AI Office must communicate its preliminary findings and the measures it is considering, allowing the operator to respond.
quote: Before adopting a decision pursuant to paragraph 1, the AI Office shall communicate its preliminary findings to the operator concerned.
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1).
tl_reason: Preliminary findings before decision. Test: yes.

right: Right to judicial review by the CJEU of AI Office decisions and fines
rightholder: operator subject to AI Office decision
addressee: Court of Justice of the European Union
description: Operators can challenge AI Office decisions before the CJEU, which has unlimited jurisdiction over fines and periodic penalty payments and may cancel, reduce or increase them.
exercise: Action before the CJEU; AI Office must indicate this right in decisions requesting information or ordering inspections (Art. 75a(3)-(4)).
quote: The Court of Justice of the European Union shall have unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions of the AI Office fixing a fine or periodic penalty payment pursuant to this Article.
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1).
tl_reason: Judicial review before CJEU. Test: yes.

right: Procedural rights under Art. 18 of the Market Surveillance Regulation in AI Office proceedings
description: Operators supervised by the AI Office enjoy the market-surveillance procedural rights: reasoned decisions, notification with information on remedies, and a right to be heard.
exercise: See Art. 18 Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
quote: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply mutatis mutandis to operators subject to the AI Office’s competence pursuant to Article 75(1) of this Regulation
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1).
tl_reason: Administrative procedural rights. Test: yes.

right: Rights of defence and access to the AI Office file
description: Operators' rights of defence must be respected and they are entitled to access the AI Office file under negotiated disclosure, excluding confidential information and internal documents.
exercise: Access in view of a possible Art. 75c(1) decision; AI Office decides disclosure terms if parties disagree.
quote: those operators shall be entitled to have access to the AI Office file under the terms of a negotiated disclosure
notes: Inserted by amending act (M1).
tl_reason: Rights of defence and file access. Test: yes.

right: Right to reasons and information on how to challenge a decision suspending or modifying real-world testing
description: Decisions suspending, terminating or requiring modification of real-world testing, and objections to a testing plan, must state reasons and explain how the provider can challenge them.
quote: the decision or the objection shall indicate the grounds therefor and how the provider or prospective provider can challenge the decision or objection.
tl_reason: Reasons and challenge information. Test: yes.

right: Protection of confidential information, trade secrets and source code disclosed to authorities
rightholder: natural or legal person whose information is obtained
addressee: Commission, market surveillance authorities, notified bodies and others applying the Regulation
description: Persons whose information is obtained in applying the Regulation can rely on its confidentiality, in particular protection of IP rights, confidential business information, trade secrets and source code.
quote: the intellectual property rights and confidential business information or trade secrets of a natural or legal person, including source code
tl_reason: Confidentiality of information held by authorities. Test: yes.

right: Procedural rights of operators in national procedures on AI systems presenting a risk
description: Where an authority requires corrective action, withdrawal or recall of a risky AI system, the operator benefits from the procedural rights of Art. 18 Market Surveillance Regulation (reasons, remedies information, right to be heard).
exercise: Also preserved in the Union safeguard phase (Art. 79(8)).
quote: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply to the measures referred to in the second subparagraph of this paragraph.
tl_reason: Administrative procedural rights. Test: yes.

right: Right of operators to be consulted in the Union safeguard procedure
description: When a national measure against an AI system is contested, the Commission must consult the operator(s) before deciding whether the measure is justified.
exercise: Commission decision within six months (60 days for Art. 5 cases).
quote: the Commission shall without undue delay enter into consultation with the market surveillance authority of the relevant Member State and the operator or operators
tl_reason: Consultation in safeguard procedure. Test: yes.

right: Right of operators to be consulted and informed on measures against compliant but risky AI systems
description: Where a compliant high-risk AI system is found to present a risk, the Commission consults the operators on the national measures and communicates its decision to them (Art. 82(5)).
quote: The Commission shall without undue delay enter into consultation with the Member States concerned and the relevant operators, and shall evaluate the national measures taken.
tl_reason: Consultation on national measures. Test: yes.

right: Right to lodge a complaint with a market surveillance authority
description: Anyone with grounds to consider that the AI Act has been infringed can complain to the relevant market surveillance authority.
exercise: Handled under the MSA's dedicated procedures in line with Regulation (EU) 2019/1020; without prejudice to other remedies.
quote: any natural or legal person having grounds to consider that there has been an infringement of the provisions of this Regulation may submit complaints to the relevant market surveillance authority
tl_reason: Complaint to market surveillance authority by ordinary means. Test: yes.

right: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
addressee: deployer of Annex III high-risk AI system (except point 2)
description: A person subject to a decision based on the output of an Annex III high-risk AI system that has legal or similarly significant adverse effects on their health, safety or fundamental rights can obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the AI system's role and the main elements of the decision.
exercise: Request to the deployer; applies only where not otherwise provided under Union law (Art. 86(3)) and subject to Union/national exceptions (Art. 86(2)).
quote: shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken
notes: Text says 'any affected person'; in practice depends on Annex III high-risk classification applying from 2 Dec 2027 (Art. 113(c)(i)).
tl_reason: Object is AI-assisted decision, but explanation is requested plainly and delivered in clear language. Object vs test conflict.

right: Protection of persons reporting infringements of the AI Act (whistleblowers)
description: Persons reporting breaches of the AI Act benefit from the Whistleblower Directive: reporting channels and protection against retaliation.
exercise: Via internal/external reporting channels under Directive (EU) 2019/1937.
quote: Directive (EU) 2019/1937 shall apply to the reporting of infringements of this Regulation and the protection of persons reporting such infringements.
notes: Cross-reference to Directive (EU) 2019/1937.
tl_reason: Whistleblower protection; ordinary reporting channels. Test: yes.

right: Right of downstream providers to lodge a complaint about general-purpose AI model providers
description: Downstream providers can complain to the AI Office alleging that a GPAI model provider infringed the Regulation.
exercise: Duly reasoned complaint indicating the provider's contact point, facts, provisions concerned and reasons.
quote: Downstream providers shall have the right to lodge a complaint alleging an infringement of this Regulation.
tl_reason: Complaint to AI Office. Test: yes.

right: Right of GPAI providers with systemic risk to offer binding commitments
rightholder: provider of general-purpose AI model with systemic risk
description: During a structured dialogue, the provider may offer commitments to implement mitigation measures, which the Commission may make binding instead of imposing measures.
quote: the provider of the general-purpose AI model with systemic risk offers commitments to implement mitigation measures to address a systemic risk at Union level
tl_reason: Offering commitments. Test: yes.

right: Procedural rights of general-purpose AI model providers
description: GPAI providers enjoy the procedural rights of Art. 18 Market Surveillance Regulation (reasoned decisions, information on remedies, right to be heard) in Commission enforcement.
exercise: See Art. 18 Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
quote: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the providers of the general-purpose AI model
notes: Article titled 'Procedural rights of economic operators of the general-purpose AI model'.
tl_reason: Administrative procedural rights. Test: yes.

right: Right to procedural safeguards and effective judicial remedies against fines
rightholder: operator subject to national administrative fines
addressee: Member State / market surveillance authority / courts
description: The imposition of penalties and fines under the AI Act is subject to due process and effective judicial remedies.
exercise: Under national law.
quote: The exercise of powers under this Article shall be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with Union and national law, including effective judicial remedies and due process.
tl_reason: Judicial remedies against fines. Test: yes.

right: Right of complainants to be associated with EDPS fining proceedings
description: Where the EDPS conducts proceedings against an EU institution under the AI Act, any complainants are closely associated with the proceedings.
quote: Complainants, if any, shall be associated closely with the proceedings.
notes: Proceedings concern Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
tl_reason: Association with EDPS proceedings; procedural. Test: yes.

right: Right of GPAI providers to be heard before a fine
description: Before fining a GPAI provider, the Commission must communicate its preliminary findings and give the provider an opportunity to be heard.
quote: the Commission shall communicate its preliminary findings to the provider of the general-purpose AI model and give it an opportunity to be heard
notes: Art. 101 applies from 2 Aug 2026 (Art. 113(b)).
tl_reason: Right to be heard before fine. Test: yes.

right: Right to CJEU review of Commission fines on GPAI providers
addressee: Court of Justice of the European Union
description: GPAI providers can challenge Commission fining decisions before the CJEU, which may cancel, reduce or increase the fine.
exercise: Action before the CJEU.
quote: The Court of Justice of the European Union shall have unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions of the Commission fixing a fine under this Article.
tl_reason: Judicial review before CJEU. Test: yes.
